News.title: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says
News.content:
Earlier this month, the BBC was given rare access inside a Jewish school in Hertfordshire, where pupils and staff operate under tight security, amid heightened concerns about antisemitism.

Spencer Lewis, the executive headteacher of Yavneh College, said that security was an "innate part" of his role.

"When you come in in the morning, there are high gates, high fences, lots of security cameras. We have four full-time security staff. And it sort of just becomes part of what you do," he said. "We think about it a lot."

Staff and pupils told the BBC they have become so used to these measures that they barely notice them anymore.

Lock-in - or "in-vacuation" - drills for dealing with intruders have become second nature, even to the youngest pupils.

"It's a bit scary sometimes, but you know you're safe," said Livi, a Year 6 pupil.

"It's sad that we can't be equal to everyone else, but people don't like us just because of the way we are," added her classmate, Sadie.

A group of a dozen older pupils who spoke to the BBC said that while they feel safe inside school, hearing about antisemitic attacks in the UK, including reports of pupils at other Jewish schools being harassed on their commute and at sports fixtures, has left them feeling targeted.

Some said that they were reluctant to wear skullcaps or necklaces featuring the Star of David â a Jewish symbol â outside school.

"Other religions get to be out and wear their necklaces and be proud - I don't get why Jewish people can't do it as much," said Year 9 pupil Ilan.

In response to the recommendations, the government is also expected to encourage schools to adopt the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA)'s working definition of antisemitism, although it cannot make it compulsory.

The definition is supported by mainstream Jewish organisations and has been adopted by 47 countries, including the UK, as well as most British universities.

However, some of the IHRA definition's examples of antisemitic behaviour have proven controversial.

The Board of Deputies of British Jews said that adopting the IHRA definition would provide schools with a tool "to deepen understanding of contemporary antisemitism".

In a statement, a spokesperson told the BBC: "Treating antisemitism in schools as a safeguarding issue will have the benefit of creating an explicit duty on all schools to address this as they would any other threat to children's safety, and will strengthen accountability."

He added: "We have advocated these measures be accompanied by other steps including improving education about Jewish life and ensuring schools maintain their duties in relation to political impartiality."

Bell, who is now vice-chancellor of the University of Sunderland, heard evidence from pupils, teachers, governors and parents across state and independent schools, as well as from community organisations.

The Department for Education has declined to comment before the review is published.

News.title: Woman says she 'couldn't speak or breathe' during alleged rape by Russell Brand
News.content:
Warning - this report contains graphic content

A woman who says Russell Brand raped her at his home in London told police she "couldn't speak or breathe" during the alleged attack, a jury has heard.

The 51-year-old entertainer is accused of raping the woman in 2009 after meeting her at London's Hammersmith Apollo, where he had been performing as a stand-up comedian.

Brand faces seven charges in the trial in total - three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.

The allegations, made by six female complainants, span a 10-year period between 1999 and 2009. He denies all the charges.

In video evidence of her speaking to a police officer, the woman said she performed a sex act on Brand at the London theatre after being invited for drinks following the show.

She said she gave him her phone number, explaining she was "a massive Russell Brand fan" and a "massive comedy fan" at the time.

After that night, she said Brand messaged her and she went to his house in Hampstead knowing they would have sex.

But she said a consensual encounter became rape when Brand started having anal sex with her and ignored her pleas for him to stop.

She said when she arrived at his home, Brand told her she needed to have a shower "because my hair smelled funny". He then asked her to brush her teeth.

"I was trying to make a joke of what he was making me do", she said. "All of those things made me feel, 'I don't like this'."

The woman said a short while after getting on his bed, she was turned over. It was then she said she was allegedly raped.

She told police: "From the very moment it happened, I felt I had willingly gone there and from what his reputation was, what did I expect?"

She said Brand "hurt me and harmed me, and when I asked him to stop, he didn't". She added: "The horror in anyone that I told was not enough to make me believe I didn't deserve it."

The woman said she told friends and family afterwards, and went through sexual health tests - believing that she had contracted a disease from Brand.

Earlier on Tuesday, another woman who claims Brand sexually assaulted her described the alleged attack as "frenzied" and "violent".

That complainant alleges Brand assaulted her at the Choice FM radio studios in central London in the mid-2000s.

She said she came out of a small room in the building to find Brand outside.

"He said 'aye aye'," she told the jury. "He grabbed me by my face, started to kiss me, and when he was kissing me he started pushing me - his body against me."

The woman continued: "He was kissing me, it was very frenzied. There was no time for me to even understand what was going on.

"He was running his hands over my body and I had my back against the wall at that point."

From behind a blue screen, the woman described the kiss as "sloppy" and "very, very rough", when asked by the prosecution barrister about the alleged attack.

"His hands at the same time were all over me," she said. "He touched my bum, my breasts, his body was pressed up against me."

The woman said she pushed him off and swore at him.

She said there were several people with him who she claims didn't say anything about what happened after the alleged assault.

The woman - now in her 50s - said she had never met Brand before and that she believed he'd been in the building because he was on Channel 4 show Big Brother's Big Mouth.

She told the jury: "His whole body was pressed against me - the kisses were hard and sloppy and going down my neck.

"His hands were moving so much - the reason I used the word frenzied was because it was violent. He just wasn't stopping."

She said she felt "dirty" after the encounter and "never told anybody", adding: "I felt shocked and stunned, shaken."

News.title: UK government to make Jackdaw gas field announcement
News.content:
The UK government is expected to announce a long-awaited decision on whether to approve the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea.

It is widely believed in Westminster that Jackdaw will be approved but that a decision on the Rosebank oil field off Shetland will not yet be made.

The question of whether to approve the two sites has become hugely politically significant and has been delayed for several months.

Multiple Whitehall sources have told BBC News the government would make an announcement on Jackdaw on Wednesday morning with the Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh expected to address MPs in the afternoon.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has spoken repeatedly of the need for a "flexible" approach to energy and is believed to be in favour of drilling more where licensing already exist in the North Sea.

Labour's 2024 manifesto pledged not to issue any new oil and gas licences in the North Sea but to honour existing ones such as Jackdaw.

News.title: Audit regulator looking into Manchester City accounting
News.content:
The UK audit regulator has confirmed it is leading inquiries into accounting irregularities at Manchester City.

The Financial Reporting Council confirmed in a letter to the House of Commons business select committee it had taken over "regulatory consideration" of the case from the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales on 30 September.

No formal investigation has started, but the FRC is making inquiries into the case.

It comes after Manchester City were found guilty by an independent commission of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons, including by artificially inflating the club's financial position by more than Â£900m. City are appealing the verdict.

The FRC has greater resources, and greater powers, to apply sanctions if it does find evidence of violations. It routinely oversees accounting standards at bigger institutions such as listed public companies, but not football clubs.

The FRC can look into the conduct of BDO, Manchester City's auditors, to ask whether the audit was in line with the rules.

It can also apply sanctions to individuals such as directors or employees of the Etihad club, if they are members of professional accountancy bodies.

BDO is the UK's fifth-biggest accounting firm, but claims to be a market leader in football, advising more Premier League and Championship clubs than any other firm.

The independent commission which looked into Manchester City found that the club gave a "misleading impression" of the scheme used to disguise the origin of shareholder funds injected into the club to its auditors, who were "unaware" of the scheme.

Manchester City have said they will appeal against the commission's decision, arguing that it contains "material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".

Liam Byrne, chair of the business select committee, called for greater powers for the FRC to look into similar cases.

He wrote on X: "The regulator's letter exposes gaps in its ability to compel evidence from the club and pursue directors who fall outside its disciplinary rules.

"This raises serious questions about the powers available to hold companies and directors to account.

"The government has a responsibility to explain why reforms to close these gaps were abandoned - and what will now be done to strengthen accountability."

BDO declined to comment.

News.title: Google resolves cloud outage affecting UK banks and websites
News.content:
Google Cloud says it has resolved disruption at its UK cloud site which caused an outage affecting UK banks, businesses and the courts.

The company, one of a few large cloud computing firms whose infrastructure and services underpin many online platforms, reported an "issue with multiple services" at its London data centre complex "europe-west2" early on Tuesday.

Revolut, Lloyds Bank and HSBC were among popular UK services that confirmed disruption on Tuesday morning, after thousands of reports of problems were raised by users online.

The tech giant apologised to those affected and thanked customers for their patience.

"We have resolved a disruption to Google Cloud services at a third-party facility in our europe-west2 cloud region due to a power event," a Google Cloud spokesperson said in a statement on Tuesday evening.

"Services have been restored."

They added that the company would publish an analysis of the incident on its service health dashboard, external, where it provides customers with updates about the status of its cloud services globally.

Cloud computing giants like Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud make their services available to clients in local or regional sites around the world, which they call "regions", containing their data centres.

In updates to its service dashboard on Tuesday morning, Google Cloud had said a number of its cloud services were "experiencing elevated errors and intermittent network failures in europe-west2 region" - its UK cloud facility in London.

It later said that the issues had stemmed from a "power event" within one of its smaller data centre zones, europe-west2-b.

These seemingly affected a host of popular UK platforms and services, with customers flagging issues with sites including Royal Mail, DPD and e-bike service Forest.

The HM Courts and Tribunals Service also said it was aware of an issue affecting the video platform used for remote hearings.

News.title: Man, 26, charged with woman's murder
News.content:
A man has been charged with the murder of a woman who was stabbed to death in a street in Manchester.

Lawrence Johnson, 26, of Dorking Avenue, has been charged with the murder of Alisha Samuels, also 26, and the attempted murder of a man following the incident on Thursday.

He has been remanded in custody and is due to appear at Manchester Magistrates' Court on Wednesday.

Det Ch Insp Justin Bryant said officers were continuing to investigate the circumstances surrounding Ms Samuels' death and to provide answers for her family.

Police are still appealing for information.

Det Ch Insp Bryant said: "I'd like to thank those that have called and supported our investigation thus far. Your reports are always taken seriously and prove vital to our work.

"I urge others who may have information, no matter how small, to please come forward."

News.title: Harry says he wants to 'reconcile' with his family
News.content:
The Duke of Sussex has said he wants to repair his complicated relationships with his father and brother, in a magazine interview.

"Some people don't want it to work out. I want it to work out. With everything else that's going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile - that's the key point," Prince Harry told GQ in New York.

"Scars stick around forever. But what your perception is, and what your mindset is to those things that have happened, letting go of the past, that's something that I would encourage everybody to do," said Prince Harry.

Last week Prince Harry and Meghan carried out their first public engagement together since their return to the UK in the summer.

The GQ interview with Prince Harry was conducted last month and released as the Royal Family were on duty in Windsor welcoming the Sultan of Oman at the start of a state visit.

But a spokesman for the Sussexes said the interview was recorded in late September and it was the entirely the publishers' decision when to run it - and that nothing should be read into the timing.

The spokesman also said that the reference to "some people don't want it to work out" was not a swipe at his brother Prince William or any other member of his family.

Prince Harry and Meghan moved from the UK to the United States in 2020, stepping down as working royals in what was an acrimonious departure.

Harry's memoir, Spare, showed the depth of the family fall out and the damaged relationship with his brother William.

Despite Prince Harry now being physically nearer to his family in the UK, there hasn't seemed to be any more emotional closeness with his brother Prince William, and in this interview Harry seems to be open to reconciliation.

It was a message of wanting to build bridges that he had previously sent in a BBC interview in May 2025, when he had been living in the US.

News.title: Second Labour MP suspended over Covid loan repayments
News.content:
A second Labour MP, Perran Moon, has been suspended over Covid loan repayments, after voluntarily referring himself for investigation.

Moon, the MP for Camborne and Redruth, is listed on Companies House as the co-director of a training company called Autoswot, external, which last filed accounts in June 2021.

Government Bounce Back Loans of up to Â£50,000 were made available to support small businesses during the pandemic, but a government report found the scheme was vulnerable to fraud and error.

In August, Labour MP Bayo Alaba was suspended after queries about a Covid-era loan, and a third MP, James McMurdock, quit Reform in 2025 after questions about eligibility for loans he received.

Bounce back loans worth a total of Â£46bn were issued when the scheme was launched in May 2020, making it the biggest of the government's pandemic-era loan schemes.

Each one had a 100% government guarantee, meaning taxpayers' cash was used to pay back banks if the companies failed, but the Covid counter-fraud commissioner later found total fraud and error estimated at up to Â£2.8bn to the public purse.

Autoswot had been set up in June 2019, a year before the loans became available, and at that time had forecast revenues of more than Â£200,000.

Moon stressed he had applied for the maximum loan of Â£50,000 within the rules, regularly seeking professional advice about its obligations, and would provide documents to the Labour Party investigation into the matter.

He said the loan was used to pay for "staffing and other essential business costs" during the pandemic and partial repayments were made until the company ceased trading in late 2022.

The BBC understands that Moon was repeatedly assured in writing by Companies House that no accounts needed to be filed after the company applied to be struck off, but that guidance was incorrect.

Moon, who was first elected in the 2024 Labour landslide following a career in communications and marketing, said the business folded due to unforeseen external market pressures and "despite the best efforts of staff".

He said: "In order for these matters to be looked into, I have voluntarily referred myself to the Labour Party's investigations process and will cooperate fully with this process.

"The loan application was made in good faith, and the information provided, including the company's turnover forecast, was accurate and properly based.

"I will continue to work hard every day representing my constituents while this party process is ongoing."

A Labour Party spokesperson confirmed Moon had referred himself for investigation.

"The Labour Party expects the highest standards from our elected representatives and we have robust processes in place to ensure those high standards are upheld," they said.

"We cannot comment further while the investigation is ongoing."

This is the second investigation the Labour Party has launched into the loans, with Alaba, the MP for Southend East and Rochford, also referring himself for investigation over loans made to a real estate company, Alaba Properties.

At the time, Alaba said: "There has been no attempt to avoid my financial obligations, and I am wholeheartedly committed to ensuring that the liability is met in full."

McMurdock, who now sits as an independent, was the first MP to be questioned over bounce back loans given to two fitness companies worth Â£70,000.

In 2025 McMurdock said all his business dealings had been compliant with the rules, adding that after taking "specialist legal advice" he had decided "to continue my parliamentary career as an independent MP".

News.title: UK to deploy jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
News.content:
The UK will deploy RAF Typhoon jets to defend Saudi Arabia in response to escalating Houthi missile and drone attacks, the government has said.

The defensive mission will help defend Saudi cities and infrastructure - a move authorised by Prime Minister Andy Burnham - against aerial attacks by the Iran-backed group.

It follows Houthi attacks on the Saudi capital Riyadh, as well as on energy sites on the country's coast.

"These aircraft will operate in a defensive role and will not conduct offensive strikes against the Houthis," Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said in a written statement on Tuesday.

News.title: Student who stabbed housemate 30 times admits murder
News.content:
A student who stabbed his housemate more than 30 times in a masked ambush has changed his murder plea to guilty.

Zack Coughlan, 23, attacked Jamie Collins, 21, in an alleyway near the garden of their home on 8 April and then left his body outside for eight hours before calling police.

A murder trial had been under way at Bristol Crown Court because Coughlan initially denied the charge, although he did admit killing Collins. He told jurors he stabbed Collins because he feared his housemate would kill him.

However, Coughlan, of Cleve Road, Filton, has now changed his plea to guilty and will be sentenced for murder on Wednesday.

Describing him as "a sensitive and caring young man", Collins' family said he had been "looking forward to finishing his journey" at the University of the West of England (UWE) and returning home to Swansea "in a matter of weeks".

"His passion for equality stood out to everyone who knew him. His unapologetic inclusivity will be his legacy for all of us. We know he was heading for a hugely successful future following his engineering and robotics degree," they added.

News.title: Jane Dodds standing down as Welsh Liberal Democrats leader
News.content:
Jane Dodds has announced she will stand down as leader of the Welsh Liberal Democrats.

Dodds said she would remain the party's only Member of the Senedd (MS), but that work to increase its presence in Wales' parliament "should be led by a new generation".

"Leading the Welsh Liberal Democrats has been the honour of my life," she said in a statement on Tuesday, adding "now is the right time" to hand over the role.

Only Welsh Lib Dem MP David Chadwick is eligible to seek nomination to replace Dodds at this stage, the party said.

Relations between Dodds and the UK Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey were strained after he previously called her leadership into question.

The Liberal Democrats have been represented by just one member in Cardiff Bay since 2016, initially by former Welsh Lib Dem leader Kirsty Williams and later by Dodds since 2021.

Dodds, who represents Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd in the Senedd, is a former social worker who was made her party's Welsh leader in November 2017.

She made headlines last year by getting the previous Welsh Labour government to agree to a greyhound racing ban and Â£1 bus fares for under-21s in return for helping it pass its budget.

In 2024 Lib Dem leader Sir Ed asked Dodds to reflect on her position over her handling of a sexual abuse case when she worked for the Church in England.

A 2021 report found Dodds made a "grave error of judgement" by not organising a meeting to discuss a particular case of abuse by a late former bishop who sexually abused at least 18 victims over a 15-year period.

Dodds accepted there were "shortcomings", but said she would continue as leader.

After nearly two years of cool relations over the matter, Davey backed Dodds before May's Welsh Parliament election, describing her as an "excellent member of the Senedd" who deserved to be re-elected.

Nominations to replace Dodds will open on 23 October and close on 16 November.

"After May's election, I've thought hard about what our party needs," she said.

"Wales needs more than one liberal voice in the Senedd.

"Building that team will take years of hard work in communities across the country, and I believe that work should be led by a new generation.

"Now is the right time to hand it over."

Brecon, Radnor and Cwm Tawe MP Chadwick said Dodds had "given an enormous amount to the Welsh Liberal Democrats and to public life in Wales, and she deserves our sincere thanks for her service as leader".

"There will understandably be questions about what comes next.

"Today should be about Jane and her contribution to our party.

"I will make a statement about my own political future in the coming days."

Welsh Liberal Democrat president Tim Sly said Dodds had "led our party with warmth, determination and integrity through some of the most turbulent years in Welsh and UK politics".

"She leaves the Welsh Liberal Democrats stronger in our communities and ready to build," he said.

Chadwick requires the support of 50 party members to be the only candidate to replace Dodds and take over as leader.

Should that not happen, or he were to decide not to run, all members on the party's approved parliamentary candidates list could then throw their hats into the ring.

News.title: Fifa call out ‘concerted effort to undermine’ Gianni Infantino after apology from The Times
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Fifa have acknowledged an apology from The Times over incorrect reporting that president Gianni Infantino was paid an undeclared second salary and have called out what it claims is a ‘concerted and ongoing effort’ to undermine the organisation and Infantino.

An article published by The Times a week ago claimed that Infantino had received a second salary from Fifa and that he had failed to declare the payments with that information proving incorrect. The newspaper removed the incorrect information and issued an apology to both Fifa and Infantino over the report.

Having seen and accepted the apology Fifa, via their Fifa Media account on X, took the opportunity to address the media and emphasise the need to ‘act responsibly’ and ‘carefully verify all sourcing’ in order to prevent false information from being published.

The organisation’s statement also addressed what it perceives is a co-ordinated effort to undermine Infantino’s presidency after the 56-year-old came under scrutiny over a proposal to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

That plan has raised concerns over his ability to perform in the role of president with Uefa among several parties to have called for his resignation.

Fifa’s statement reads: “FIFA takes note of an apology published today by The Times following an inaccurate and damaging report:

‘“On 13 October 2026 (Sport), we reported that Gianni Infantino received a "second salary" from Fifa, which Fifa had failed to disclose. This is incorrect. There was no “second salary.” Regulations do not require Fifa to include expenses and reimbursements received by Mr Infantino in its annual report as they are not considered "compensation" under Swiss reporting requirements. We also accept Mr Infantino did not purchase a property in Miami at a suspected undervalue as we reported and neither he nor his family are the legal or beneficial owners of Shadi LLC and have no control over that company, as we suggested. We are happy to make these corrections and apologise to Mr Infantino and Fifa for the errors.’

“As FIFA stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President. FIFA urges the media to act responsibly and carefully verify all sourcing to prevent the publication and subsequent reproduction of false and defamatory information.

“FIFA welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a license to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate, misleading, or totally false, as in this case, FIFA will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously.”

News.title: Rio Ngumoha shines in comeback Villarreal win but unsung Liverpool hero was true star
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

It might have been fitting that, on the night the watching Ian Rush’s 65th birthday, the goals flowed at Anfield. Yet even as Liverpool celebrated their most prolific ever No 9, it was more about the man in the No 10 shirt.

The vast majority of Rush’s record 346 goals for Liverpool were penalty-box finishes and if much of Alexis Mac Allister’s best work comes in rather deeper positions, the midfielder displayed his predatory streak. In the process, he ensured that Andoni Iraola’s attempts to rest and rotate, which looked likely to backfire after the worst half-hour of his reign, did not cost Liverpool.

“They were much better than us in the first half, and we were much better in the second half,” said Iraola. If both the teamsheet and the opening stages suggested Iraola was either being generous to his old teammate and assistant Inigo Perez or had underestimated his former sidekick, by the final whistle Liverpool were second in the embryonic Champions League table.

open image in gallery The worst half-hour of Andoni Iraola's reign did not cost him against former assistant Inigo Perez ( Getty )

And if they scarcely resembled potential continental champions, Iraola’s taste of European nights at Anfield has brought twin continental comebacks, each featuring a starring role from Mac Allister. It was witnessed by his near namesake, Gary McAllister, himself no stranger to important goals in Europe for Liverpool.

It was the kind of talismanic display that Dominik Szoboszlai provided last season. But with the Hungarian injured and Iraola benching the three biggest signings in Liverpool’s history, they needed someone to supply the inspiration. Mac Allister obliged. “The character, when you are 2-0 down and not playing well, he doesn’t panic,” noted Iraola.

Mac Allister was aided by the excellent Rio Ngumoha while Ronald Araujo’s equaliser again underlined what a fine bit of business Liverpool did by borrowing the Uruguayan from Barcelona. Florian Wirtz, one of the £364m trio held in reserve, came off the bench to score the fourth.

open image in gallery Alexis Mac Allister was aided by a brilliant Rio Ngumoha (centre) performance ( PA Wire )

But Mac Allister, scorer of a winner against Atletico Madrid and, on another occasion when Iraola fielded a weakened team, the opener against Tottenham was pivotal. His footballing intelligence gives him an eye for goal. “I'm not tall but I love going in the box,” said the Argentinian. “My dad is a bit smaller than me but he was quite good in the air so maybe it's something I got from him.” So the younger Mac Allister rose highest to glance in a header from Kostas Tsimikas’ corner.

His second showed another attribute for a goalscoring midfielder. “He can arrive inside the box like a No 8,” added Iraola. Mac Allister timed his run into the penalty box perfectly to put Liverpool ahead, crashing in a shot from six yards off the underside of the bar and following a cutback from Ngumoha. “It’s up there with one of the best I’ve played,” said the 18-year-old, who became the youngest player since Michael Owen to make two goals in a game for Liverpool.

The first came when Araujo snuck in at the far post to capitalise on poor defending by Cardona and head in the teenager’s cross. It was, albeit indirectly, a second goal from a corner and a second in as many Champions League games for Araujo. ‘Big Ron’ is proving a big threat from set-pieces.

After Mac Allister doubled his tally for the night, Wirtz drove in Liverpool’s fourth following a pass from Cody Gakpo, who was making his first appearance for a month.

open image in gallery Florian Wirtz scored his first goal of the season to give Liverpool daylight ( PA )

He had been summoned at half-time when Ryan Gravenberch, who had begun as the No 10, moved to right-back in place of Araujo. Iraola had left Liverpool’s three £100m men on the bench. After half an hour, it seemed he would need to summon them straight away. Instead, he waited before introducing Wirtz. By the time Alexander Isak came on, Liverpool led. They had four goals to their name when Bradley Barcola joined them.

Liverpool ended up with a 16th win in 19 group-stage games since the Champions League expanded. For Villarreal a seventh straight away defeat in Europe. It could, though, have been very different. “If you score three goals and play very well in the game and you end up taking home a defeat where you have to analyse it is on the errors we made,” said Perez.

But Villarreal started superbly. Iraola’s version of his strongest available side was his freshest, with six changes. A fixture list of Brighton, Chelsea and Arsenal may have been prominent in his thoughts. Yet Liverpool scarcely showed sharpness at the start. They were strangely passive, applying too little pressure to the players on the ball. Their offside trap malfunctioned. They committed individual mistakes.

The worst came from Virgil van Dijk. An attempt to head the ball back to Alisson was horribly misdirected, the Liverpool captain only finding Georges Mikautadze, who angled a shot past the goalkeeper. Van Dijk had his hands up in apology immediately.

open image in gallery Virgil van Dijk’s error gifted Villarreal an early opener ( PA )

Villarreal’s second came when they pierced the offside trap with two runners. Nathan Saliba slid a pass through; Villarreal had two men played onside by Tsimikas and Sergi Cardona slid his shot past Alisson.

Even after seemingly sealing victory, Liverpool afforded them a lifeline. After conceding three goals to LASK last week, they let Villarreal get a third through Tani Oluwaseyi’s calm far-post finish; the stand-in right-back Gravenberch gave him too much room.

The danger was that Iraola and Perez, who had shared so much, would share the points. This was a reunion for the former double act, even if it seemed that Iraola had not warned his friend about the weather. Perez did not even don a coat in the Merseyside rain. His attire was more suitable for the Spanish sun, even if he had greater regrets. “We didn’t know how to manage the emotion tonight,” he rued.

News.title: Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey spares death row inmate, citing doubts about evidence
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey on Tuesday commuted the death sentence of a death-row inmate after a number of former public officials, and the current district attorney, raised doubts about his conviction.

The Republican governor said she was commuting Toforest Johnson’s death sentence to life in prison without parole. Johnson was convicted of the 1995 murder of Jefferson County Deputy Sheriff William Hardy. Johnson has long maintained he is innocent.

“When presented with Mr. Johnson’s case, I had concerns there was not enough direct evidence to carry out the most serious punishment, death,” Ivey said in a statement. “My decision is not a determination of innocence, but a recognition that the circumstances of this case justify commuting his death sentence to life imprisonment, without possibility of parole.”

Ivey has overseen 27 executions during her time as governor. She has commuted the death sentence of three death row inmates.

Hardy was shot twice in the head while working off-duty security at a hotel. Johnson has maintained he was on the other side of town at the time of the shooting.

Ty Alper, one of Toforest Johnson’s attorneys, said they are grateful to Ivey for “diligently reviewing Toforest’s case and taking action to spare an innocent man from execution.” Alper said the fight to overturn the conviction will continue.

“Toforest Johnson is innocent. Now it is up to the courts to overturn his conviction and grant him a new trial. We will keep fighting until he is home with his family,” Alper said.

There has been a long-running legal effort to win a new trial in the case that has garnered national attention and was the subject of a podcast. Jefferson County District Attorney Danny Carr, who was elected in 2018, has supported Johnson’s bid for a new trial. Carr wrote in a 2024 court filing that the “evidence in this case has unraveled over 20 years.”

Carr said in 2024 that credible alibi witnesses place Johnson elsewhere at the time of the crime. He said there are multiple reasons to doubt the key prosecution witness, a woman who “claimed she overheard Johnson confess to the murder on a three-way phone call on which she was eavesdropping.”

The key prosecution witness at Johnson's 1998 trial testified that, while eavesdropping on a phone call, she heard a man she believed was Johnson admitting to the crime. She was paid $5,000 in 2001 for her testimony, and Johnson’s lawyers argue that the state withheld evidence of monetary motivation for the testimony.

A number of former judges and prosecutors have joined those seeking a new trial for Johnson amid questions about his conviction more than 20 years ago. Former Alabama Attorney General Bill Baxley, former Chief Justices Sonny Hornsby and Drayton Nabers, and several former judges and prosecutors have submitted briefs or written editorials supporting a new trial.

News.title: Wanna go to Magic Kingdom for Thanksgiving? Better luck next year
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Thanksgiving travelers hoping to add a festive night at Disney World to their holiday plans may be left with a plate full of disappointment after tickets to a popular Magic Kingdom event have sold out.

Tickets to Mickey’s Very Merry Christmas Party on November 25, the night before Thanksgiving, are no longer available at Magic Kingdom in Orlando, Florida, according to the event’s ticketing website.

Tickets for the November 25 event cost $209 per adult (guests over the age of 10) before selling out. However, travelers still have other opportunities to attend the Christmas party around Thanksgiving Day, with tickets available as of Tuesday for November 27 at $219 per adult and November 29 at $214 per adult.

The sellout applies only to the separately ticketed Christmas party, not regular daytime admission to Magic Kingdom. Standard park tickets were still available for November 25 at the time of publication Tuesday.

Mickey’s Very Merry Christmas Party transforms Magic Kingdom into a holiday celebration on select nights in November and December, featuring exclusive entertainment, seasonal treats, festive decorations and experiences not available during regular park hours.

open image in gallery Standard park tickets for November 25 were still available Tuesday, but tickets to Mickey’s Very Merry Christmas Party that night – the eve of Thanksgiving – had sold out ( Getty Images )

Highlights include Mickey’s Once Upon a Christmastime Parade, featuring Disney characters, holiday floats and Santa Claus, Mickey’s Most Merriest Celebration stage show, and Minnie’s Wonderful Christmastime Fireworks Show.

The after-hours party runs from 7 p.m. to midnight, although ticket holders can enter the park as early as 4 p.m. to enjoy rides and attractions before the festivities begin.

Visitors must purchase a separate ticket to attend the Christmas party, as regular park admission, Park Hopper tickets and annual passes do not include access to the event.

Guests who already have Christmas party tickets for November 25 can attend as planned. Those who missed out can choose another available date or adjust their holiday itineraries.

As of Tuesday, Christmas party tickets were also available for the following December dates: December 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 11, 13, 15, 17 and 18.

Travelers planning a Disney World trip for the 2027 holiday season should prepare for a pricier getaway.

A one-day ticket to Magic Kingdom on Thanksgiving Day 2027 is currently listed at $224 per adult, up from $209 this year.

Disney unveiled its 2027 ticket prices earlier this month, with admission reaching a record $229 per adult at Magic Kingdom and EPCOT on the most expensive dates: Christmas Day and New Year’s Eve.

News.title: PSG star hailed as ‘most underrated player of all time’ after Barcelona win
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Fabian Ruiz has been hailed as the “most underrated player of all time” after scoring in the Champions League holders’ statement 4-2 victory over Barcelona.

Ruiz tapped home PSG’s fourth after the French giants were pegged back twice in their win at the Parc des Princes, first by Xavi Esparti before Lamine Yamal produced his latest moment of magic to level in the 79th minute.

Vitinha’s strike two minutes later gave PSG the lead once again and it didn’t take much longer for Ruiz to put the game out of sight, finishing Achraf Hakimi’s cross.

“He could be the most underrated player of all time, Fabian Ruiz,” said Joe Cole on TNT Sports. “He’s won everything in the game, Champions League, does his job, and what I would say is they look a stronger side with him in.”

open image in gallery Fabian Ruiz scored PSG's fourth goal ( AP )

Ruiz came into the season off the back of winning the World Cup with Spain, being an integral figure in midfield alongside Rodri.

PSG winger Desire Doue, who brilliantly fired in the opener in Paris, was delighted with his side’s performance.

“The atmosphere was crazy tonight,” he said. “We did a great job because we won obviously but we’re really happy with the content of the match.

“We did some amazing things, we never quit and when you win against one of the biggest teams in Europe you are really happy so we are really happy tonight. I’m always happy when I can help the team.

“Every game you say that we send a message, I don’t know. We just try and play the best football we can and we did a great job tonight.”

PSG return to action this weekend against Ligue 1 leaders Lyon, who are above them in the table on goal difference.

News.title: Paris NFL game given green light to go ahead after violent protests in France
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Sunday's NFL matchup in Paris between the New Orleans Saints and the Pittsburgh Steelers will proceed as scheduled under heightened security measures, the league announced Tuesday, following a period of violent unrest that engulfed the French capital.

Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu confirmed Tuesday that military personnel will reinforce police in a "massive" security operation targeting demonstrations set for Saturday, following looting and widespread rioting across Paris and other French cities on October 17.

"We always have a very strong security presence," said Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's executive vice president of club business, international and league events.

"That presence will be heightened with local authorities (as we are) making sure that there's nothing more important from our standpoint than team security, fan security (and) everybody involved with this game."

Hosted at the Stade de France, the fixture marks the first regular season game the league has ever staged in the French capital. It forms part of a record nine-game slate of international matches this season as the NFL targets lucrative global markets.

Peter O'Reilly has confirmed Sunday's game will go ahead ( AP )

O'Reilly noted that the NFL is considering adding a 10th international game to the season starting in 2027.

The turmoil over the weekend, representing some of the worst unrest France has suffered in years, followed weeks of largely peaceful student demonstrations over school conditions and living costs. French authorities imposed curfews across several cities on Monday.

NFL officials have already been on the ground in Paris for 10 days, O'Reilly told reporters.

"We feel confident that we would not have any impact on the broader resources needed," he said. "That's always top of mind for us and we feel confident that we wouldn't be depleting resources in a negative way around this game."

Saints star Juwan Johnson voiced concerns over safety on Monday, stating some of his family members are “very undecided" about whether to travel to Paris for the game.

“Just being safe is obviously the biggest thing,” Johnson said. "Some guys have family here. Some guys have their parents, their kids and things like that."

Johnson said his family “may be making the trip. If they do I’m sure it’ll be great. If they don’t, obviously I completely understand. We’re very undecided right now.”

News.title: Even Mike Lindell is worried about Trump’s health
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Even Mike Lindell, a fierce Donald Trump loyalist, has voiced concerns about the 80-year-old president’s health, apparently suggesting that he’s exhausting himself with nightly rallies to boost Republicans’ chances of winning the midterm elections.

In an effort to keep control of Congress, Trump has been stumping for GOP candidates like Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and Sen. Roger Marshall from Kansas as Democrats gain ground in red states.

Lindell — the founder of bedding company MyPillow who unsuccessfully ran for Minnesota governor this year — seemed to imply that those nights standing in front of crowds and giving hour-long speeches are catching up to the president.

During a video call with supporters, someone asked Lindell how he and the president were doing, noting that they both look exhausted, according to a recording of the call posted on X by independent journalist Aaron Rupar Monday.

“He looked about as tired as I’ve seen him. He was very…I don’t want to say the word ‘down’...him and I, we don’t get down,” Lindell responded. “But he’s got to realize he’s on these rallies. I mean, just one after another after another.”

open image in gallery Even Mike Lindell, a Donald Trump loyalist, has voiced concerns about the 80-year-old president’s health, apparently suggesting that he’s exhausting himself with nightly rallies to boost Republicans’ chances of winning the midterm elections ( Getty Images )

Lindell has denied reporting about his comments on Trump’s tiredness, calling it “fake news.”

“Here’s a REAL quote for everyone: President Trump works TIRELESSLY everyday to SAVE OUR COUNTRY. Nobody I know could keep up with his schedule and stay as optimistic as he is everyday,” Lindell wrote on X Tuesday.

Trump has drawn increased scrutiny over his health in his second term, after appearing to doze off during public events and being photographed with bruised hands and swollen ankles.

The president’s doctor, Sean Barbabella, has chalked up the bruising to frequent handshaking and aspirin use and said the leg swelling was from a common condition in those over 70 called chronic venous insufficiency.

Trump has appeared to have trouble staying awake during Cabinet meetings and Oval Office appearances — and even more lively events like the UFC fight he hosted on the White House lawn for his birthday and an NBA Finals game at Madison Square Garden in June.

open image in gallery ‘He looked about as tired as I’ve seen him,’ Lindell said on a video call with supporters. ‘But he’s got to realize he’s on these rallies. I mean, just one after another after another’ ( AFP via Getty Images )

Just 44 percent of Americans thought Trump was in good enough physical health to serve effectively as president in a Washington Post/ABC News/Ipsos poll from April. Fifty-five percent said he was not in good enough physical health to properly lead.

When asked if he has the mental sharpness to serve effectively as president, 59 percent said he did not, while 40 percent said he did.

But the White House and his doctor insist that Trump is in great shape.

Barberella wrote in a summary of Trump’s medical exam in May that the president’s “cognitive and physical performance are excellent” and that he’s “fully fit to carry out all duties of the Commander-in-Chief and Head of State.”

“President Trump is the sharpest, most accessible, and energetic president in American history,” White House spokesman Davis Ingle told The Independent in August.

A man has been charged with murder and attempted murder after the death of a woman in Manchester.

The charges relate to the death of Alisha Samuels and the attempted murder of a man in Dorking Avenue, Manchester, on October 15, Greater Manchester Police said.

Lawrence Johnson, 26, of Dorking Avenue, Manchester has been charged with murder and attempted murder, police said on Tuesday evening.

He has been remanded in custody and is due to appear at Manchester Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday.

Investigators are still appealing for information relating to the death of Ms Samuels.

Detective Chief Inspector Justin Bryant said: “We are continuing to work into establishing the full circumstances of Alisha’s tragic death and to provide Alisha’s family with some answers.

“We have now charged a man, but our investigation is not over.

“I’d like to thank those that have called and supported our investigation thus far, your reports are always taken seriously and prove vital to our work.

“I urge others who may have information, no matter how small, to please come forward.”

Anyone who may have witnessed this incident, or has mobile phone, CCTV or doorbell footage, is asked to contact police on 0161 856 5464 or via the Major Incident Public Portal at https://mipp.police.uk/operation/06GMP26S62-PO1.

Alternatively, people can contact the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Rio Ngumoha dazzles with coming-of-age night in Europe
News.content:
A precious victory at Brentford, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak among the goals and a couple of improved showings from Florian Wirtz mean things now look a little brighter for Liverpool.

They are strong favourites to make it nine points from nine in the Champions League by beating Villarreal at Anfield this evening, the Spanish club they vanquished in the 2022 semi-finals under Jürgen Klopp.

Liverpool drew Atletico Madrid at home (already ticked off) and Inter Milan away as their two pot-one fixtures, which is about as kind as you can expect. A top-two finish in the league phase is a realistic aspiration for Andoni Iraola’s team, and something would need to go badly awry for them to miss out on the top eight.

Cody Gakpo, Dominik Szoboszlai and Isak returned from injury to strengthen Liverpool at Brentford, although Szoboszlai has been lost for a few weeks following another hamstring complication.

Villarreal have punched well above their weight in Europe for the past few decades, reaching two European Cup semi-finals (beaten by Arsenal in 2006 as well as Liverpool in 2022) and winning the Europa League under Unai Emery in 2021.

They have been mediocre in La Liga so far this season though, 12th after nine games on nine points and with a goal difference of zero. Their Champions League performances have been promising though, losing by the odd goal in a frantic finish at Borussia Dortmund and beating Napoli 3-1 at home. Villarreal’s best player is probably Senegalese central midfielder Pape Gueye, and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pépé is also in their ranks. Gueye, despite his position, is their joint-top scorer in all competitions with three goals.

Iraola will be up against his close friend and former Athletic Bilbao team-mate Inigo Perez who is now in charge at Villarreal. Perez was also Iraola’s assistant at Rayo Vallecano, the job which earned the Basque his move to Bournemouth. Perez guided Rayo Vallecano to the Uefa Conference League final last season.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: England dealt harsh lesson in Pakistan collapse
News.content:
Brendon McCullum wants his team to learn how to adapt as they prepare for the World Cup and this was a lesson in how not to master a run chase.

Failing to overhaul 302 is not an embarrassment, but the way England threw away a good start with some brittle batting gives McCullum plenty to ponder.

Spin exposed familiar failings as left-armer Arafat Minhas added six for 40 to his 59 from 58 with the bat, but it was also short balls from the seamers that hurt England. A two-paced pitch made the back-of-a-length delivery tricky, as it had in the match between Sri Lanka and Pakistan on the same ground at the weekend, but England failed to find a way to adjust their tempo.

Ben Duckett, Joe Root and Sam Curran were all dismissed by seamers hitting the pitch hard and forcing them to play square while Arafat exposed limitations against spin. He bowled Harry Brook for five with a beauty that dipped and straightened as he mixed up his arm ball with consistent accuracy to deadly effect.

News.title: Fried chicken and sugary drinks: Tanzania battles a growing obesity problem
News.content:
In early 2025, Said Shukuru, 31, was experiencing life-threatening health concerns. He weighed 150 kg (over 20 stone); his body mass index (BMI) was over 40 and he had a blood pressure of 190/100.

“It was very serious,” says Shukuru. In April last year, he underwent a successful mini gastric bypass operation at the Aga Khan Specialised Polyclinic in Masaki, Dar Es Salaam. His weight has since halved.

Shukuru’s case may be extreme, but his story serves as a warning. Overweight and obesity levels are increasing fast across East Africa, and particularly in Tanzania. Unless the government responds properly, the country faces a looming public health crisis.

Overweight and obesity in Tanzania have grown over the past 40 years because of economic development and liberalisation, urbanisation and increasingly sedentary lifestyles. Traditional diets, based on whole foods, are being replaced by refined and processed products. To make matters worse, chicken and chips, known as kuku chips, and sugary drinks are everywhere.

“When you live in an urban area like Dar (Es Salaam),” says Shukuru, “junk food is cheaper than groceries.”

The origins of these developments lie in Tanzania’s economic history. During the colonial period, fruits and legumes were exported while high-energy, starchy foods like maize were produced for domestic consumption, says Joyce Kinabo, professor of nutrition at Sokoine University.

“Food security was considered as having a lot of maize,” says Kinabo.

News.title: US warns over travel in Kenya as Ebola cases mount
News.content:
The United States has urged citizens to reconsider travel to Kenya, raising its travel alert level after the country reported an eighth case of Ebola.

The East African nation has recorded a rash of cases linked to a Kenyan businessman who died after travelling from Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

DRC is currently enduring the second worst Ebola outbreak on record with more than 4,000 deaths since May, though the true toll is thought to be far higher.

“The level was changed from Level 2 to Level 3 due to health risks,” the US embassy in Kenya said, a day after the State Department issued renewed travel advice for its citizens.

“Reconsider travel in Kenya due to risk of health, crime, kidnapping, terrorism, unrest and traffic safety. Some areas have increased risk,” it said.

The alert came as Kenyan doctors leaders demanded better protective equipment against the highly infectious virus.

Three of the confirmed Ebola cases are reported to be health staff who cared for the businessman and the others are thought to be relatives who visited him.

News.title: US records first human case of H5N1 this year
News.content:
A man in Washington has tested positive for H5N1, marking the first human case of bird flu in the US this year.

The patient, who works on a dairy farm, was reportedly infected after being exposed to two infected cows.

H5N1 has become endemic on US dairy farms after ‘spilling over’ from birds in 2024, and has since infected more than 1,000 herds across dozens of states.

The person is not seriously ill and is isolating at home, according to the Washington State Department of Health.

Scientists have long warned that if H5N1 mutates and gains the ability to spread person-to-person, it could trigger the next global pandemic – and each new infection gives the virus more opportunities to replicate and change.

Last week, a 50-year-old man in Taiwan was infected with a different strain of bird flu, H7N7, genetic analysis of which showed the virus had undergone adaptations to spread more effectively between mammals.

Of the more than 1,000 people who have contracted H5N1 since it was first detected in the late 1990s, almost half have died.

Its “extraordinarily high” mortality rate means that, were it to gain the ability to spread between people, it would be of “enormous concern”, the World Health Organization (WHO) previously warned.

However, the strain circulating among US dairy cattle, clade 2.3.4.4b, has proven less lethal to humans.
