Sports.title: The Phil Foden show in front of 20,000 empty seats at the Etihad: Man City's hat-trick hero has found the fizz and purpose that deserted him last season as he stakes his claim in style, writes JACK GAUGHAN
Sports.content:
The Phil Foden show in front of 20,000 empty seats at the Etihad: Man City's hat-trick hero has found the fizz and purpose that deserted him last season as he stakes his claim in style, writes JACK GAUGHAN

More captivating and competitive adverts for the Champions League’s group phase are available – a night when thousands of blue seats remained strikingly vacant - but Phil Foden won’t mind.

While all eyes are on how Manchester City replace Erling Haaland in the eventuality of a more pressing injury than the knock from the weekend, Foden made his point on who fills in for Antoine Semenyo on the right wing.

Semenyo will miss the next two months with a knee problem and it will be a fight between Foden and Iliman Ndiaye as to who makes that spot their own. Foden’s hat-trick after notching against Ipswich Town four days earlier does his chances no harm. His first two goals were products of super link-up with Rico Lewis, the pair in sync in one-touch blurs of movement, and Foden slamming high into the AEK Athens net.

And after appearing generally more buoyant at the weekend, Foden is playing with a little more fizz – the sort he found early on last season before his form nosedived – and just looks more confident. Less sideways stuff, more purpose.

Enzo Maresca has publicly accepted responsibility for relocating Foden’s consistent best, something not seen for over two years, and the signs are that manager and player are working well together. But it is only a start at the moment and Semenyo’s absence should provide a greater chance to build upon that.

City were already leading once Foden found the net, Elliot Anderson mopping up the rebound once Enzo Fernandez’s free kick had kissed the bar and bounced back.

Phil Foden sparkled like the player of old as he snagged a hat-trick against AEK Athens at home

With the absence of Erling Haaland in the starting XI, it was up to the Striking Viking's team-mates to seize the spotlight in Europe

That Anderson celebrated while collapsed in a heap after being caught by a late lunge as he found the net seemed perfectly in keeping with the central midfielder’s Action Man act, somebody who spends half of his matches on the floor as tackles fly.

The free kick had been won by European debutant Floyd Samba, a 17-year-old who became their second-youngest starter in the Champions League. Son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Chris, the academy graduate scored twice in the Carabao Cup against Norwich City last month in an unfamiliar centre forward role and was called to perform similar on Tuesday.

Samba’s tenacity in tracking back saw him barge Kervin Arriaga out of possession and off he charged towards goal, bouncing off challenges until finally felled 20 yards out. Seconds later, Anderson had his first goal since a £116million summer move.

Rayan Cherki’s sumptuous drag back produced the third, the Frenchman placing into the far corner, after AEK briefly threatened to make a fist of the evening when Stavros Pilios drove across Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Some of the City movement showcased further signs of their improvement under Maresca, and the Cherki clipped pass for Lewis to lay-off for Foden’s first-time finish for City’s fourth provided the best example of that. Yet eyes continued to cast up towards the stands. Whatever the reason, it almost felt as if there were more inflatable bananas inside this stadium on Saturday than there were supporters for this continental tie.

The Etihad Stadium and City fans are often dealt a bad rap for attendances but the sparsity was certainly stark. Unusually stark, the new Pep Guardiola Stand yawning three weeks since the guilty verdicts dropped and the appeal lodged.

Rayan Cherki produced a sumptuous third goal but there were fewer than normal in the Etihad to watch the show

The stands were unusually bare - but the rafters will be packed for the return of Premier League action

This will be back to being a full house for their next Premier League assignment, against Brighton a week on Saturday, although it will be intriguing to see how many show up when Napoli arrive at the end of November. The potential to watch Kevin De Bruyne again might skew that somewhat.

This was well-priced, certainly more affordable than Paris Saint-Germain last week. But the Etihad was only really half-full, a similar crowd to that Norwich game in fact, and they missed the Foden show.

That was complete 14 minutes from time when he raced away into the corner having secured a hat-trick, his fourth for the club. A gaping net, timing a run to meet the cross of another European debutant, Ryan McAidoo. Maybe that month off following the red card at Old Trafford did Foden good.

Sports.title: Revealed: How Lord's is taking drastic action to sort pitch problems for 2027 Ashes Test after 'unsatisfactory' surface against New Zealand
Sports.content:
Revealed: How Lord's is taking drastic action to sort pitch problems for 2027 Ashes Test after 'unsatisfactory' surface against New Zealand

Lord’s will not host any cricket for 18 days during the build-up to the 2027 Ashes Test in a bid to avoid a repeat of the pitch problems that made headlines over the summer.

The groundstaff had only a clear 10 days before the first Test against New Zealand in June, when a surface of variable bounce was rated ‘unsatisfactory’ by the ICC, prompting a public apology from MCC and earning the venue an unprecedented demerit point.

There were also 10 days between finals day of the Hundred and the second Test against Pakistan in August, when the surface was rated ‘satisfactory’ – the second-highest of the four ratings.

The ECB want to ensure venues have between seven and nine clear days before hosting a Test next summer.

But Lord’s officials are taking no chances when it comes to next summer’s high-profile second Test against Australia starting on June 30, and have given head groundsman Karl McDermott and his team what Rob Lynch, MCC’s director of cricket and operations, called ‘the best chance of producing the best pitch’.

MCC’s determination to deal with the slowness and inconsistency of their surfaces has produced a raft of bold measures, including the recent decision to dig up Pitch 9 – which hosted the New Zealand Test.

Lord’s will not host any cricket for 18 days during the build-up to the 2027 Ashes Test in a bid to avoid a repeat of the pitch problems that made headlines over the summer

The pitch for June's Test against New Zealand was rated 'unsatisfactory' amid variable bounce

It is the first time in over 25 years that the home of cricket has taken such drastic action, taking the pitch out of action until 2029. The process involved digging down 12 inches, and replacing it with four inches of stabilising crushed granite, 20mm of porous matter and nearly eight inches of Ongar loam.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this year, MCC are also moving ahead with plans to instal three permanent drop-in pitches over the next few years, with a view to staging a domestic match on one of them in 2029, and international cricket the following summer. Each pitch should have a lifespan of 10-15 years.

With the Wormsley ground, an hour’s drive away up the M40, now bearing some of the Lord’s load, MCC plan to reduce the number of days’ cricket they host in 2027 from this year’s 63 to 55 or 56.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick dismisses Erik ten Hag's damning suggestions of 'toxic' culture and broken promises at Man United - and insists he has the backing of his Old Trafford bosses despite six games without a win
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick dismisses Erik ten Hag's damning suggestions of 'toxic' culture and broken promises at Man United - and insists he has the backing of his Old Trafford bosses despite six games without a win

Michael Carrick is adamant there is no ‘toxic culture’ at Old Trafford despite explosive allegations by former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag.

United landed in Italy for their Champions League clash with Como without a win in six games and missing nine senior players as they were met with a storm warning ahead of Wednesday's game at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia.

Asked about Ten Hag’s comments, where he complained of broken promises and a toxic dressing room culture during his time at the club, Carrick insisted he has the support of the owners, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

He also knows that will count for nothing if he cannot deliver results after the club’s worst start to a league season in 40 years.

‘That’s Erik’s opinion,’ said Carrick. ‘Why wouldn’t I (feel backed)? I’m in this position. I have a really good relationship with everybody at the football club.

‘There are really no issues and no problems with any of that side. There are certain conversations we have that we’re really clear — with Jason, with Omar, with the owners, and down to the players. It’s really important we’re all pulling in the same direction.'

Michael Carrick has stressed that he has full backing of Manchester United's hierarchy

The current head coach was forced to answer to an inflammatory interview from one of his predecessors Erik ten Hag

Carrick also dismissed suggestions of a toxic culture at United after Ten Hag claimed that the club fed it by giving power to the players during his time in charge.

‘Since I came back, the players and the staff have given us everything that they could give,’ Carrick added.

‘We’ve had some good performances. We’ve had some performances that we want to do better and we can improve on. We’ve made some mistakes.

‘But I have to say, the type of performance we put into the weekend and for large parts against Atletico, there’s a lot of togetherness there. There’s a lot of will and determination to do better and wanting to do it for each other, which is important.

‘So in that regard for the group, I couldn’t be happier with the togetherness, for sure.’

With United struggling for form, Carrick accepted his future is going to be a source of debate, adding: ‘I don’t need any reassurance. It’s pretty clear. I know the role, I know my responsibilities. I don’t need anyone else to tell me when it’s going well or when it needs to be better.

‘I know we’ve got to win football games for everything to flow and everything to fall into place.’

Ten Hag saw things differently, saying of the ownership: ‘They promised me loyalty, they promised me backing, they promised communication, that we get aligned. We spoke about the issues. But the promises, they didn’t keep.’

Ten Hag also hit out at Ronaldo during his second spell at the club, telling the Athletic: ‘He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him.

‘I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United. Obviously, he’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision and keep the players I admire in.’

As for the present crop, Carrick must do without the suspended Leny Yoro, while Lisandro Martinez, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Benjamin Sesko, Luke Shaw, Patrick Dorgu, Ayden Heaven and Manuel Ugarte are unavailable due to injury or illness.

It leaves Carrick with a major headache in defence with Matthijs De Ligt set to make his comeback from a back injury after nearly a year out of action.

‘It’s great to have him back,’ said Carrick. ‘He’s had such a long journey of maybe 11 months or so of being out, being patient, worked hard.

‘So we’re delighted to have him back. He’s fit, he’s ready and he’s been training for a number of weeks now, so he’s in a really good place.’

The weather forecast made equally grim reading for United after they landed at the end of a day of downpours here. Up to 64 millimetres of rain is due to fall before the game, and lightning is expected close to the early kick-off time.

‘There are no immediate concerns for me,’ smiled Carrick. ‘We’re kind of used to the rain, so we’ll make the most of it.’

Sat next to him at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Tuesday night, Andrey Santos was asked about Martinez’s bombshell interview after last week’s defeat in Madrid in which his teammate criticised the Old Trafford hierarchy — and by association the club’s summer signings – over United’s transfer strategy in the summer.

‘We know the comments about Licha,’ said Santos, a £50million buy from Chelsea. ‘But I think now it’s done, so we have to move on to tomorrow. We are on the same page (as a group) and we believe in ourselves and our teammates.’

Sports.title: England's fallibility against spin comes back to haunt them: Scratchy and overly cautious batting sees Harry Brook's men implode to heavy defeat against Pakistan
Sports.content:
Just as England thought they had got their white-ball house in order, their fallibility against spin came back to haunt them: their final nine wickets toppling for 95 runs in heavy tri-series defeat to Pakistan in Rawalpindi.

In a throwback to the kind of performance that saw the one-day team plunge as low as eighth in the rankings, temporarily threatening their direct qualification for next year’s World Cup, they somehow ceded the momentum of the match from a position of 120 for one in the 19th over.

From the moment Tom Banton became the first domino soon after registering a third successive half century in this format, slapping the previously unheralded left-arm spinner Arafat Minhas straight to midwicket, there was a familiar inevitability about what followed.

In half a dozen victories versus Sri Lanka and India earlier this year, England appeared to have struck the perfect tempo against spin but here they became overly cautious, scratching through a boundary-less, 48 ball spell in mid innings that saw the required rate surge from under a run a ball to over seven an over.

England captain Harry Brook said afterwards that his side were ‘pretty happy’ being set a target of 303 - and what would have represented their third successful highest chase in Asia.

But against Minhas’ collection of arm balls, subtle variations and moderate turn, they imploded. Only Brook amongst the half dozen victims could argue that he had been undone by a delivery that truly ripped off a surface upon which the 21-year-old all-rounder claimed a debut five-for versus Australia in May.

England collapsed to a disappointing 87-run defeat against Pakistan on Tuesday in Rawalpindi

England were scratchy and cautious and succumbed to spinner Arafat Minhas, who took 6-40

In recent months, England have shown improvement in their rotation of strike against the spinners through the middle overs, yet here neglecting the chance to be aggressive proved detrimental. Until Jamie Overton, a player much more accomplished walking to the crease to face seam, did so fatally with an awkward lunge to long-on after only a couple of sighters. From seven down, England lasted only a further dozen deliveries.

These collective travails rekindled memories of the Test team being tortured by turn in Pakistan two years ago, spoiling what had until that point been a tactically adept performance.

Yes, there was some shoddy fielding, with Gus Atkinson and wicketkeeper Jordan Cox, twice, squandering presentable chances that allowed Minhas and another newbie Hasan Nawaz to post career-best ODI scores.

But at the start of a 21-game minimum stretch heading into the 2027 World Cup, Brook highlighted the kind of flexibility England are going to need both from venue to venue and within game if they are to challenge for a second global 50-over title in southern Africa.

England begin their campaign with fixtures against Bangladesh and Sri Lanka in Windhoek, Namibia, and also play a couple of group matches in Port Elizabeth, which at sea level plays very differently to the bouncier conditions of South Africa’s Highveld grounds, Centurion and the Wanderers.

Their planning is focused on adapting in real time and it was therefore encouraging to see Brook adopt a different game plan to the one that has seen England win three straight series coming into this triangular tournament.

Since the playing conditions in ODIs were changed in July 2025, reducing two white balls to one after 34 overs of an innings, England have used reverse swing as a primary weapon at the death, but with minimal movement on offer, Brook became creative instead, rotating six bowlers including three spinners in the final 10 overs.

It might not have had the greatest effect as Pakistan smacked 91 runs in that period, but opting for variety rather than uniformity in the attack will undoubtedly serve this team better in the long run.

England have improved against spin recently but their lack of aggression was detrimental

Similarly, the promotion of Sam Curran to number five - a tactic used against the Indians in midsummer, before injury struck - showed adaptability within the batting too.

Previously when Curran was deployed in such a position back in 2023, it was because he was the best of a bad bunch of options on a tour of Bangladesh spurned by players focusing on franchise gigs.

Here, his left-handedness broke up a middle-order bank of right-handers. Technically, he is also one of England’s best strikers of spin. Not that you could tell on a day when everyone flunked against it.

Sports.title: 'Boring' training sessions, four-hour meetings and annoying the owners: 'Crazy' Antonio Conte would be a 'DISASTER' at Man United, claims Ashley Young
Sports.content:
Ashley Young has claimed Antonio Conte would be a 'disaster' managing Manchester United - after the Italian revealed his desire to manage a fallen giant.

Conte, 57, is out of work after leaving Napoli at the end of last season following a two-year stint where he won Serie A and the Italian Super Cup.

Michael Carrick is still in post at Old Trafford and there are no immediate suggestions of that changing, but their struggles so far this season have raised alarm.

Young played under Conte at Inter Milan, where they won a Serie A title together, and says that Manchester United's players would be unhappy with his love for running and lengthy meetings - even if he is grateful personally to the Italian.

United's lack of running in matches this season has left them exposed and led to Gary Neville branding them an 'absolute disgrace'.

And Young told the Overlap Daily show: 'A lot of talk has been about Man United’s running stats. If they’re not going to run and Antonio Conte goes in there, it’s going to be a disaster, I think.

Antonio Conte would be a 'disaster' at Manchester United, Ashley Young has claimed

Young says Man United's players would not appreciate the level of running and long meetings

'He is throwing his name in the hat. Whether that is something that’s going to happen or not, I’m not sure whether the Man United players will be happy. I think you saw that when he went to Tottenham Hotspur.

'Speaking to a lot of Tottenham players – and I had spoken to Chelsea players before I went to Inter Milan and was like, "So what’s he like?" And they were like, "You’re gonna run a lot, you’ll be fitter than you’ve ever been."

'But do you know what? That was one of the things where I think that I was able to continue my career for so long because of the running, although it was crazy.

'The training sessions were a lot of 11 v 11, at times a little bit boring. Meetings were long. When I say long, I’m talking, if we lost the game, we could go in and do the meeting after the game and it’d stop literally everything.

'And you could be in there for three, four hours. I think that’s one of the reasons why he doesn’t last long at places, because not just the players – he tries to test mentally – but the board as well, and the owners, and I think that people get annoyed with him.'

Conte has a dazzling CV, having won league titles at Chelsea, Juventus, and Inter, but he is also known for his combustibility and not lasting long in jobs.

His longest gig was with Juventus between 2011 and 2014 but he is often too honest with people to retain relationships.

He was sacked by Tottenham in 2023 after a savage 10-minute rant where he branded them selfish, accused them of lacking 'fire in the eyes', and admitted the collective spirit had regressed.

Young played under Conte at Inter Milan and they won a Serie A title together in 2020-21

'They don't play for something important. They don't want to play under pressure. They don't want to play under stress. It is easy in this way. Tottenham's story is this,' he said.

'Until now, I try to hide the situation but there are 10 games to go and some people think we can fight. Fight for what? With this spirit, this attitude, this commitment? What? For seventh, eighth, 10th place?'

Conte's name is being mentioned around United after he did an interview with The Athletic earlier this month and told them of his ambition to restore a fallen giant.

He has been linked with the managerial role at Manchester United in the past and told The Athletic: 'If you go to a club where the history speaks for itself - a history made up of trophies, league titles and victories - you can only honour that history in one way: by having the ambition to bring that club back, if it isn't there today, to fight for those goals.

'I know full well that only one team can win every year, but I must carry in my heart, and instil in the hearts of the fans, my players and my directors, that spark, that hope that makes you say, "f***, we can win". You only make history by winning.

'There are many clubs that have somewhat lost sight of their history. I'd like to go to one of these clubs to dust off that history and make it shine once more.

'Clubs where there's pressure, where, ultimately, you know full well that you're not going there just to take part, but to compete.'

United continue to endure a tough period, with the club having not won the Premier League title since Sir Alex Ferguson's last season in 2012-13.

In the subsequent 13 years, United's only trophies have been the FA Cup (in 2016 and 2024), the EFL Cup (in 2017 and 2023), and the Europa League (in 2017), and they have rarely threatened to challenge for the biggest titles.

There does not appear to be much chance of that this season, with the Red Devils sat 13th in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Dejan Kulusevski thanks Tottenham fans as star completes 'impossible journey' after 526-day absence with serious knee injury... and admits he told loved ones 'it might not work out' just two months ago
Sports.content:
Dejan Kulusevski completed his ‘impossible’ and ‘beautiful’ journey back to the Premier League and promised to repay Tottenham fans for their support in the difficult times. Kulusevski returned as an 87th-minute substitute on Monday. It was his first appearance since a serious knee injury in May 2025 and coincided with an upturn in fortunes for Spurs. Roberto De Zerbi’s strugglers beat Coventry 3-1 to secure their first league win of the season at the seventh attempt and climbed off the bottom of the table. James Maddison’s first goal for almost 18 months after his own injury nightmare and Kulusevski’s long-awaited return served to fuel the celebrations. 'The journey felt impossible,' said Kulusevski, 26. 'It was the most difficult it could be, but I had a feeling I was going to come back to play football. I just had to believe and that is what I do. 'I had to tell my closest ones it might not work out, just a couple of months ago. But in my heart, I always knew it would work out. I kept working. For 10 hours every day when no one is watching. Dejan Kulusevski has vowed to repay Tottenham fans support after making his first appearance in 526 days after a serious knee injury Kulusevski admitted the injury, sustained in May 2025 against Crystal Palace, led to him telling his loved ones a couple of months ago that his return might not work out 'Imagine when everyone gives up on you. And football for me is like breathing. Imagine you can’t breathe for two years but still you have a family, so you show up, you do it with a smile, you go with your team-mates, you hype them up and that takes a lot of love, a lot of courage and a lot of belief. That is what I had to practise. 'So, when everything was impossible and everyone gave up, I never gave up.' Kulusevski damaged a kneecap in a game against Crystal Palace. He had surgery but found he was still in pain and discomfort when he returned to training seven months later. There followed a course of injections and further rest and when that did not solve the problem he underwent another operation in March. It has been a long and difficult road with dire warnings about the delicate nature of the injury, and the popular Swede told how his Christian faith helped him through darker parts of his recovery. 'God, he gives me all the power,' said Kulusevski. 'I can’t take credit for what I’ve done because I haven’t done it alone. Every day he has been doing it for me. 'I will tell everyone about the journey. It has been an amazing journey even if it was hard sometimes. Hard is beautiful and I am so grateful that I had to experience it. 'Now I am ready to play football. I see myself a little different now. I think I am a different man now. Same guy, same guy that wants to play football but a little bit smarter.' Tottenham fans gave Kulusevski a rapturous ovation when he came on in the closing stages of their 3-1 victory over Coventry Spurs fans gave him a rapturous ovation as he peeled off his tracksuit to replace Mohamed Kudus. 'I am so grateful that they miss me play,' said Kulusevski. 'It means a lot and I am here to show them a better me. And a better me will be a better Spurs so we will be good.' He played in an internal practice match at the Tottenham training centre at the start of October and travelled with the squad but didn’t make the bench for the first game after the international break at Manchester United. By the time of the Coventry game, he was straining at the leash to get back on the pitch. 'I was more emotional in the morning,' said Kulusevski. 'I wasn’t nervous. I was ready to play those 10 minutes and make a good impact. It was amazing. It was fun. A beautiful day and I’m so happy we won.'

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Huge points deduction leaked as EFL 'ready to agree' punishment
Sports.content:
A statement from the Premier League at the end of September read: "An independent Commission has found Manchester City FC guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League’s investigation.

"The independent Commission found that between Seasons 2009/10 and 2017/18: - Manchester City arranged ‘sham’ contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on ‘sham’ agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club’s revenues and reduce its costs - The club filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators - Manchester City was significantly in breach of both the Premier League’s and UEFA’s spending limits - During the Premier League’s investigation, Manchester City committed multiple breaches of its duties of co-operation and utmost good faith towards the League (three of the four alleged breaches were upheld)

"The independent Commission found that Manchester City arranged ‘sham’ commercial deals with a number of its sponsors during the period, which were part of a disguised funding scheme, whereby those companies were only required to pay a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees. The remainder was funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club. As part of the scheme, further ‘sham’ arrangements, funded by ADUG, were entered into to enable the club to record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred, as well as a ‘sham’ circular arrangement with Fordham, an entity that purchased the club’s players’ image rights, that was funded by ADUG.

"The purpose of these schemes was found to have been to artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than £900 million during the affected period, to appear to comply with financial rules. The consequence of this, as the Commission found, was that the club filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators. The Commission concluded that ‘by its conduct the club clearly intended to circumvent the PL Rules‘.

"As a result, Manchester City failed to accurately report its income and expenditure for the purposes of the Premier League’s Profitability and Sustainability Rules and UEFA’s Club Licensing and Financial Fair Play Rules. The Commission found that, had all of the relevant agreements been reported accurately in the club’s accounts, it would have been in breach of both the League’s and UEFA’s spending limits by a very substantial amount.

"In addition, during the course of the four-year investigation conducted by the Premier League, the club committed multiple breaches of its duties of co-operation and utmost good faith towards the League. The Commission concluded that the club had ‘made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the PL investigation’."

City continue to insist they are innocent.

Sports.title: PSG earn statement Barcelona win as Phil Foden continues hot streak for Man City
Sports.content:
PSG earn statement Barcelona win as Phil Foden continues hot streak for Man City

CHAMPIONS LEAGUE ROUND-UP: There was a six-goal thriller in Paris as the holders faced Barcelona, as the Champions League delivered on a mouth-watering set of fixtures

View 3 Images Paris Saint-Germain are still on top (Image: Mustafa Yalcin/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Paris Saint-Germain showed once again why they're the kings in Europe by beating in-form Barcelona 4-2 in a back-and-forth bout. There were also high-scoring wins for Manchester City and Liverpool - but in vastly different circumstances.

‌



‌



Topping the bill was the clash in Paris, and it was the hosts who took the lead first when Desire Doue capitalised on a mistake from Lamine Yamal and curled in a sumptuous finish. Barcelona nearly hit back through Fermin Lopez, who'd replaced the injured Dani Olmo in the first half, but he was denied by a combination of Matvei Safonov and Willian Pacho.

‌



Barca didn't take long to level things, though. 10 minutes into the second half, 19-year-old Xavi Espart driving down the right and beating Safonov for power just after Achraf Hakimi had missed a golden opportunity. But for all the technical quality on the pitch, it was a set piece that decided the game.

‌



After Ferran Torres missed a chance from close range against his former club, Lucas Hernandez powered home a header from the resulting corner. But Yamal still had something to say.

‌



Minutes after Warren Zaire-Emery entered the fray and was tasked with dealing with him, the Barcelona superstar blazed past the PSG substitute and prodded the ball past Safonov at his near post. Zaire-Emery's misery would then turn to relief only two minutes later when Vintinha hit an audacious effort from the edge of Barca's box, and the ball nestled into the back of the net past the sprawling Joan Garcia.

After Fabian Ruiz's clincher, it was another statement win for the holders but also highlighted their imperfections. PSG's night was blotted by an injuries to three of their best players - Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

‌



At the Etihad, City took an early lead against AEK Athens through Elliot Anderson, who had a tap-in after Enzo Fernandez's free-kick hit the crossbar. Enzo Maresca's side doubled their lead when Phil Foden played a neat one-two with Rico Lewis and fired home.

AEK threatened a comeback shortly after the break when Stavros Pilios scored, but Cherki made it 3-1 just five minutes later. It then turned into the Foden show, as the City star grabbed a hat-trick in a 5-1 battering.

‌



Who'll win the Champions League? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 3 Images Phil Foden grabbed a hat-trick as Manchester City won 5-1 (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



It was less straightforward for Liverpool, who came from 2-0 down to beat Villarreal. An error from Virgil van Dijk allowed the La Liga side to go in front with four minutes on the clock before Sergi Cardona quickly made it two.

But a brace from Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo's header flipped the game on its head. Florian Wirtz then grabbed a much-needed goal to make it 4-2 before a consolation effort from the visitors. It ended 4-3, as Liverpool followed PSG by making it three wins from three games in the Champions League.

‌



In the early kick-offs, Borussia Dortmund survived a scare to claim a 2-1 win away to Sabah. Fenerbahce, meanwhile, failed to convert their fast start and threw away a two-goal lead against Slavia Prague, who picked up their first point of the campaign as the league table starts to take shape.

Later on, Napoli and Bodo/Glimt played out a seven-goal thriller, with the Italians coming out on top to win 4-3. Roma were also big winners against Slovan Bratislava, hammering them 4-0.

‌



PSV also snatched a narrow 1-0 victory at Porto thanks to Guus Til's goal. And in Germany, the points were shared as Stuttgart drew 1-1 with Atletico Madrid, who played the final half-hour with 10 men.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick confirms message from Man Utd board and responds to 'toxic' Erik ten Hag claim
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick confirms message from Man Utd board and responds to 'toxic' Erik ten Hag claim

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick was asked whether he has received backing from the club's board amid his side's winless run, as he prepares to face Como in the Champions League

View Image Michael Carrick believes that he has the backing of Manchester United's board (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick believes he has the backing of Manchester United's board and has no concerns over Erik ten Hag's claims that the hierarchy is 'toxic'.

‌



‌



Former United head coach Ten Hag made the assertion after revealing that the club had broken promises of loyalty to him at the end of his tenure. The Dutchman was sacked in October 2024, just a few months after being awarded a new contract.

‌



Carrick earned a permanent deal at the end of last term, having guided the club to Champions League football, but has failed to hit the same heights since. The Red Devils are winless in their last six matches heading into the game against Como.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Speculation has started over the security of Carrick's position after the club recorded their worst top-flight start for 40 years. The United boss was asked if Ten Hag's experience had raised any red flags for him, but the ex-midfielder could only praise the environment he is currently working in.

"Not for me," he said. "That's Erik's opinion. I don't know the details or ins and outs of that. It's wrong o me to comment or get involved because it was nothing to do with me at that stage.

‌



"As a football club, the way we're working, behind the scenes and away from it, results dictate a lot of the feeling and a lot of the energy and the positivity or the not-so-positive around the place. Within our walls as a group and a team, we're pretty composed but driven. We're pretty stable, we've got to think calmly, we've got to keep our emotions and direct them in the right way.

‌



"Certain conversations that we have that we're really clear with as a football club, with Jason [Wilcox], with Omar [Berrada], with the owners and down to the players. It's really important we pull in the same direction and there's a real balance between that fire and desire to make things happen but you've got to do it from a platform of stability and having a clear plan.

Ultimately, the 45-year-old admitted it simply boils down to winning. Asked if he'd received backing, Carrick offered a stern response.

‌



"I don't need any reassurance," he said. It's pretty clear. I know the role. I know the responsibilities. I don't need anyone else to tell me that or when it's going well or needs to be better. I know that myself, I know the realities. I've got no problem with that.

"There's not much I can elaborate on that. We've got to win football games for everything to flow and fit into place. That's the great thing, we can do something about it."

"Yeah, why wouldn't I? [feel backed] I'm in this position, I have a really good relationship with everyone at the football club," he added. "There's really no issues and no problems with that side. We've got to win games of football and that's what we're striving to do."

Sports.title: Man Utd set to admit Lisandro Martinez was right as chiefs draw up transfer plan
Sports.content:
Man Utd set to admit Lisandro Martinez was right as chiefs draw up transfer plan

Lisandro Martinez was fined after slamming Manchester United's hierarchy for not making enough signings in the summer transfer window, but the club appear to have accepted that he was right

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez wanted Michael Carrick to be given a stronger squad (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

Manchester United plan to address their issues in defence next summer - and have added Bournemouth left-back Adrien Truffert to their list of targets. United have conceded a concerning 15 goals in their first seven games of the season and manager Michael Carrick has been dealt several injury blows in his backline.

‌



‌



As a consequence, club chiefs such as director of football Jason Wilcox have come under fire for not signing a defender in the summer transfer window. Lisandro Martinez poured fuel on the flames last week when he accused United of not doing enough to bolster Carrick's squad on their return to the Champions League.

‌



His decision to heavily criticise his employers - including calling out Wilcox - divided pundits and supporters, with some arguing that the Argentine shouldn't have spoken out. Most agreed, however, that his comments had merit.

‌



United's failure to sign a left-back has been exposed two months into the new season, with an injury to Luke Shaw forcing Ayden Heaven and Diogo Dalot to play out of position. Shaw is notably one of the eight players who are set to miss Wednesday's trip to Como.

The i Paper report that senior figures at Old Trafford recognise they should've addressed their defence in the summer. United were keen on signing Newcastle left-back Lewis Hall, but the England international proved to be out of their price range.

That's why Truffert, 24, is now on the Red Devils' shortlist, with United said to be long-time admirers of the Frenchman. Truffert is enjoying his second season at Bournemouth after the Cherries paid Rennes £14.4m to sign him in June 2025.

‌



Centre-back is also a position which United will focus on, with Martinez and Harry Maguire in their final year of their deals. The report states that they'll sign at least one central defender and could target a second if Martinez leaves amid interest from Atletico Madrid.

Who should Manchester United sign? Let us know your picks in the comments section.

De Ligt's first start since last October could come against Como, with Daniel Armer the only other recognised centre-back spotted in training before United flew to Italy on Tuesday.

Sports.title: Newcastle's major Mikel Arteta offer failed months before Arsenal appointment
Sports.content:
Newcastle's major Mikel Arteta offer failed months before Arsenal appointment

Newcastle made a play to hire current Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta as their new manager back in 2019, with owner Mikel Ashley prepared to back him with a rarely seen contract

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta was offered a long-term deal to lead Newcastle, even though he'd never held a top job before

Newcastle almost landed Mikel Arteta in the summer of 2019 - months before he joined Arsenal - with the Spaniard tempted by the role.

‌



‌



The Magpies had just seen Rafa Benitez depart, which greatly angered fans given his popularity at St James' Park, and Ashley was keen to give Arteta a lengthy deal that showcased his desire to have him on board.

‌



The Newcastle boss was willing to hand out the type of contract that is not normal for a rookie coach, given Arteta's only managerial experience was as a No.2 at Manchester City.

‌



He was genuinely tempted, reports the Telegraph, and made moves to assemble a backroom staff to aid him in the north east. Having never worked as a No.1 he didn't have previous assistants to fall back on, and those he wanted were unable to join him at the time, leading him to turn down the role.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Newcastle had finished a modest 13th in Benitez's final year and would've, in theory, provided Arteta with the ideal start to his life as a manager. The situation at St James' Park was tense given Benitez's popularity and Ashley's immense unpopularity among the fanbase.

The Magpies had also seen Ayoze Perez and Salomon Rondon leave after the duo had combined to score 23 of the 42 goals that Newcastle scored in previous campaign. They would instead hire Steve Bruce after Arteta's rejection, finishing 13th once again.

‌



Arteta has ultimately proved himself to be among Europe's top managers, ending Arsenal's wait for a Premier League title, but in the years after he was appointed he endured some notable frustration at the hands of Newcastle.

View 2 Images Mike Ashley was determined to hire Mikel Arteta when he was still at Manchester City (Image: NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



The 2021-22 campaign was the first in the Arteta era during which Arsenal were clearly competitive, and they recovered from a horror start to challenge for the top four. They had their destiny in their own hands in the final weeks but lost at a resurgent Newcastle in the penultimate game of the season, which saw Tottenham pip them.

In 2025, when Arteta was being mocked for his inability to get over the line, Arsenal were favourites to make the final of the Carabao Cup, but fluffed their lines against Newcastle. Eddie Howe's side would win both games 2-0, securing a 4-0 aggregate win.

Sports.title: Real Madrid tell Premier League 'Big Six' to pay for European Super League costs
Sports.content:
Real Madrid tell Premier League 'Big Six' to pay for European Super League costs

Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham were among the 12 clubs that agreed to be part of the European Super League in April 2021 before they quickly pulled out

View 2 Images All six Premier League clubs withdrew from the project amid intense backlash (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

Real Madrid are reportedly demanding that the six English clubs that signed up to the European Super League (ESL) pay a share of the project's initial costs, despite its premature collapse. Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham were among the 12 clubs involved in the ESL before it was abandoned following widespread condemnation.

‌



‌



In April 2021, the so-called Big Six of the Premier League initially signed up to a shareholders' agreement for the Spain-based European Super League Company. After five other clubs - Atletico Madrid, AC Milan, Inter Milan, Juventus and Barcelona - pulled out in the years since, Real remain the only side who are still committed to the much-maligned project.

‌



The Athletic report that chiefs at the Bernabeu believe Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, City, United and Spurs should be liable for the setup costs of the plan. Those costs could be as high as €80million (£67.3m) in total.

‌



At the time of the project's demise, Real president Florentino Perez commented: "I'm not going to take my time to explain what a binding contract is here. But the fact is, the clubs can't leave."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



News of Real's demand comes as the La Liga giants close in on appointing Bernd Reichart as their new head of business operations. Reichart, a German businessman, was formerly the CEO of A22, the management company based in Madrid working on behalf of the ESL.

In December 2023, when only Barcelona and Real were left in the project after Juventus had decided to withdraw earlier that year, A22 announced a change to how the competition would work. It was explained that 64 clubs would compete across three divisions, with relegation and promotion possible and the potential for new clubs to qualify for the league, rather than a closed shop.

‌



There was another change of plan 12 months later. This time, the ESL would be comprised of 96 teams and four divisions, and was branded the 'Unify League'.

Should clubs have been punished for joining the European Super League? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Florentino Perez still believes that in the European Super League's future (Image: Dennis Agyeman/AFP7 via Getty Images)

Barcelona formally pulled out of the ESL in February of this year, four months after Perez insisted that he was convinced it'd come to fruition.

‌



"We have had our right to create our own competitions recognised," Real's president stated. "We can also claim multimillion euro damages for UEFA's conduct.

"We have two rights: to be compensated for our losses, and to arrange a competition in the future, and we will tirelessly pursue both."

Sports.title: Man City's Champions League wildcard with UEFA battle serving as Premier League warning
Sports.content:
Manchester City can get away from the outside noise, for one night at least, when they take on AEK Athens on Tuesday, looking to put last week's hammering against Paris Saint-Germain behind them.

Every time they take to the pitch in the Premier League, their results - which this season have been only wins - are caveated by the idea that this could all be rendered redundant by a serious punishment. Yes, Enzo Maresca's side have been flawless domestically, winning seven from seven, but this could all come crashing down with a mega points deduction once their appeal has ran its course and the Premier League can react to their guilty verdict.

However, while their misdemeanours have threatened to undermine England's top flight, their perception on the European stage is less tainted. And there is a world whereby City are playing in the Championship next season and also participating in the Champions League itself - which certain rivals are fearful of.

Right now, despite the anger and frustration surrounding City in England, should they conquer Europe then there is no precedented for denying a team a spot in the following season's Champions League if they qualify on sporting merit.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

The major issue surrounds the UEFA licence, which every club needs in order to play in Europe. They are handed out by the Football Association and are based upon information which does not take into account sanctions or breaches related to historical offences. If a club fulfils all minimum criteria required for admission, which City would, the licence cannot be refused.

Even then, City continue to bang the 'we're not guilty' drum. Last week's European outing, which didn't go to plan, was their latest show of defiance, at least off the pitch. Pep Guardiola and his former assistant were back and sat amongst chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak, chief executive Ferran Soriano and sporting director Hugo Viana.

‌



"I think they are convinced that in the end we will win the appeal," claimed City boss Maresca, who also said: "The reason why I joined this club is I completely trust 100 per cent, the owner, the sporting director, the CEO - all the organisation. I have no doubt about that."

View 3 Images Manchester City's hierarchy have remained defiant and maintain their innocence

City have developed a siege mentality but had to cop it from rival fans. It was written in the stars that their first game after being found guilty would be at Liverpool, where banners were held up calling them cheats.

There's plenty of debate over City's guilty period and the residual affect of that. Would Erling Haaland have joined a team that hadn't won the Premier League? Because that may well have been City had they not overlooked the rules to achieve that what they did from 2009 to 2018.

‌



Ultimately, no member of City's current squad was signed during the period in which an independent commission found the club guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

The David Silvas, the Sergio Agueros and the Kevin De Bruynes are all gone. So those at the Etihad now have all been signed, in essence, fairly. And yet their successes, which includes only the second treble in English football history, are being questioned by those outside the club.

View 3 Images Ruben Dias is the club's longest-serving signing - and joined after their guilty period (Image: Matt McNulty, Getty Images)

Their longest-serving first-team player who was purchased from another club (so not Phil Foden) is club captain Ruben Dias. He joined from Benfica in 2020.

‌



He remains the team's defensive leader, and he's come out with a clear show of defiance, proclaiming: “I really feel like I speak for the whole group; we trust the club."

The Portugal centre-half also said: “If there’s more or less noise or whatever the reason the noise is, at the end of the day it’s all the same, same as before, because people don’t love us winning and we love to win.”

Well they've made a habit of that, bar their PSG hammering, which even then could've ended so different had a wasteful City been more clinical in the second-half. The first-half from the Parisians did blow the home side away, showcasing the standard in Europe right now, but will City will relish trying to chase them down, starting tonight against the Greek side.

‌



Those on the blue half of Manchester know full well how it feels to get hit with a major punishment but win on appeal. They took on UEFA after they were expelled from European competitions back in 2020, having it overturned at the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

Now they're taking on the Premier League, another juggernaut in the footballing world. But time will determine whether the City hierarchy's defiance is in fact arrogance, believing they have enough clout on and off the pitch to win this battle as well.

Sports.title: Ex-Man Utd star makes Michael Carrick U-turn and names ideal Old Trafford replacement
Sports.content:
Ex-Man Utd star makes Michael Carrick U-turn and names ideal Old Trafford replacement

Manchester United boss Michael Carrick is a man under the cosh and Dwight Yorke, who had backed the ex-player, believes giving him the Old Trafford job may have been the wrong call

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is a man under pressure with one win in seven games to start the Premier League season (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Former Manchester United star Dwight Yorke admits he will "hold his hands up" and concede that appointing Michael Carrick perhaps wasn't the right call - despite backing him initially.

‌



‌



The ex-Middlesbrough boss came in to steady the ship in January and enjoyed a stunning interim period, which saw United rise up to third place in the Premier League and return to the Champions League. Those exploits landed him the job on a permanent basis.

‌



However, he's found things much tougher this season and Carrick has now presided over the worst start in 40 years with United winning one of their seven league games thus far and being dumped out of the Carabao Cup.

‌



The pressure is very much on the United boss, who had the backing of several former players last season. United's desire to stick by a manager is clear following several poor calls by the hierarchy, but Yorke is no longer convinced he's the man for the job.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



He told Keys & Gray Unleashed: "That (sacking managers) is the current trend, isn’t it? It’s been the trend for the last five years: you get the manager, you say you’re going to back them and then at some point you end up getting rid of them,’ the former Trinidad and Tobago international went on. Obviously that is something that’s been in the DNA certainly for the past five years.

"Putting my hands up, I was one that said give Carrick the chance, but then I look back at it now, see what we’re doing, and I’m not sure if that was the right decision."

‌



"These guys are brilliant guys when you meet them and you know them like I have done. They’re brilliant. I’m not sure they’re made for managerial jobs when the pressure is on. Like anything else, when the going is good then it’s fantastic. When it’s not so good, I’m not so sure. I’ve seen it with Ole [Gunnar Solskjaer] and I’ve seen it with Carrick."

View 2 Images Dwight Yorke is no longer convinced by Michael Carrick (Image: Matthew Peters/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



United have tried several different types of managers over the past decade. They've gone after proven big names, up and coming talents and ex-players - none of whom have worked out.

Antonio Conte is being linked with the job but Yorke admits he's consider going after Eddie Howe, who left Newcastle in the summer after several successful years.

Article continues below

He said: "Who is out there? Howe would be one of those guys who stand out out there at the moment. He’s not in a job, looking for a job. But if you expand it out there even more, who else is out there? There is nobody else and that’s why Carrick will survive for a little bit longer. There are no top managerial candidates out there who can come in and really excite the people and the fans at Manchester United."
