Sports.title: Featured Comment: Budget cap not to blame for lack of winning teams in F1 | Brief
Sports.content:
This week’s poll asks whether Formula 1 needs to rethink its budget cap as the series’ top four team have pulled further away from their rivals this year.

But reader @Skydiverian suggests it might not be realistic to expect F1 to regularly have more than four race-winning teams:

Four competitive teams has happened before but it’s still not great and the problem is as it always is, money. And I’d like to see more teams in a season have a realistic shot of winning races. It’s unfortunate that the stats are not on my side.

Pretty much since the late 80s the problem has been that the best teams could throw more money at the problem to fix it. Now, teams that are significantly behind can’t throw more money at the problem to catch-up due to the cost cap, rather than simply not having the money in the first place as was common in the 80s. (This season is interesting. It seems that Mercedes blew most of it’s cap early to get and maintain their advantage, whereas Red Bull didn’t and that’s in part why Max has had a better car the last two races. But it’s not like Williams or Aston Martin can fix their problems by spending more money to fix the deficit).

The problem is that ultimately there’s no easy fix, but spending millions to be the so-called best of the rest basically seems pointless if there is a very unlikely chance of a team outside of the top four having a realistic shot at the podium or even a win. And that’s always been a problem going back decades.

Some number crunching by looking at the history books: the 500th race was 1990 Australia, 1,100th being Vegas 2023. In those 600 races I’ve found six that were won by drivers driving for teams who finished outside the top four in the constructors championship.

That’s six of 600 races over 33 years where we had a winner driving for a team who finished outside the top 4 in that years constructors championship, 1% of all races. Seven if you count Johnny Herbert’s win at the Nurburgring which to me was a genuine surprise at the time. To me those stats aren’t good enough.

Whether that’s the fault of teams with no money, teams with too much money or teams with a cash limit so they can’t design their way out is up for debate. But my point is that I’d like to see more teams have a reasonable chance of winning. F1 has never really had that and will continue not to unless something changes (maybe by letting teams further down have a bigger budget the following season rather than just more CFD time).

I’d rather that at least 70% of drivers have a realistic chance of winning, ideally 100% of teams. It’s the reason I preferred IndyCar before Alex Palou showed up, results were unpredictable and smaller teams have a chance of getting a win or two. That’s just so rare in F1 and the current cost cap rules will continue to make unlikely.

@Skydiverian

Sports.title: Early coronation for Antonelli? Five talking points for the United States Grand Prix | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli could win the world championship this weekend in only his second year as a Formula 1 driver. Here are the talking points for the United States Grand Prix.

Will Antonelli clinch the title?

The odds are stacked heavily in favour of Mercedes’ new star clinching the title at some point, but most likely not this weekend. That said it is not beyond the realm of possibility team mate George Russell could have another poor weekend and come away point-less while Antonelli takes his ninth victory of the season, putting him over the line.

The title has been won at this track twice before, and both times it was by a Mercedes druver: Lewis Hamilton won the championship there in 2015 and 2019. But regardless of whether Antonelli does clinch the title this weekend it is clearly a matter of ‘when’ not ‘if’.

Verstappen dominating again?

The driver most likely to delay Antonelli’s championship celebrations is not his team mate but Max Verstappen. Red Bull have made a breakthrough with their RB22 and as well as winning the last two grands prix plus a sprint race, Verstappen could have taken victory in Baku as well with better luck.

He arrives at this weekend’s race looking like the driver to beat, with every indication he could dominate the final rounds of the season, setting himself up for a shot at the title next year.

McLaren’s driver headache

McLaren arrive in Austin in a curiously similar situation to last year: a clash between their drivers at the previous race in Singapore has created an obvious tension. What’s more, Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri’s collision during the sprint race in Singapore was more costly than the one they had in the grand prix 12 months ago.

Norris’s radio messages during the grand prix gave the distinction impression he was looking for ways to make amends, having eventually accepted he was the one at fault for their collision. But above all the team will be anxious to avoid a repeat of the first-corner collision which wrecked their sprint race at the circuit 12 months ago. Particularly as a resurgent Red Bull are poised to relegate the reigning constructors’ champions to fourth place in the standings.

US teams’ driver decisions

Of the two teams competing in their home event this weekend, one has settled its driver plans for 2027. Haas has announced Rafael Camara as the replacement for Esteban Ocon, whose Formula 1 future is in serious doubt as few likely alternatives remain for next year.

Could Cadillac be one of them? F1’s new American team is yet to confirm its plans for next year. However its hopes IndyCar star Colton Herta would take Formula 2 by storm and make himself an obvious candidate for promotion have been dashed: he lies 19th in the standings, 181 points behind fellow rookie and championship leader Camara.

Are Colapinto’s die-hards paying attention?

Last week Franco Colapinto spoke out in criticism of the element of his fanbase which has sent vile abuse to his rival drivers, team members and FIA officials since he made his F1 debut this year. The Alpine driver told those attacking others in his name that they are not helping his cause in F1.

Will they take his words on board? We’ll get an indication the next time he is involved in any kind of incident on-track – however slight it may be.

Sports.title: On This Day: Ralf Schumacher wins Formula Nippon title despite spinning out | Brief
Sports.content:
30 years ago today Ralf Schumacher won the Formula Nippon title despite retiring two laps into a rain-lashed race.

Schumacher arrived at the final race at Fuji Speedway just two points ahead of team mate Naoki Hattori. But Schumacher spun out two laps into the rain-hit race (see 3’50 in the video below).

That left Hattori on course for the title, which looked increasingly secure as the laps ticked down. But conditions worsened, and seven laps from home he spun out too, handing Schumacher the 1996 title. Schumacher made his F1 debut the following year for Jordan (now Aston Martin).

Katsutomo Kaneishi won ahead of future Formula 1 driver Pedro de la Rosa. Another future F1 driver, Shinji Nakano, took fourth place behind Masahiko Kageyama. Just seven of the 26 starters were running at the finish.

Sports.title: David Haye Urges Fabio Wardley To Take Year Off
Sports.content:
David Haye thinks Fabio Wardley needs to step away from the ring for an entire year to rebuild his mechanics from the ground up following another brutal second-round TKO loss to Daniel Dubois.

While Haye still sees a path forward for Wardley, he doubts a standard eight-week training camp offers enough runway to fix the technical flaws Dubois repeatedly punished. His advice is simple: take an extended break to master the fundamental skills Wardley missed by turning pro without an amateur background.

“He should take a year out. But not a year out partying, holiday. No, just working on the basic fundamentals,” Haye said to talkSPORT Boxing about Wardley. “Go get a good Cuban coach, someone who just gets your legs right, gets your balance.”

Haye is assuming a lot if he thinks a year off in a Cuban school of boxing is going to rewire a 31-year-old brawler who learned his trade on the white-collar circuit. Fighters do not magically develop fluid footwork, ring IQ, and nuanced balance at this stage of life in an empty gym. Those instincts are drilled into kids through hundreds of amateur bouts between the ages of twelve and twenty.

If Wardley steps away for twelve months with millions already sitting in the bank, he will not return as Guillermo Rigondeaux. He will return as an older, heavier, rustier version of the exact same guy, minus whatever sharp edge kept him dangerous.

Taking a year off ignores human nature, especially for a fighter who just cashed massive checks. Inactivity dulls timing and slows reflexes, and when a fighter relies almost entirely on explosive athleticism and punching power, ring rust is lethal.

“In the heat of the battle, you do what you do,” Haye explained. “He hasn’t done the correct thing, enough reps.” “He could continue in this division, and we’ll have some great fights, but it’s not going to be good for his health.”

The blueprint to keep his career alive is obvious: step down levels immediately. Wardley needs active reps under the lights against beatable, mid-tier opposition. He needs guys who will test him for six to eight rounds without having the world-class power or technical precision of a Daniel Dubois or Joseph Parker to punish every fundamental mistake.

The punishment he absorbed across those three elite fights is the kind that takes chunks out of a fighter’s prime. Throwing him into gym purgatory will only make him think too much in the ring, and a hesitant brawler gets knocked out twice as fast.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Extends Matchroom Deal, Targets 2027 Unifications
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly is staying put. The IBF light middleweight champion just signed a multi-fight contract extension with Eddie Hearn and Matchroom Boxing, setting his sights directly on major unifications for 2027.

The deal keeps Kelly locked in with Matchroom following a breakout run where he claimed his first world championship and successfully defended it. While Matchroom announced no date or opponent alongside the new paperwork, Kelly made his intentions clear immediately.

“I’m World Champion, and I am very excited about the future with Matchroom Boxing,” Kelly said. “Now I only want the biggest fights in the division. Unifications. Bring it on.”

The 32-year-old slickster took the IBF belt via majority decision over Bakhram Murtazaliev at Newcastle’s Utilita Arena in January. He then traveled to Jeddah in July, handing Caoimhin Agyarko his first career defeat over twelve rounds.

Those victories completely transformed his negotiating leverage. Kelly enters future talks holding genuine hardware rather than petitioning as a challenger.

Matchroom must now translate that ambition into reality. Kelly wants fellow champions, though Hearn stopped short of naming specific targets for the stablemate.

“We are thrilled to extend Josh Kelly’s contract with Matchroom Boxing,” Hearn stated. “He is an elite operator and one of the pound-for-pound best the UK has to offer. It is no secret that we have some huge plans ahead for Josh in 2027, where he will be aiming to add more World Titles to his collection.”

Kelly’s signature footwork carried him to the top. Meeting another belt-holder will test if that slick style holds up while mounting enough offensive output to take rounds against elite champions.

Now sitting at 19-1-1 with nine knockouts under trainer Adam Booth, Kelly gave his promoter clear instructions for 2027: line up the champions and let him work.

Hearn is rolling the dice here, because putting Kelly in the ring with Jaron Ennis looks like a recipe for a demolition. If that unification gets made, Kelly is facing an elite-level talent.

Ennis operates on an entirely different level of spite, power, and switch-hitting precision. Kelly might have the flashy reflexes to look cute for two or three rounds, but once Ennis starts cutting off the ring, targeting the body, and applying sustained heat, Kelly’s habit of pulling straight back with his hands down will catch up to him fast.

The foundation holding up Kelly’s sudden championship status looks shaky at best. Squeaking past Agyarko in Jeddah exposed all his familiar flaws. He spent long stretches coasting on the back foot, surviving on safety-first potshots, and failing to stamp any real authority on an opponent who had never operated anywhere near world level.

Before that, taking the belt off Murtazaliev raised plenty of eyebrows. Murtazaliev was relentlessly pressing the action, landing the heavier, more damaging blows while Kelly relied on flashy flurries that largely caught gloves and air. Handing Kelly a majority decision on home soil in Newcastle felt like a gift, not a definitive changing of the guard.

Locking Kelly down to a multi-fight extension right now puts Matchroom in a vulnerable spot. If the grand plan for 2027 is throwing him in against Ennis in a unification, Kelly’s market value could disappear in a defeat.

Sports.title: Gareth Davies Believes Tyson Fury Will Fight Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury could face Daniel Dubois after Anthony Joshua, according to Gareth A. Davies, who believes Fury possesses the skills to neutralize the newly crowned WBO heavyweight champion.

Davies floated the possibility following Dubois’s second-round stoppage of Fabio Wardley. Although he now rates Dubois as the world’s best heavyweight, he still sees a route to victory for Fury through movement and ring intelligence.

“He’s got the skills to nullify Daniel Dubois, but he’s got to be at his very best,” Davies said to iFL TV. “He needs to be elusive, and he needs his movement, and I think that will be key in the fight. He’s certainly got the IQ to do it.”

Fury would give Dubois a different fight than Wardley did. His movement could force Dubois to keep turning and chasing him, making it harder to plant his feet and land his power shots.

Whether Fury can actually pull that off inside the ropes at this stage is a massive question mark.

Knowing the blueprint to mess with Dubois’ offense is one thing, but dragging those thirty-something legs through twelve rounds against a younger brawler constantly walking him down is another test entirely. Davies thinks a dominant win over Joshua might tempt Fury into stepping in with Dubois, though he floated it purely as speculation rather than a done deal.

“I can see the winner of Fury and Joshua, or either Fury and Joshua, fighting Daniel Dubois,” Davies said. “It’s probably because I want to see it.”

Davies also pointed to Dubois growing as a ring craftsman. He liked the composure Dubois showed while closing the show against Wardley, picking his spots without walking into incoming right-hand counters.

That added discipline makes life tough on Fury. Dubois wouldn’t have to outbox him minute by minute if relentless heat drains the gas tank and leaves Fury carrying concrete in his boots.

Gareth’s theory hinges entirely on Fury having the wheels to dictate where the action happens. If those legs are spent, keeping Dubois off his chest turns into a brutal fight.

Fury has shown zero real appetite to get anywhere near Daniel Dubois, and the reasons are obvious.

Dubois is in his physical prime, throws heavy artillery with both hands, and walks opponents down without blinking. For an aging Fury whose legs are not what they used to be, taking on a puncher like Dubois is high risk with little appeal.

Fury is looking for massive paydays against names that match his era, like Anthony Joshua, or manageable outings where he can control the terms without taking life-altering punishment. Getting cornered by Dubois, taking shots to the body, and being forced into a grueling trench battle simply does not fit Fury’s career plans at this point.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Faces WBA Appeal Rejection Over Catterall
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is convinced Teofimo Lopez will not wiggle out of facing Jack Catterall. Matchroom holds stack after stack of written promises from the WBA guaranteeing the mandatory order stands.

Teofimo’s camp wants an exception so they can chase a unification scrap with Ryan Garcia. Hearn is betting the WBA refuses to play along, forcing Teofimo to either step into the ring with Catterall or give up the welterweight crown.

“Teofimo has pushed back and said, ‘We don’t think we should have to fight Jack Catterall. We’d like to try and make another fight,’” Hearn told iFL TV. “Basically, the WBA are going to say no because we’ve had multiple dozens of assurances in writing through the resolution.”

The WBA ordered the fight on September 22, giving the sides until October 22 to negotiate. That deadline does not guarantee a ruling on Teofimo’s request that day. Failure to reach an agreement could lead to purse bids, depending on how the sanctioning body handles the pending petition.

Hearn claims Matchroom holds ironclad written guarantees from the WBA locking in the Catterall defense, leaving him convinced the sanctioning body will shut down Teofimo’s petition to steer elsewhere.

“Teofimo Lopez will have the decision to fight Jack Catterall or vacate the belt,” he said.

Hearn knows Teofimo would earn more fighting Ryan, but says that doesn’t give him a pass to skip Catterall.

“I get it. It’s not a fight that pays you as much money as Ryan Garcia, but it’s a good fight that pays you a lot of money,” Hearn said. “Do as champions should do and make the fight.”

Right now, Catterall sits on hold while Teofimo chases the bigger fight against Ryan. Enforcing the mandatory would give Catterall clarity, but it might not actually hand him the fight he wants. Teofimo can still chase the Ryan fight, but Hearn says he’ll have to give up his WBA belt to do it. He doesn’t expect the WBA to let him keep Catterall waiting.

If Teofimo vacates his WBA belt, fans will not call it a shrewd business maneuver, though. Many will call it a duck. It becomes Ryan defending his WBC title against a challenger who showed the boxing world he didn’t want to face a Catterall, who fights a lot like Shakur Stevenson.

For the Ryan Garcia bout, it knocks a massive dent in the promotional luster. More importantly, it destroys Teofimo’s bargaining power at the negotiation table. Without a belt, Teofimo loses any claim to parity. Ryan will dictate the purse split, the ring walks, the poster placement, and the rules of engagement. The moment Teofimo drops the title, the event gets downgraded.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Celebrates Shakur’s Zuffa Departure Without Addressing Cost
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn called Shakur Stevenson leaving Zuffa Boxing an outright embarrassment, but he skipped over the core financial question. How much money was Zuffa supposed to put up for the matchups Shakur demanded?

Hearn openly questioned how any promoter could lock down an elite talent, only to let him walk without staging a single fight.

“How can you sign your most high-profile fighter and then he leaves you without even fighting?” Hearn said to iFL TV about Shakur.

Optically, that hurts Zuffa. Still, it does not mean holding onto Shakur made sound business sense.

Reporter Sean Zittel reported that Shakur sought at least $15 million per outing, even for a bout against Rayo Valenzuela, with an even steeper price tag for Devin Haney. Those numbers matter when evaluating what ended this partnership.

Hearn praised Shakur for walking away, hinting he could join Haney over at DAZN.

“Of course we’re going to dine out on it, aren’t we? Because they would do the same thing,” Hearn admitted.

The real test is whether Matchroom can satisfy that reported price tag. If Shakur sticks to those demands, Hearn faces the exact math problem Zuffa chose to avoid.

Bringing up Conor Benn’s paydays misses the point. Benn commands a massive following across Britain. Shakur has not shown that kind of commercial pull in America. Pure ring skill does not automatically generate the ticket sales needed to justify a $15 million purse before covering the opponent’s guarantee or card production.

Zuffa letting him walk says plenty about where they drew the line. The promotion simply decided the cost outweighed the return. Until contract paperwork surfaces, neither party holds the full truth.

Hearn can celebrate a rival stumbling all he wants. Actually signing Shakur fight by fight takes serious cash. If that $15 million asking price stands, someone has to absorb that risk, and Hearn hasn’t explained how he plans to make the numbers work.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Claims He Can Dominate Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster insists he has Emanuel Navarrete completely figured out ahead of their October 24 unification bout in San Antonio. Foster plans to outclass him, take his belt, and force critics to treat him like an elite name at 130 pounds.

Foster claimed he could turn this into a one-sided blowout if he simply sticks to the outside and picks Navarrete apart.

“I believe not only that I can beat Navarrete, I believe that I can do it in a dominant fashion, a super dominant fashion,” Foster said to Bradley’s channel. “I can make it an easy night and just box his head off.”

At the same time, Foster called this matchup a nine out of ten in difficulty and admitted it represents the biggest threat of his career. Navarrete throws wild, looping bombs from angles nobody learns in the gym. Foster insists none of that will rattle him. He points to past rounds with Rey Vargas, Robson Conceicao, and Jon Fernandez as proof that he knows how to handle height, awkward attacks, and long-range pressure.

Navarrete brings chaos, not textbook mechanics. Surviving separate elements from past opponents does not guarantee Foster can absorb the non-stop pressure Navarrete brings from opening bell to the final seconds. Foster cannot afford to run and let rounds slip away on activity alone.

He claims he wants to dominate, yet talking about an easy night while hunting for a highlight reel finish creates immediate risk. If Foster gets trapped between cruising on points and trying to look spectacular, Navarrete will make him pay with relentless volume.

“I’m looking to come in to make a statement,” Foster said. “I’m coming in to put on a dominant performance, show the world who I really am.”

Trying to invent power and aggression at age 31 against Navarrete is playing with fire. If Foster wants to leave San Antonio with the belts, he has to accept who he is, ignore the crowd, use his legs, and be content with a disciplined, ugly points win. Anything else plays right into Navarrete’s hands.

Foster has his sights set on undisputed status before jumping up in weight. Talking about blowing through Navarrete is bold talk, but a flat decision win will not deliver the respect he expects. Foster made big promises, and on October 24, he has to back them up against a puncher who never stops coming forward.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Plans His Own Promotional Company
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is launching DB Promotions to guide his own career once his contract with Sampson Lewkowicz wraps up in December. Even with the change, he intends to keep working alongside PBC and his existing inner circle.

Benavidez revealed his upcoming December bout marks the end of his decade-long deal with Lewkowicz. He treated the decision as a natural progression, making sure to acknowledge the promoter who helped build him into an attraction.

“This is the last fight on my contract,” Benavidez said to Brian Custer. “You know, I’ve honored the contract. The contract has been 10 years.”

Benavidez spoke carefully about the shift, never downplaying Lewkowicz while making it clear he is ready for independence.

“Sampson, he’s did a wonderful job,” Benavidez said. “He’s one of the greatest promoters of all time. But, you know, it’s just my time to do my own thing.”

When questioned about the venture’s name, he confirmed it will be DB Promotions, serving as his primary promotional banner starting early next year.

Stepping out on his own gives him significant leverage over the business side of his fight nights. Still, key details like equity splits, bankrolling, and operational responsibilities remain unstated, meaning the precise financial upside is impossible to calculate right now.

Putting his name on the banner gives Benavidez a chance to pocket more of the promotional money. That’s an obvious reason to make the move. But he still wants Al Haymon and TGB running the show alongside him. Having his own company won’t make the television money his, and he’ll still need those partners to get fights funded and dates booked.

Benavidez also aims to look past his own headline slots, expressing interest in signing boxers who train alongside him and his father, Jose Benavidez Sr.

“There’s a lot of great fighters I could take under my wing and put them under the promotion company,” he remarked.

Signing prospects gives DB Promotions life after Benavidez hangs up the gloves, yet building an actual stable turns a fighter into a financier. The expenses add up quickly with club show site rentals, airfare, hotel blocks, and purse guarantees that rarely turn a dime. Promoting his own headlining dates is one thing, but bankrolling young talent is a financial drain that devours capital long before a prospect ever sniffs a television date.

The move could let Benavidez pocket more of the money from potential fights with Jai Opetaia, Artur Beterbiev or Oleksandr Usyk. But with Haymon and TGB still involved, putting DB Promotions on the banner hardly means he’s going it alone.

Sports.title: Lucas Bahdi Seeks Schofield Rematch Over Knockdown Calls
Sports.content:
Most Valuable Promotions has formally challenged Lucas Bahdi’s defeat against Floyd Schofield III, petitioning the WBA for an immediate rematch after claiming uncalled knockdowns cost their fighter the vacant lightweight world championship.

The promotional outfit submitted video footage alongside detailed documentation to the WBA following the October 10 clash in Chicago. MVP maintains that if the referee had correctly recognized and scored the disputed incidents, Bahdi would have emerged with a majority decision win instead of leaving the ring empty-handed.

Schofield took the vacant belt by unanimous decision, capturing wide margins on the official cards with scores of 116 to 110, 115 to 111, and a steep 119 to 108. Bahdi’s side now wants the sanctioning body to grant another title opportunity, arguing that multiple officiating blunders corrupted those final numbers.

“The video evidence demonstrates multiple significant officiating errors that directly impacted the outcome of the fight,” MVP said in its statement. “Our review shows that had these knockdowns been properly ruled and scored, Lucas would have won the WBA lightweight world championship by majority decision.”

That claim sounds bold on paper, yet MVP failed to provide the necessary receipts to back it up. The public release never identified which specific rounds contained the uncalled drops, nor did it offer an adjusted scorecard breakdown to illustrate how Bahdi overturned an eleven-point deficit on the widest card.

Rather than rehashing standard complaints about judges favoring the house fighter, MVP pinned the blame directly on the third man in the ring. The core of their protest argues that referee mistakes prevented the judges from scoring mandatory 10 to 8 rounds, skewing the overall totals.

“We have submitted our findings to the WBA and requested an immediate rematch,” MVP said.

Securing a second fight remains an uphill climb. A rematch forces Schofield to revisit an opponent he already officially conquered, and lodging a protest never guarantees the WBA will order the boxers back into the ring. The sanctioning body has not issued a ruling on the video review, leaving MVP’s victory claim as promotional posturing until officials deliver a verdict.

Ghana News.title: FGMSA sues Medical and Dental Council to halt Common Registration Examination
Ghana News.content:
The Federation of Ghana Medical Students’ Associations (FGMSA) and affected graduating medical and dental students have sued the Medical and Dental Council (MDC), seeking to restrain the regulator from conducting the Common Registration Examination (CRE).

In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, and signed by its National Executive Council, FGMSA said the case had been filed at the High Court’s Human Rights Division in Accra.

The applicants are seeking an injunction to prevent the examination from being conducted pending the determination of the substantive legal issues before the court.

The action follows unsuccessful attempts to resolve their concerns through engagement with the relevant authorities, according to the Federation.

“FGMSA remains committed to protecting the interests of medical and dental students and will pursue the legal process to its conclusion,” the statement said.

The Common Registration Examination is a new licensing examination introduced by the MDC for graduating medical and dental students.

Its implementation has drawn opposition from some students, who have raised concerns about the examination and its potential implications for their careers.

FGMSA said it had previously engaged the MDC and other relevant authorities in an effort to resolve the concerns, but those efforts did not produce an agreement, prompting the legal action.

The application seeks to prevent the MDC from proceeding with the examination while the court considers the issues raised by the applicants.

The specific legal arguments and reliefs sought beyond the injunction were not detailed in the statement.

The timing of the hearing and whether the court will grant the injunction were also not specified.

The case is therefore pending, and the court’s decision will determine whether the examination can proceed while the substantive legal challenge remains before it.

Ghana News.title: Doue impresses as PSG beat Barcelona in thriller
Ghana News.content:
Desire Doue, Lamine Yamal and Vitinha scored superb individual goals as Champions League holders Paris St-Germain overcame Barcelona in a breathless encounter at Parc des Princes.

After starring in PSG's victory against Manchester City last week, Doue opened the scoring in the 38th minute of a first half in which both sides missed several clear chances.

Teenage full-back Xavi Espart drew Barcelona level early in the second half with a rifled near-post effort, before PSG defender Lucas Hernandez powered in a towering header.

Lamine Yamal made it 2-2 with a genius near-post finish, but less than two minutes later Vitinha sent a volley into the bottom corner to reclaim the lead for PSG.

Fabian Ruiz put the result beyond doubt five minutes later by converting Achraf Hakimi's low cross at the back post, in a win that ends Barcelona's 11-match unbeaten run at the start of their season.

The Parisians had wasted little time in implementing their high-pressing gameplan to force Barcelona into several mistakes in the early stages.

The game was 79 seconds old when Khvicha Kvaratskhelia struck the foot of the post after Pedri was dispossessed, before Doue and Ousmane Dembele were denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia following high turnovers.

It was then Barcelona's turn to launch their own rapid attacks, but Raphinha could only fire straight at Matvey Safonov in the PSG goal after running on to a neat Anthony Gordon pass.

Garcia had a busy end to the half as he twice denied former Barcelona team-mate Ferran Torres - who replaced the injured Dembele - but the goalkeeper could do nothing about Doue's opener.

After PSG intercepted a Barca ball out from defence, Doue drove to the edge of the penalty area and rifled a low shot into the bottom left corner.

Minutes before half-time Fermin Lopez was thwarted in a one-on-one situation by Safonov, but 10 minutes into the second half Espart, 19, beat the Russian goalkeeper at his near post after bursting into the box.

Barcelona were starting to look the more likely side to claim a winner, but, moments after Torres hit the post following a quick counter, Hernandez planted a header past Garcia from a corner.

Out of nothing, Lamine Yamal then turned Warren Zaire-Emery, sprinted into the box and squeezed the ball in between Safonov and the post.

Just as the momentum looked to have swung in Barca's favour, Vitinha controlled a clearance with his chest before launching a stunning volley into the bottom corner, before Ruiz put the seal on an exhilarating match.

PSG have nine points and will next face Villarreal in Spain on Tuesday, 3 November (20:00 GMT).

Barcelona remain on six points and will host Aston Villa at Camp Nou at the same time.

Ghana News.title: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case amid concerns about continental spread
Ghana News.content:
Nigeria has confirmed its first Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who travelled from Uganda tested positive for the virus.

The case in the West African country comes amid an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and some cases in Kenya, raising concerns about a spread across the continent.

According to Nigeria’s Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the woman began showing symptoms on October 7 and was admitted to a private hospital in Abuja on October 11, before being diagnosed with Ebola.

Health Minister Muhammad Pate said authorities had begun trying to trace 44 people who came into contact with the patient.

“We are doing everything possible to contain this case by tracing all the contacts the individual may have had,” he said.

New case in Kenya

Earlier on Tuesday, Kenya confirmed ⁠its ninth case of Ebola.

A 24-year-old man, who was already being held in quarantine, is the latest to test positive, Kenya’s Ministry of Health said in a statement on Tuesday.

“He was isolated at the first sign of illness, tested and started on treatment immediately upon confirmation of his positive test result,” it said, adding he “was already in quarantine when he fell ill”.

The man was a close family member of Kenya’s first Ebola patient, who had travelled from the DRC, through Uganda and before arriving in Kenya and dying at a Nairobi hospital on ⁠October 5.

“All nine cases belong to one cluster, and as of ‌today there is no evidence of transmission outside this group,” Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth said in a statement on Tuesday.

“Eight patients are stable and responding well to treatment, while 134 of 135 contacts have been traced and quarantined,” Amoth said.

Amoth said a milestone was in sight for the majority of the contacts in quarantine as they had remained well for the 21-day monitoring period and could return home from October 25.

It appealed to communities to welcome them back, saying they “pose no risk of infection”.

The ministry said no infections had occurred within quarantine facilities and that it was continuously monitoring infection-prevention measures to protect health workers.

Despite the nine infections, Kenya has not imposed restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings, with authorities saying the country remains open for business.

In the DRC, there have been more than 9,000 Ebola cases and 4,000 deaths since May.

The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control says it’s the second-largest epidemic on record.

It has been difficult to contain because there is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for the Bundibugyo strain of the virus.

Uganda had previously reported Ebola cases but was later declared free of the virus.

Ghana News.title: Adansi group petitions chief to reopen Obuasi SHTS, reinstate 38 teachers
Ghana News.content:
A group calling itself Concerned Citizens of Adansi has petitioned the Adansihene to intervene for the immediate reopening of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), which has remained closed for months following disturbances on campus.

The school was shut down after the Ashanti Regional Education Directorate and the Obuasi Municipal Assembly ordered its closure following a riot in which students reportedly attacked the headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, over allegations of sexual abuse involving female students.

Abdulai is currently under investigation following a recent JoyNews exposé that further examined allegations of sexual encounters with about 19 girls at the school. The allegations have not been established, and investigations are ongoing.

Despite the commencement of the new academic calendar in senior high schools, academic activities at Obuasi SHTS have yet to resume.

In their petition, the concerned citizens said the closure had left Form Two and Form Three students at home without a clear timeline for returning to the classroom.

“The situation is particularly alarming for Form Three students, who should be preparing intensively for their West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE). The loss of valuable instructional time threatens their examination preparation and academic prospects,” the statement said.

The group said parents and guardians were increasingly distressed by the uncertainty surrounding their children’s education.

“Our children must not become collateral victims of an administrative crisis. Their right to education and their prospects for academic success must not be sacrificed while the relevant authorities deliberate over the issues surrounding the school,” it added.

Group questions reported dismissal of 38 teachers

The group also expressed concern over the reported dismissal of 38 teachers from the school following criticism of the handling of allegations involving the headmaster.

It said the reports raised questions about administrative accountability, procedural fairness and the protection of teachers who raise concerns about developments within their institution.

“We acknowledge that the allegations require independent verification. Nevertheless, we are deeply concerned that the reported transfers could create a perception of victimisation and divert public attention from the substantive issues that require investigation,” the statement said.

“The displacement of teachers must not become a substitute for establishing the truth, nor should innocent educators suffer professional consequences for raising legitimate concerns.”

Calls for impartial investigation

The concerned citizens are appealing to traditional authorities to intervene to secure the reopening of the school.

They are also demanding an impartial investigation into the allegations against the headmaster and the circumstances surrounding the reported directive affecting the teachers.

The group said resolving the issues was necessary to protect students’ education while ensuring that the allegations and concerns raised by staff were addressed through a fair process.

Ghana News.title: Specsavers founders get lifetime retail award
Ghana News.content:
Specsavers' founders have been given a lifetime award for their role in "transforming access to optical and audiology care".

Douglas and Dame Mary Perkins started the multinational company in Guernsey on a table-tennis table in their spare bedroom in 1984. The company now has more than 2,600 stores in 11 countries.

They received the Lifetime Contribution Award at the Retail Gazette Awards last week, which honours people shaping the industry's future.

Dame Mary said she was "genuinely surprised" to receive the award, and described it as a "real honour to be recognised".

She said: "It's a real honour to be recognised by the industry, especially as Doug and I approach 60 years in optics.

"What makes it even more special is knowing that Specsavers has only ever been possible because of the passion and commitment of our partners and colleagues.

"They've helped shape the business from day one and continue to make a difference for our customers every day."

Ghana News.title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman wins dismissal of sister’s lawsuit
Ghana News.content:
OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman has won a dismissal of a lawsuit brought against him by his sister that claimed he had sexually abused her more than two decades ago.

A US district judge dismissed the case after Ann Altman refused to attend an independent medical examination, adding that she was warned that failing to do so would result in the case being thrown out.

Ann Altman had claimed the OpenAI founder had regularly sexually abused her between 1997 and 2006. Sam Altman has denied those accusations.

The Altman family has said Ann Altman has mental health challenges and they have supported her financially, adding the claims were made as she continued to demand more funds.

District Judge Zachary Bluestone said that despite multiple accommodations and opportunities, Ann Altman did not appear for an independent medical exam on three separate occasions and "failed to meaningfully prosecute her case".

"Because Annie has continued to violate her discovery obligations and forced this case to a halt through her intransigence, the Court has run out of options and, thus, dismisses her claims with prejudice," he said in his written order.

The case was filed on 6 January 2025 in the Eastern District of Missouri.

In it, Ann Altman claimed that her older brother Sam Altman began abusing her when she was three, and he was 12.

However, in a joint statement released by Sam Altman along with his mother and two brothers at the time, the family said they were concerned for Ann Altman's well-being and had spent years trying to support her financially and look after her well-being.

The family said she receives monthly financial support, and her bills and rent are covered, while they also try to help with medical care.

The statement said her claims against Sam Altman changed drastically over time, but all of them were "utterly untrue".

Sam Altman is the co-founder of OpenAI, which launched its popular ChatGPT artificial intelligence chatbot in 2022.

Ghana News.title: Trump sued over Canadian tariffs in latest legal challenge
Ghana News.content:
US President Donald Trump faces another tariff-related legal challenge after the group that successfully sued over his so-called "liberation day" import taxes filed a new lawsuit over the latest Canadian levies.

The White House imposed a 50% levy on some $20bn of Canadian goods after trade talks between the US and Canada broke down in August.

The Liberty Justice Centre filed a suit on behalf of US food business Gellert Global Group, urging the US Court of International Trade to find the levies unlawful and to order refunds with interest for affected importers.

The lawsuit argues the White House exceeded its authority in imposing the tariffs and caused "immediate harm to American businesses".

The White House has been contacted for comment.

Gellert Global Group is a third-generation family business that is paying 50% tariffs on cheese exported from Canada. The New Jersey-based firm is also facing retaliatory tariffs from Canada on American-made cheese it sells north of the border.

Co-chief executive Thomas Gellert said the firm spent generations building relationships with food industry suppliers and customers.

"These tariffs disrupt those relationships overnight and create costs and uncertainty that ripple through the entire supply chain," he said on Tuesday.

The Liberty Justice Centre is challenging the administration's use of Section 338 of the 1930 Tariff Act to hit Canadian goods from wine to dairy products and hockey sticks.

That section of the nearly 100-year-old Act aims to protect US businesses from foreign discrimination, but the legal group argues it does not allow the executive branch to "impose sweeping tariffs or import restrictions whenever a trade dispute arises".

The lawsuit seeks to challenge the White House's reliance on retaliatory tariffs imposed by Canada to justify its own duties under Section 338.

Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures against numerous US tariffs. Last month, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney matched the Section 338 US tariffs "dollar for dollar" after Trump imposed them for what he called "unequal treatment" of US cars, dairy and alcohol.

It also points out that Section 338 requires a 30-day waiting period before levies can be imposed, but the tariff on products including cheese was added to the list just a week before tariff collection began.

Sara Albrecht, chief executive of the Liberty Justice Centre, said the case was not about Trump himself but about the presidency.

"No president should have the power to pull a dormant statute off the shelf and use it to impose sweeping tariffs or import bans without the limits Congress required," she said.

The lawsuit argues that Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930 has been superseded by Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974.

It also argues that if Section 338 still applies, the White House has not established the legal basis for the sweeping tariffs against Canada.

"The case is not an objection to tariffs as such. It asks who has the power to impose them and whether the executive branch followed the law Congress wrote," the Liberty Justice Centre said.

The law group has also filed a motion for a preliminary injunction to block their collection.

It is the fourth case the group has brought against Trump's tariffs, including its successful challenge to the sweeping tariffs brought in under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) that were struck down in February this year.

Albrecht said the group had brought all the cases for the same reason: "The Constitution gives tariff power to Congress. The executive branch cannot keep moving the same policy from one statute to another and pretend the limits disappear".

Ghana News.title: Veteran gospel musician Bernice Offei to be buried on November 14
Ghana News.content:
Veteran Ghanaian gospel musician Bernice Offei will be buried on Saturday, November 14, 2026, with funeral activities scheduled to take place at the Legon Interdenominational Church (LIC) in Legon, Accra.

The funeral arrangements include a remembrance night on Wednesday, November 11, ahead of the burial service and final funeral rites on November 14.

The remembrance night will begin at 7:00 pm, with seating scheduled to start at 6:30 pm.

On Saturday, November 14, filing past will take place from 7:00 am to 9:00 am, followed by the burial service from 9:00 am to 11:00 am.

The interment will be private, while the final funeral rites will be held at the church after the burial service.

A thanksgiving service is scheduled for Sunday, November 15, at 10:30 am at the same venue. The funeral announcement indicates that there will be no sitting after the memorial service.

Background

Bernice Offei died on Saturday, September 12, 2026, at the age of 63, after a career spanning several decades in Ghana’s gospel music industry. Her death was announced by fellow gospel musician Nii Okai, while music producer Kwasi Ernest also confirmed the news.

Her passing came days after she had been reported missing in Accra on September 1. She was later found, bringing relief to her family and members of the public who had joined efforts to locate her.

Her former manager, Kwasi Ernest, disclosed that she had battled dementia for about five years before her death. He said the condition affected her memory and ability to carry out everyday activities.

Offei was widely known for gospel songs including Life Is Short, Hold On and Kaa She Gbeyei. Her contribution to Ghanaian gospel music was recognised at the 2009 Ghana Music Awards, where she won Best Female Vocal Performance and Songwriter of the Year.

She leaves behind a musical legacy that inspired generations of gospel music lovers in Ghana and beyond.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
