World.title: Basketball: NBA sets Africa-player record for 2026-27
World.content:
By Emmanuel Okogba

The National Basketball Association (NBA) has announced a record number of players born in Africa or with at least one parent born on the continent on opening-night rosters for the 2026-27 season, with six Nigerian players listed among the international contingent.

According to the league, more than 60 players with African backgrounds feature on opening-night rosters, while the overall number of international players stands at 125 from 43 countries across six continents.

The NBA said this marks the sixth consecutive season with at least 120 international players and the 13th straight season with at least 100.

The six players listed under Nigeria are Ugonna Onyenso of the Detroit Pistons, Charles Bassey of the Golden State Warriors, Adem Bona of the Philadelphia 76ers, Precious Achiuwa of the Sacramento Kings, Josh Okogie of the Utah Jazz and Felix Okpara of the Washington Wizards.

The league also reported that more than 25 of the players with African backgrounds have Nigerian connections, including those born elsewhere or with at least one parent from Nigeria.

Among the prominent players with Nigerian heritage are Miami Heat star Bam Adebayo, New York Knicks forward OG Anunoby and Milwaukee Bucks forward Giannis Antetokounmpo. The African-connected group also includes Philadelphia 76ers centre Joel Embiid and Indiana Pacers forward Pascal Siakam, both of whom were born in Cameroon.

The NBA said France leads the international player count with 17, followed by Canada with 16. Australia has nine players, Germany seven, while Nigeria and Serbia have six each.

France’s representation is led by San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama, the reigning NBA Defensive Player of the Year. Canada’s contingent includes Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning two-time NBA Most Valuable Player.

The Dallas Mavericks, Miami Heat and Washington Wizards have the highest number of international players among NBA teams, with seven each. All 30 franchises have at least one international player on their opening-night rosters.

The league also recorded 70 European players for the season, marking the second consecutive campaign with at least that number.

International players have continued to make their mark on the NBA’s individual awards. According to the league, four international stars have shared the last eight Most Valuable Player awards: Gilgeous-Alexander, Nikola Jokić, Joel Embiid and Giannis Antetokounmpo.

Last season also marked the fifth consecutive campaign in which three international players finished among the top three in MVP voting, with Gilgeous-Alexander first, Jokić second and Wembanyama third.

The NBA further announced that a record 19 international players who have previously been named All-Stars are on opening-night rosters for the 2026-27 season.

More than 45 players on the rosters have also participated in Basketball Without Borders, the NBA and International Basketball Federation’s global basketball development and community outreach programme.

The 2026-27 campaign is the NBA’s 81st regular season. The league said its games would reach fans in 214 countries and territories in more than 50 languages through broadcast partners and NBA League Pass.

The record African representation and Nigeria’s six-player contingent underscore the continued presence of Nigerian talent in the NBA as the league expands its international reach.

World.title: EBOLA: FAAN urges calm, vigilance among airport users
World.content:
By Dickson Omobola

Following the confirmation of an Ebola Virus Disease case in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, has said it is working with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, Port Health Services, the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, and other relevant agencies to support ongoing containment efforts.

FAAN urged passengers, airport users, airlines and other stakeholders to remain calm, vigilant and cooperative with health officials.

Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection at FAAN, Henry Agbebire, in a statement, said the authority had maintained heightened vigilance across airport operations and would continue to coordinate with public health authorities.

The statement reads: “The early identification of the case and commencement of contact tracing underscore the importance of established public health protocols, effective surveillance and inter-agency collaboration in responding to potential health threats.

“FAAN is maintaining heightened vigilance across airport operations and will continue to coordinate with public health authorities, align its response with further guidance and support additional measures considered necessary to safeguard passengers, airport personnel and the wider public.

“The authority urges passengers, airport users, airlines and other stakeholders to remain calm, vigilant and cooperative with health officials. The public is also advised to rely on verified information and avoid spreading unconfirmed reports.

“FAAN reassures the travelling public of its continued readiness to work with relevant agencies to protect public health and support the safe operation of Nigeria’s airports.”

World.title: PSG late show downs Barca in Champions League, Liverpool fight back
World.content:
Barcelona’s Spanish forward #10 Lamine Yamal (R) reacts at the end of the UEFA Champions League first round day 3 football match between Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and FC Barcelona at the Parc de Princes stadium in Paris on October 20, 2026. (Photo by JULIEN DE ROSA / AFP)

Holders Paris Saint-Germain made it three wins from three in this season’s Champions League, beating Barcelona 4-2 thanks to late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz on Tuesday, while Liverpool clinched a dramatic comeback victory over Villarreal.

Phil Foden scored a hat-trick as Manchester City thrashed AEK Athens 5-1, while there were also much-needed wins for Roma and Napoli.

PSG kept their place at the top of the early league-phase table, but could yet count the cost of injuries suffered by Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia at the Parc des Princes.

Barcelona twice levelled against the two-time defending champions, but were ultimately well beaten as they slipped to their first defeat of the season.

Hansi Flick’s men had won their previous 11 games in all competitions this term.

Kvaratskhelia hit the post, Dembele hobbled off and Ferran Torres was denied by Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia in a fast-paced opening.

PSG took a deserved lead in the 38th minute as Desire Doue collected the ball outside the area and thumped a shot into the bottom corner.

Garcia made another excellent save shortly after the break from Achraf Hakimi, before Xavi Espart burst through to level for Barca against the run of play.

Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos both pulled up injured within seconds of each other and had to leave the field.

The home team continued to press, though, and Lucas Hernandez restored their advantage 18 minutes from time with a brilliant header, shortly after former Barcelona forward Torres hit the post.

Lamine Yamal powered past Warren Zaire-Emery to equalise again seven minutes later.

But Vitinha hammered home from outside the box in the 81st minute and Ruiz’s tap-in gave Luis Enrique’s team a second straight 4-2 Champions League win after seeing off Man City by the same scoreline last week.

– Liverpool fight back –

Liverpool battled back from two goals down to also maintain their 100-percent record by edging out Villarreal 4-3 at Anfield.

Liverpool fell behind in the fourth minute when Georges Mikautadze pounced on a terrible error from Virgil van Dijk, before Villarreal defender Sergi Cardona strolled through their defence to make it two.

Alexis Mac Allister pulled one back for the hosts nine minutes before half-time by heading in Kostas Tsimikas’s corner.

Andoni Iraola’s men were level in first-half added time through Ronald Araujo’s back-post header after Cardona inexplicably left Rio Ngumoha’s cross.

Mac Allister completed the turnaround by firing in from Ngumoha’s square pass, and half-time substitute Florian Wirtz’s first goal of the season gave the Reds some breathing space.

Tani Oluwaseyi set up a nervy finish for Iraola, but Liverpool held on.

At the Etihad, Elliot Anderson put Manchester City in front with his first goal for the club, tapping in a 12th-minute opener after Enzo Fernandez’s free-kick bounced back off the crossbar.

Phil Foden made it two goals in as many games after scoring against Ipswich at the weekend, but AEK halved the deficit early in the second half through Stavros Pilios.

Rayan Cherki capped a fine individual performance by sweeping in City’s third in the 57th minute.

Foden later fired in his second and third goals in a comprehensive victory, despite Erling Haaland being rested after picking up a knock at the weekend.

– Respite for Serie A clubs –

Roma eased to their first Champions League win since 2019 as the capital club brushed aside pointless Slovan Bratislava 4-0 at the Stadio Olimpico.

All four Serie A clubs in the competition lost last week, but Napoli made it two wins from two on Tuesday for the Italian sides.

Massimiliano Allegri’s men were twice pegged back by Bodo/Glimt but eventually got the better of the Norwegians in a 4-3 thriller, as Scott McTominay scored a brace.

Atletico Madrid played out a 1-1 draw with Stuttgart in Germany, despite playing much of the second half with 10 men.

Borussia Dortmund ended a run of four straight away defeats in the Champions League with a 2-1 win over Sabah in Baku.

Fenerbahce suffered another setback after last week’s humiliating 6-0 loss at Aston Villa, blowing a two-goal lead to be held 2-2 at home by Slavia Prague.

PSV Eindhoven clinched their first victory with a 1-0 success at Porto.

World.title: Tinubu mourns Afenifere leader Fasoranti
World.content:
Pa Fasoranti

By Adeola Badru

Afenifere has mourned its leader, Chief Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, recalling his contributions to Nigeria’s independence struggle, opposition to military rule and the campaign for the restoration of the annulled June 12, 1993 presidential election, as it described him as an exemplary leader whose life embodied patriotism, courage and service to humanity.

The pan-Yoruba socio-political organisation announced his passing in a statement issued on Tuesday by its National Publicity Secretary, Comrade Jare Ajayi, who said the centenarian, also known as Asiwaju Yoruba, died at about 4pm.

Fasoranti, who turned 100 on May 11, 2026, was described by Afenifere as “a humanist, a philanthropist, an exemplary leader, a genuine patriot and a Yoruba leader and an icon” who remained a model of courage even in the most heart-rending circumstances.

The organisation said the late elder statesman was the first of its leaders to attain the age of 100, having assumed the leadership of Afenifere in November 2008 following the death of his predecessor, Chief Abraham Adesanya, in August of the same year.

According to the statement, Fasoranti followed in the footsteps of his predecessors by living an exemplary life from which individuals and organisations could draw inspiration and model their conduct.

One of the frontline followers of the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo in the Action Group’s struggle for Nigeria’s independence, Fasoranti remained involved in progressive politics in the post-independence period.

His lifetime spanned Nigeria’s colonial era, independence, the Civil War, successive military administrations and the return to democratic rule.

Afenifere recalled that Fasoranti was actively involved in the National Democratic Coalition (NADECO), which spearheaded the struggle for the restoration of the June 12, 1993 presidential election won by the late Chief Moshood Kashimawo Olawale Abiola.

The organisation said he participated actively in efforts to restore civilian rule whenever the military intervened in Nigeria’s political process, describing him as “a democrat par excellence”.

It added that Fasoranti, like his political mentor, Awolowo, and his predecessors as Afenifere leader, the late Chief Adekunle Ajasin and Chief Abraham Adesanya, believed that public office should be used to serve the best interests of the people.

Beyond his political engagements, the late elder statesman was an educationist who established Omolere Nursery and Primary School, Akure High School and St. Frances’ Academy in Igoba, Akure, Ondo State.

He also served as Ondo State Commissioner for Finance between 1979 and 1983 under the administration of the late Governor Michael Adekunle Ajasin in the old Ondo State.

Afenifere described Fasoranti as an unassuming progressive icon whose commitment to humanity, philanthropy and public service would continue to inspire individuals and organisations.

The organisation said it would “sorely miss this exemplary, unassuming, progressive icon who was a humanist and philanthropist in every sense of it”.

It extended its condolences to the deceased’s immediate and extended families, the Ondo State Government and people, members of the Afenifere family in Nigeria and the diaspora, the Yoruba people worldwide and Nigerians, noting that Nigeria was a country dear to Fasoranti.

World.title: FIFA U17 WWC: Flamingos beat Puerto Rico 2-0 to boost hopes
World.content:
Nigeria’s U-17 women’s national team, the Flamingos, boosted their chances at the ongoing FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco after securing a 2-0 victory over Puerto Rico in their Group B encounter in Rabat on Tuesday.

The Flamingos, who won bronze at the 2022 edition of the competition, took the lead in the 25th minute through striker Oluwakemi Adegbuyi, who converted a pass from Queen Joseph.

Nigeria started brightly, applying pressure on Puerto Rico’s defence and creating opportunities through quick passing and forward movement.

Adegbuyi’s goal rewarded the team’s early efforts and gave Nigeria greater control of the game as the first half progressed.

The Nigerian side continued to search for a second goal after the break, with Queen Joseph, Tosin Rafiu and Favour Nkwocha among those who threatened the Puerto Rican defence.

Puerto Rico attempted to respond with tactical changes, but Nigeria coach Hakeem Busari also made substitutions to strengthen his team’s attacking options.

Awawu Bashiru and Oluebube Umejiaku were introduced in the 67th minute as the Flamingos maintained their push for another goal.

Their efforts paid off in the 90th minute when substitute Precious Oscar headed home a cross from Kemi Adegbuyi to double Nigeria’s lead and secure the victory.

The Flamingos held on through six minutes of added time to claim all three points and strengthen their position in Group B.

In the other group fixture, North Korea defeated Poland 6-1, setting up an important encounter with Nigeria on Friday.

The result against Puerto Rico gives the Flamingos a boost ahead of the meeting with North Korea, which could prove crucial to their progress in the tournament.

World.title: 2027: PDP, APGA, Accord join Tinubu’s re-election campaign — Yilwatda
World.content:
Yilwatda

-Says ruling party ready for Saturday’s campaign flag-off in Kaduna

-As Yari promises issue-based campaign, says APC will showcase Tinubu’s achievements without insults

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — The National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, has claimed that major opposition parties, including the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) and the Accord Party, have aligned with the ruling party’s campaign for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election in 2027.

Yilwatda stated this while speaking to State House correspondents shortly after meeting with President Tinubu alongside the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC), Senator Abdulaziz Yari, to brief him on preparations for the campaign.

He said the development demonstrated the growing political support for the President, adding that the APC had completed preparations for the formal launch of its nationwide presidential campaign in Kaduna on Saturday, October 24.

The APC Chairman said the party has attracted support from political parties that previously defeated the APC in elections, a development he described as evidence of the broadening political alignment around the President.

According to him: “If you look at what the party is doing now, the oppositions are with us. All political parties that have defeated us in any election are all with us; PDP is with us, APGA is with us, Accord Party with us. These are the only political parties that have defeated us, except APM, and they are all with us in this campaign.

“It shows that the entire Nigerian political cycle is Mr. President, and that’s what we’re doing now to ensure that we prepare for this grand flag off in Kaduna”, he declared.

He, however, did not specify whether the claimed support represented formal endorsements by the national leaderships of the opposition parties or political alliances involving individual members and groups within them.

Yilwatda expressed satisfaction with the level of preparations for the Kaduna campaign launch, saying the party’s leadership, campaign committees and state structures were fully mobilised for the exercise.

He explained that his meeting with the President, alongside Yari, was intended to provide an update on arrangements for the event and the readiness of the campaign organisation to commence activities across the country.

“We’ll flag-off the campaign on Saturday, 24th of October, and as you can see, we’re together with the DG to brief Mr. President on the preparation for the flag off.

“For now, everything is set; the preparation is on, the members are motivated, the states, the committees are ready, and everything that is supposed to be done has been done”, he said.

Speaking separately, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, said the ruling party would conduct a responsible and issue-based campaign anchored on the achievements of the Tinubu administration rather than personal attacks against opposition candidates.

Yari, a former governor of Zamfara State, said the campaign council had resolved to focus on the record of the APC-led Federal Government and present its accomplishments to Nigerians as the basis for seeking another mandate in the 2027 presidential election.

He maintained that the ruling party would avoid insults and name-calling, insisting that its campaign would be driven by evidence of government performance and the argument for continuity.

“As a Council, what we say we are going to do? We are going to do a campaign with the records. A responsible campaign, no insults, no calling of names because there’s no name before us, but we have a record before us to show to Nigerians”, Yari stated.

He explained that the campaign would provide an opportunity for the party to engage Nigerians on the policies and programmes implemented under the Tinubu administration and make the case for their continuation.

“This is what our party did, this what our government did, so because of that, we are asking, pleading Nigerians to look at this record carefully so that they give us a second chance for continuity”, he added.

The remarks came as the APC intensified preparations for its nationwide presidential campaign ahead of the 2027 general elections, with Kaduna designated as the venue for the formal flag-off.

Yari had earlier announced, following a meeting with Tinubu on October 9, that the President had approved the campaign timetable, including planned visits to states across the federation.

The Presidential Campaign Council was subsequently inaugurated on October 14, setting the stage for the commencement of the ruling party’s nationwide mobilisation activities.

President Tinubu chairs the campaign council, with Vice President Kashim Shettima and Yilwatda serving as vice chairmen, while Yari oversees the day-to-day coordination of campaign activities as Director-General.

World.title: APC campaign: Tinubu has nothing to say to Nigerians — Baba-Ahmed
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

The National Chairman of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, has described President Bola Tinubu as a failure, alleging that the president has nothing to say to Nigerians as the 2027 general election approaches.

Baba-Ahmed made the remarks during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Tuesday, while criticising Tinubu’s administration over worsening insecurity, economic hardship and the impact of its policies on Nigerians.

“Tinubu inherited Nigeria, but what has he done with it? He inherited a poor country; he inherited weak institutions; he inherited poverty and insecurity. We don’t blame him, but he’s been in power for three and a half years. He is a failure,” he said.

The PRP chairman also questioned the president’s reported decision to campaign in only a few places, asking why Tinubu would not commit himself to meeting Nigerians and explaining his policies and the impact on their lives.

“Why doesn’t Tinubu commit himself to say, I will. I have the energy, I have the intention, I want to see Nigerians, I want Nigerians to see me, I want them to hear me explain why they are more hungry,” Baba-Ahmed said.

Asked why he believed Tinubu had indicated he would visit only a few places during the campaign, Baba-Ahmed replied: “Yes, he has nothing to say to them, I’m telling you, he has nothing to say to Nigerians.”

He added: “The reason why he said, Go, gentlemen, go and campaign for me. I will stay here in Abuja and run the country. You’re running the country now? For three and a half years, you didn’t run the country, now you remember that you are here to run the country?”

Baba-Ahmed also faulted the administration’s economic reforms, arguing that the difficult decisions taken by Tinubu had hurt ordinary Nigerians rather than improved their lives.

“He (Tinubu) made some tough decisions but they were anti-people decisions, a tough decision doesn’t have to be a good decision,” he said.

He questioned the impact of the administration’s policies on education, particularly for children living in areas affected by insecurity.

“You talk about creating loans, that’s good, but do you know how many millions of children that can’t go to school under Tinubu’s watch in this country? Children who live in territories taken over by bandits, kidnappers, and who can’t go to school at all?”

The PRP chairman further alleged that insecurity had deteriorated under the current administration.

“Security has gotten considerably worse, it has never been worse like this,” he said.

On the administration’s defence of its economic reforms, Baba-Ahmed dismissed the presentation of economic statistics as propaganda, arguing that the figures did not reflect the hardship experienced by ordinary Nigerians.

“All these things you mentioned, this is the propaganda. Unfortunately, for Tinubu, Nigerians are not going to buy it. Children are not going to school, life is more insecure, life is harder,” he said.

He argued that the president’s appeal for another four-year term would require Nigerians to accept that the current difficulties would eventually give way to better conditions.

“He flashes all these statistics, he is saying, give me a second chance, even Tinubu will not say he made lives more better, what he will say is that yes, we are going through a difficult part, if you give me another four years, we will get better,” Baba-Ahmed said.

He also questioned the administration’s economic sequencing, arguing that a government anticipating significant economic consequences from its policies should have considered their effects before implementing them.

“You said the microeconomics is good, those are statistics that they use and they will tell you, if you give me another four years, I will see them. Sir, if you knew you had four years within which you’ll embark on a profoundly influential policy, shouldn’t you look at it first of all and say, I’m going to have four years and if I embark on these policies, it will have major economic impacts.”

Baba-Ahmed added that a president should consider the immediate effects of economic policies on citizens before proceeding with them.

“A thinking president will say let me do one or two things first, because I will impoverish people and the cost of transportation is vital and central to everything.”

World.title: UK reaffirms commitment to deepen defence, security partnership with Nigeria
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

The United Kingdom has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening its longstanding defence and security partnership with Nigeria, with renewed focus on military cooperation, professional military education, institutional capacity building and enhanced operational effectiveness.

Director of Defence Information, Major General Samaila Uba said the commitment was reiterated when the recently appointed British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Mr. Pete Vowles, paid a courtesy visit to the Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General OO Oluyede, at the Defence Headquarters, Abuja.

The British High Commissioner expressed appreciation for the enduring political, diplomatic and military relations between both countries, emphasising that defence and security cooperation remain critical pillars of the UK-Nigeria bilateral relationship.

He underscored his determination to sustain the momentum of existing security initiatives and explore opportunities to deepen collaboration in response to evolving regional and global security challenges.

He further highlighted the importance of maintaining a strong and mutually beneficial partnership that support regional stability and strengthens Nigeria’s capacity to address contemporary security threats.

In his response, the CDS highlighted the longstanding historical ties between Nigeria and the United Kingdom, noting that both countries have sustained a productive defence relationship for several decades and continued to work together in addressing shared security concerns.

General Oluyede emphasised the importance of sustaining and expanding existing areas of cooperation, particularly in professional military education, transfer of technology and institutional capacity building.

He noted that ongoing defence agreements and training programmes have contributed to enhancing the professional competence and operational capabilities of the Armed Forces of Nigeria.

The CDS stressed that continued collaboration with strategic international partners remains important to strengthening the Armed Forces’ capacity to respond effectively to emerging threats, while promoting greater self-reliance, institutional resilience and operational efficiency.

Both parties expressed optimism about the future of the UK-Nigeria defence and security partnership, reaffirming their commitment to building on existing achievements and identifying further areas of cooperation for mutual benefit.

World.title: Obasanjo ​‌⁠⁠​‍⁠⁠‍‌​​‍‍⁠‍⁠‌​Mourns Fasoranti, Uduaghan
World.content:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has expressed sadness over the deaths of Chief Reuben Fasoranti, former Afenifere leader, and Dr Emmanuel Uduaghan, former Delta governor.

Obasanjo described Fasoranti as one of the last surviving titans of a generation that laid the foundation for modern Nigeria through selfless service, sacrifice and unwavering integrity.

He said this in a statement on Tuesday in Abeokuta by his Special Assistant on Media, Kehinde Akinyemi.

According to Obasanjo, Fasoranti’s life exemplified purposeful leadership, integrity and an unwavering commitment to the progress of the Yoruba nation and Nigeria.

The former president described the late elder statesman’s death as the end of an extraordinary era, recalling his contributions to education and nation-building.

Obasanjo said Fasoranti had served as a school principal in several historic institutions, moulding minds, instilling discipline and building character before venturing into politics.

He also recalled Fasoranti’s tenure as Commissioner for Finance in the old Ondo State under the Unity Party of Nigeria (UPN) administration.

According to him, the late Afenifere leader’s record in office remains a reference point for fiscal discipline, transparency and accountability.

Obasanjo said Fasoranti provided unifying leadership when he assumed the leadership of Afenifere amid internal divisions and national uncertainty.

He added that the late elder statesman consistently opposed military dictatorship and advocated true federalism, justice and equity despite threats to his life.

“When the mantle of leading Afenifere fell upon him during a period of fragmentation and national uncertainty, Baba did not falter.

“He stepped up as a unifying anchor. He led with a calm and resolute authority that derived its strength not from loud proclamations, but from the immense moral weight of his convictions.

“On a personal note, I will always remember Baba’s warmth and his open-door policy. Even when we found ourselves on different sides of political debates, our mutual respect never waned,”he said.

On Uduaghan, Obasanjo described his death as a painful loss to Nigeria, saying the country had lost a gentleman, dedicated medical professional, and an accomplished statesman.

He recalled working with Uduaghan during his presidency when the latter served under former Delta governor, James Ibori, as Commissioner for Health and later Secretary to the State Government.

Obasanjo said Uduaghan distinguished himself as a brilliant administrator and a calm voice of reason during periods of political turbulence and heightened agitation in the Niger Delta.

He added that their interactions on healthcare policies and federal-state relations demonstrated Uduaghan’s administrative competence and commitment to Delta State’s peace and development.

Obasanjo said these qualities prepared Uduaghan for the responsibilities of leadership when he became governor of Delta State in 2007. (NAN)

World.title: Tinubu Mourns Fasoranti, Pays Glowing Tribute to Late Afeniifere Leader
World.content:
.Says Nigeria’ll sorely miss his voice of wisdom, moral authority, fatherly counsel

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has paid glowing tribute to the late Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, who died on Tuesday at the age of 100.

The President, in a tribute signed by him described the patriarch and elder statesman as an icon, beacon of principle and one of the last great titans of Chief Obafemi Awolowo’s progressive family.

According to him, Nigeria will sorely miss Pa Fasoranti’s voice of wisdom, moral authority and fatherly counsel.

Tinubu, in the 13-paragraph release stated, inter alia: “I received with profound sadness the news of the passing of Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, our father, patriarch, elder statesman, and foremost Afenifere leader, who died at the glorious age of 100.

“On behalf of the Federal Government and the people of Nigeria, I commiserate with the Fasoranti family, the good people of Akure Kingdom, the government and people of Ondo State and South-West Nigeria, and the entire Afenifere family.

“Pa Fasoranti was an icon, a beacon of principle, and one of the last great titans of Chief Obafemi Awolowo’s progressive family.

“His life, spanning a century, was a lesson in integrity, discipline, selflessness, and unwavering commitment to the Yoruba people and the unity and progress of Nigeria.

“From his days as an educationist and principal, to his stewardship as Commissioner for Finance in the old Western Region, and later as the leader of Afenifere, Baba never wavered in his belief in true federalism, social justice, and a Nigeria that works for all.

“Baba made immense contributions to this country and, at the risk of his life, fought for the democracy we enjoy today.

“Pa Fasoranti distinguished himself in every respect: in his disciplined, Spartan way of life, his belief in principles, and his commitment to noble causes.

“Our nation will sorely miss his voice of wisdom, moral authority, and fatherly counsel, especially now, when we need his guidance most.

“I recall Baba’s centenary on May 11 this year, when we celebrated not just longevity, but a legacy of honour. He lived a fulfilled life and left indelible footprints in the sands of time.

“I also recall his prayers and counsel when I came to his residence in Akure in 2022 to inform him of my decision to contest the presidency. Pa Fasoranti told me I would be President in his lifetime, and God answered his prayer.

“I had hoped Papa would also be around with us for my second term to witness the full dawn of economic growth and prosperity in the land.

“But we must thank God for Pa Fasoranti’s long life of service, grace and fulfilment.

“May his gentle soul rest in perfect peace. May God comfort all who mourn him and grant his family the fortitude to bear this great loss.”

World.title: Presidency: Draft Of National Policing Bill Now Ready
World.content:
.Submitted along with 29 consequential amendment bills for legislative drafting review

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The Presidency on Tuesday disclosed that the draft of the 2026 National Policing Bill is ready.

Chief of Staff to the President and Chairman of the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill, Hon Femi Gbajabiamila, stated in a release that the group has completed the drafting stage of its assignment and has formally submitted the draft National Policing Bill (2026), together with 29 consequential amendment bills, to the Federal Ministry of Justice for legislative drafting review and validation.

According to him, the submission took place on Monday, to the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, in line with the Working Group’s work plan while the Ministry’s review will ensure that the bills conform to legislative drafting standards and conventions, and that they do not conflict with existing laws.

The Ministry of Justice, he further said, is expected to return the validated draft bills to the Working Group on or before Friday, 30th October 2026 and the Working Group will then give the validated bills final consideration before presenting them to Mr President, thereby concluding its mandate.

Gbajabiamila further said: The proposed National Policing Bill seeks to establish the constitutional and legislative framework for a dual policing structure, comprising a Federal Police Service and State Police Services.

“The Working Group remains committed to a rigorous and transparent process that will deliver a comprehensive legislative proposal for consideration by the President and subsequent transmission to the National Assembly.

“The work on preparing the National Policing Bill is proceeding alongside the ongoing consideration of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026 by the States Houses of Assembly, which must be completed before the Bill is transmitted to the National Assembly.”

The Presidency had last Thursday hinted that the National Policing Bill will be transmitted to the National Assembly within two weeks.

Gbajabiamila had told newsmen after the steering committee meeting at the State House in Abuja that “The National Policing Bill is more or less ready for transmission to the National Assembly. We will probably have one more meeting after this to cross the t’s and dot the i’s and make sure every area is covered. So, we are 90% ready.

“The governors have one or two observations, and we should be ready in about a week or so.”

He described the bill as ‘the most consequential Bill of the administration so far’ adding that it has undergone strenuous exercises in the last few weeks since the working group’s steering committee began deliberations on August 3, 2026.

Also commenting on the possibility of the states dragging their feet on the passage of the Sixth Constitution Alteration Bill (State Police), especially against the backdrop of the information that only about six states had passed the amendment out of the 36 states and the FCT, Gbajabiamila affirmed that there was a “national consensus” among Nigerians on the need for the amendments.

“I see no reason why anyone will want to have a rethink on it,” he said.

Members of the committee present at the Thursday’s meeting held at the conference hall of the Chief of Staff Office at the State House, Abuja, were Chairman of the Governors’ Forum and Governor of Kwara State, AbdulRazak AbdulRahman; Governors Dapo Abiodun, Ogun State; Uba Sani, Kaduna State; Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, and the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice represented by the Solicitor General and Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Justice, Mrs Beatrice Jedy-Agba.

Others included Chairman, Policy Advisory Committee, Justice Abdullahi Liman (rtd); Head, Nigeria Police Reform Secretariat, Professor Olu Ogunsakin; Special Adviser to the President on National Assembly Matters (House of Representatives), Dr Lanre Smart; Senior Special Assistant to the President on Planning and Research who also doubles as the Secretary of the Committee, Nnadubem Moghalu; representative of the President of the Nigerian Bar Association; and AIG Abraham Nabhon Thomas, representing the National Security Adviser, among others.

President Bola Tinubu had on July 7, 2026,

inaugurated the Presidential Working Group on the National Policing Bill to prepare the legal framework for the implementation of state police across the country.

The Working Group’s inauguration followed the National Assembly’s passage of the Constitution Alteration (State Police) Bill, 2026, in which the President proposes a dual policing structure comprising the Federal Police Service and 36 State Police Services.

Tinubu had pisited that while the constitutional amendment creates the framework for state police, the National Policing Bill would provide the legal structure for its implementation.

“The Constitution Amendment Bill establishes the framework for dual policing, but it does not operationalise it. That work is left to the National Policing Bill.”

According to him, the proposed legislation would address issues necessary for a smooth operationalisation of the State Police system.

“The proposed National Policing Bill will include provisions on minimum policing standards, state readiness certification, federal-state coordination, accountability, human rights safeguards and fiscal conditions.”

The President said that the committee will produce an implementation-ready draft bill immediately after the constitutional amendment process.

“The Working Group has been constituted to produce a technically robust, implementation-ready draft National Policing Bill for transmission to the National Assembly,” Tinubu said.

He said the committee was necessary to avoid delays after the State Police bill passed.

“We must not wait until the constitutional process is concluded before beginning this important assignment,” he said.

World.title: Breaking: Afenifere ​‌⁠⁠​‍⁠⁠‍‌​​‌‍‍​‌‌​Leader, Pa Fasoranti, Dies at 100, Aiyedatiwa Mourns
World.content:
Gov. Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has expressed sadness over the death of the leader of the pan-Yoruba socio-poitical organisation, Afenifere, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, at the age of 100.

Aiyedatiwa, in a condolence message he personally signed on Tuesday in Akure, said the death of the centenarian was a great loss to Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria.

The governor described Fasoranti as a patriarch and beacon of wisdom, integrity and selfless service, whose life was dedicated to the development of the society.

According to him, the late elder statesman demonstrated uncommon commitment to the progress and development of Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria throughout his lifetime.

“With a heavy heart but with total submission to the will of God, I announce the passing of our revered elder statesman, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, who departed this world at the glorious age of 100.

“Pa Fasoranti was a patriarch, a beacon of wisdom, integrity and selfless service whose century-long life was marked by uncommon commitment to the development of our dear State, Yorubaland and Nigeria at large,” he said.

Aiyedatiwa said the deceased would be remembered for his fatherly guidance, wise counsel and principled positions on issues bordering on justice and good governance.

He noted that Fasoranti lived a fulfilled life and left behind enduring legacies worthy of emulation by the present and future generations.

“His counsel, fatherly guidance and principled stand on issues of justice and good governance will be sorely missed.

“He lived a fulfilled life and left indelible footprints of honour and legacy for generations to come,” the governor said.

Aiyedatiwa, on behalf of the government and people of Ondo State, commiserated with the Fasoranti family, the people of Akure Kingdom and the entire state over the loss.

He prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul. (NAN)

World.title: Breaking: Nigeria Confirms Ebola Case in FCT, Identifies 44 Contacts, Activates Emergency Response
World.content:
The Federal Government has confirmed one imported case of Bundibugyo ebolavirus in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and has activated public health response measures to prevent further spread.

The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Pate, disclosed this at a media conference in Abuja on Tuesday, following laboratory confirmation of the infection on Oct. 20.

Pate said the patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was currently in isolation and receiving medical care.

He described the case as “a contained case,” while assuring Nigerians that the government was working with relevant authorities and partners to prevent further transmission.

Pate said the woman had been admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received care for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed.

He said contact tracing had commenced, with 44 close contacts identified so far, while public health teams were identifying and monitoring people who might have been exposed, including healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and travel contacts.

“Surveillance has also been intensified, and the private hospital where the patient was treated is receiving immediate support to strengthen infection prevention and control measures,” he said.

The minister urged public and private healthcare facilities nationwide to remain on high alert, maintain a high index of suspicion, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases.

He also urged the public to observe strict infection prevention and control measures, and immediately report suspected cases to public health authorities.

He said Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or body fluids of an infected person who is sick or has died from the disease, as well as contact with contaminated materials.

Pate advised Nigerians to practise regular hand hygiene, avoid contact with the body fluids of anyone suspected to have Ebola and watch for symptoms.

The symptoms, he said, included fever, severe weakness, headache, vomiting and diarrhoea, particularly following possible exposure.

He said people who might have been exposed should report immediately, even if they felt well, while anyone who developed symptoms should avoid close contact with others and call public health authorities for guidance before visiting a healthcare facility.

The minister also urged people contacted during the tracing exercise, including relevant airline passengers, to provide the required information and comply with public health advice.

He cautioned against rumours, misinformation and stigmatisation, advising Nigerians to rely on verified information from official health authorities.

Pate recalled that Nigeria had successfully contained Ebola in 2014 and had the experience and public health systems required to respond to the current case.

He, however, emphasised that containing the infection required cooperation from the public, early detection and prompt reporting of suspected cases.

“The Government of Nigeria through the Presidential Taskforce on EVD and NCDC will continue to provide updates.

“NCDC free call centre is available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. For information or to report a suspected case, please call NCDC toll-free number 6232,” Pate added.(NAN)

World.title: Zitra Investments Vows to Close Financial Inclusion Gap, Expands Access to Credit
World.content:
Marking its sixth anniversary, the management of Zitra has expressed its determination to close the financial inclusion gap and expand access to credit for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria.

The Chief Executive Officer of Zitra, Mr Babatunde Obadero, said at a press conference recently held in Lagos that SMEs remain the heartbeat of commerce in the country, and that the company is poised to help them access credit.

He said: “I dare say over 300,000 loans worth N30 billion have been disbursed in the last six years, with 200,000 customers on our digital platforms. The journey has just started, and there is still a lot of ground to cover.

“In six years, we have secured our banking licence, a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) asset management licence, and built a payment company called ZitraPay. All of these entities give us a platform to provide the services our customers need.

“We have built an ecosystem that delivers financial services just the way our customers need them. We are proud to say our growth has only just begun. We have a combined balance sheet of over N50 billion, which is the beginning of our journey to greater things ahead.”

Looking ahead, he said the company’s goal is to lead retail digital financial services in Nigeria, adding that it aims to expand its footprint geographically and improve access to its digital channels.

Co-founder of Zitra, Mr Femi Okuyelu, recalled that the company started with five staff and now has over 120 staff across different locations in the country.

“In terms of growth, we have seen the business evolve, and we have been able to solve some problems in the nation’s economy.

“Today in Nigeria, financial inclusion is about 79 per cent, which leaves 21 million adults financially excluded. That may look small, but it is more than the combined populations of Finland, Denmark and Estonia. And we have contributed our quota to that financial inclusion story,” he said.

On why credit penetration is still low, Okuyelu said: “Only 10 per cent of the adult population has access to credit. Most people borrow from family and friends, cooperatives and churches. Why can’t they access formal credit? Number one, they don’t have collateral. Number two, they operate in the informal sector, which is not organised. And number three, they have no credit history or records.”

He said Zitra’s response has been to create a social business model that onboards informal customers, helps them organise their businesses, monitors their cash flow and lends against it.

“What we have created will make it easier for them to access credit. We monitor their cash flow and lend against it, because in this environment, lending against collateral is difficult,” he said.

On his part, Director, Chief Olaotan Olamuyiwa, recalled that the idea for Zitra was conceived during COVID-19, when the founders decided to start their own firm after working in different organisations.

He said the journey has been built on relationships and one major investor who believed in the vision.

Speaking on how small businesses struggle with funding, he noted that many SMEs have their own money trapped with clients.

“You see people who want N5 million to stock up, but they have sold products to other businesses, and those businesses owe them in excess of N20 million. They cannot afford N5 million to finance a transaction because their cash is tied up,” he said.

He said products like invoice discounting address that gap, adding: “If you have N20 million in invoices due in 60 to 90 days, you can come to us and say, fund this N5 million project, and I will pay when my debtor pays.”

World.title: TETFund Urges Academics to Turn Research into Practical Innovations
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The Tertiary Education Trust Fund (TETFund) has urged Nigerian academics and researchers to move beyond publishing scholarly papers to developing practical innovations that address societal challenges and create economic opportunities.

The Executive Secretary, Sonny Echono, made the call in Abuja at the closing ceremony of the 35th cohort of the Research for Impact Initiative (R4i).

Echono said the initiative, implemented in partnership with Innov8 Hub, is part of the fund’s strategy to institutionalise research and development in public tertiary institutions and strengthen the relationship between academic research, industry and government.

“We must empower our scholars to create local solutions for our societal problems. This is why a commitment to education is a commitment to our nation’s future, ensuring that our people are not just consumers of foreign technology, but innovators who can drive sustainable growth,” he said.

He stressed that Nigeria needed to strengthen its capacity to develop home-grown technologies rather than depend on innovations from other countries.

He noted that technological advancement had become a major driver of economic transformation, adding that countries seeking sustainable development must invest in quality education, research and innovation.

“At TETFund, we are refocusing and reinvigorating our intervention activities to drive the institutionalisation of Research and Development in public tertiary institutions, enhance research capacity, and support research-industry linkage, among others,” he said.

He said R4i is designed to reposition public tertiary institutions as drivers of a knowledge-based economy through innovative practices and solution-driven research.

Echono commended Innov8 Hub for providing technical expertise and mentorship to participating academics, and urged the graduates to apply the knowledge acquired to develop solutions for their institutions and communities.

He disclosed that some innovations from previous editions of the programme were showcased at the maiden TETFund National Research Fair and Exhibition in November 2024.

The second edition will hold from November 23 to 27, 2026 at the Abuja Trade and Convention Centre, Airport Road, giving researchers the opportunity to showcase their innovations, connect with industry players and explore partnerships for commercialising research outputs.

The Deputy General Manager of Innov8 Hub, Dr. Deji Ige, said the initiative was designed to establish a culture in which research and development drive innovation, enterprise creation and national development.

“Innovation thrives in a culture where research and development are the primary languages of interaction. If we can learn, understand and revive this culture, the outcomes will include inventions, solutions, technological advancement, enterprise development, job creation, wealth generation, meaningful impact and societal development,” he said.

Ige described the programme as a shift towards stronger collaboration among government, academia, industry and society, adding that research without practical impact could limit the ability of tertiary institutions to contribute to technological advancement.

“Impact-driven research and development is what keeps it afloat and enables it to navigate safely. Without impact flowing from research and development, academia becomes an immobile vessel, bereft of progress, possibilities and the power to navigate,” he said.

World.title: ADC Unveils Kele As Running Mate, Intensifies Push for Plateau Govt House
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Plateau State has unveiled Hon. Chungdung Bitrus Pwajok Kele as the running mate to its governorship candidate, Brig.-Gen. John Sunday Sura (rtd), ahead of the 2027 governorship election.

The event, which took place in Jos, attracted party officials, stakeholders, supporters and political associates from across the state.

Speaking at the unveiling, Sura described Kele as an experienced politician and grassroots mobiliser whose emergence would strengthen the party’s efforts as it prepares for the forthcoming election.

He said the ADC ticket was aimed at providing what he described as an alternative platform for governance in Plateau State, adding that the party would focus on issues of security, rural development and inclusive leadership.

According to him, the unveiling marked the beginning of a series of political activities designed to expand the party’s presence across the state’s 17 local government areas.

He disclosed that the ADC would subsequently launch its governorship campaign and embark on consultations and mobilisation efforts in various constituencies across the state.

“We want Plateau people to know that ADC is on the ground. This is the beginning of our activities ahead of the campaign proper,” he said.

Sura also expressed confidence in the party’s chances in the election, stating that voters would assess the performance of the incumbent administration alongside the programmes being presented by opposition parties.

He said his campaign would focus on issues affecting citizens, including infrastructure, transportation, economic development and public welfare.

Responding to questions on the incumbency factor, the ADC governorship candidate maintained that the party remained focused on its objectives and would continue to engage voters.

On his running mate, Sura described Kele as a politician with extensive grassroots experience, noting that she had previously served as councillor representing Gyel ‘A’ Ward in Jos South Local Government Area and had contested for several elective offices.

He added that her political network and experience in mobilising women and young people would be of great advantage in the state governance.

ADC officials at the event expressed optimism that the Sura-Kele ticket would enhance the party’s reach across different demographic groups as political activities gradually gather momentum ahead of the 2027 general election.

World.title: ‘What did she do’? Fans speculate why Tracy Hlophe MUST apologise
Kearsney College mourns former top student’s tragic death
World.content:
Kearsney College is mourning the death of one of their star past pupils. Images via FB

Kearsney College is mourning the death of one of their Old Boys, Ndabenhle Shazi, who died in a car accident last week.

The star actor and performer passed just two days before his 33rd birthday.

The KwaZulu-Natal all-boys private school is South Africa’s Top 5 expensive schools.



KEARSNEY COLLEGE MOURNS ACTOR AND ARTIST ALUMNUS

On their social media platforms, Kearsney College shared the tragic news of the passing of their former top student, Ndabenhle Shazi.

They shared: “With deep sadness, we announce the tragic death of a shining Kearsney star and one of our dear brothers. Shazi, also known to family and older friends as Boyo, died in a car accident on the afternoon of Monday, 14 October 2026, near Ermelo. He was laid to rest at the family’s homestead on Saturday.

Affectionately known as “Shazi”, the 2012 matriculant was a distinguished drama student and musical artist who was involved in the school choir and theatre productions that were performed around the world.

This included an international tour to Asia in 2010 and to the World Choir Olympics in Cincinnati, USA, 2012, where the Kearsney College choir won 3 gold medals.

“Shazi made us laugh, cheer, sing and smile over many years. His laugh and personality brought joy to so many. With a heart of gold, he loved his Kearsney brothers and, being based in KZN, often popped in to visit staff members he respected and cared for.

“Shazi, you will always be a Kearsney legend and loved by many around the world. Rest in Peace, ” added the post.



CELEBRATED MUSIC AND DRAMA STUDENT

During his tenure at Kearsney College, Shazi served as chairman of the dance and drama club, head of choreography, and soloist in the school choir. He was also co-head of the Pembroke Inter-House Plays.

During his matric year, he received his colours and honours in music and dramatic arts.

After matriculating, he pursued his love of the performing arts through his entertainment company, SM ENT, where he continued to produce music and DJ under his artist name, Shazi Mayne.

He also graduated with a BCom in Supply Chain Management from the University of Pretoria.

World.title: Wednesday’s coastal tides: What beachgoers and anglers should know
World.content:
Beachgoers, surfers and anglers can check Wednesday’s high and low tide times before planning activities along South Africa’s coastline. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Tuesday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Water levels change throughout the day, while wind, waves, swell and the shape of the seabed also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

When to expect the next spring tide

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual.



The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing. High tides may cover rocks and reefs, while low tides expose more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: Tso uses Max Verstappen analogy to explain Kaizer Chiefs’ struggles
World.content:
Former Orlando Pirates midfielder Benedict Vilakazi believes Fernando Da Cruz’s time as Kaizer Chiefs coach could be short-lived, arguing that the club’s struggles go beyond the technical team.

Vilakazi, popularly known as Tso, believes Amakhosi lack the quality of players needed to compete for major trophies and fears the club could once again turn to a foreign coach if Da Cruz is dismissed.

Speaking to iDiski Times, the former midfielder predicted that Chiefs would look overseas for another coach rather than appoint a local tactician.



“He will leave and again, they will still go overseas to get a new coach,” he said.

Vilakazi also questioned why Chiefs did not consider local coaches such as Rulani Mokwena and Pitso Mosimane when they were available, pointing to their achievements at Mamelodi Sundowns.

“I don’t think Kaizer Chiefs will consider a local coach. When Rulani Mokwena and Pitso Mosimane were unattached, that was a perfect opportunity for them to say, ‘If we want to bring back glory days, here are people who showed at Sundowns that they are winners’. It didn’t happen,” he said.



However, Vilakazi believes changing coaches alone will not solve Amakhosi’s problems, insisting that the club must improve the quality of players at its disposal.

He argued that even an elite coach would struggle to deliver results without the right squad, using a car analogy to illustrate his point.

“Even if they bring in the best coach like Jose Mourinho, you still driving the same car. You can’t beat a Maserati driving a Toyota Tazz. You can put Max Verstappen in a Tazz and I’ll drive a Mercedes and I’ll be faster than him; that’s how it is,” he said.



Kaizer Chiefs told to get quality players

Vilakazi added that the quality of the squad ultimately determines what a coach can achieve, regardless of their reputation or experience.

“So whoever you put in the team, with the same material, he won’t get results for Kaizer Chiefs,” he concluded.

Do you agree with Tso?

World.title: Friend testifies about final moments before AKA and Tibz were shot dead
World.content:
Rapper Kierna ‘AKA’ Forbes’ friend and celebrity chef Tebello ‘Tibz’ Motsoane repeatedly said he could not breathe after gunshots were fired outside Wish restaurant on Florida Road in Durban, the Durban High Court heard on Tuesday.

Motsoane and AKA were gunned down on February 10, 2023.

Lindokuhle Mkhwanazi, Lindani Ndimande, Siyanda Myeza, Mziwethemba Gwabeni, Lindokuhle Ndimande, Malusi Ndimande and Siyabonga Ndimande face charges 11 charges including conspiracy to commit murder, murder, unlawful possession of a firearm, unlawful possession of ammunition, five counts of attempted murder, and money laundering.





WITNESS RECOUNTS DAY AKA WAS MURDERED

State witness Lusaso Ngcobo, a Durban musician and event organiser, testified on Tuesday and requested that his face not be shown.

Ngcobo told the court that he had known AKA for more than a decade through the music industry and that they were close friends. He also knew Motsoane through the industry.

He testified that on 10 February 2023, he went to the Bryd and Groom hair salon on Florida Road at around 18:30, as he usually did on Fridays. About 15 minutes later, AKA arrived with his entourage. The rapper, who was visiting the establishment for the first time, also had his hair cut.

Ngcobo said they spent time catching up before heading to Wish restaurant for dinner, where they discussed AKA’s plans, including the release of his new album Mass Country which was released posthumously on 24 February 2023.

Motsoane later joined them during the approximately two hours they spent at the restaurant.

Ngcobo testified that the group eventually left Wish through a passage leading outside. He was among those at the front, while AKA and Motsoane were behind him.



Once they reached the pavement, the group said their goodbyes. Ngcobo said he turned towards the passage to return inside after saying goodbye.

He testified that AKA was standing to his right and speaking to Motsoane, and AKA was about an arm’s length away just before the shooting. They planned to meet again later after the performance at Yugo nightclub in Durban.

Ngcobo recalled hearing a loud bang that initially sounded like fireworks.

“Right at that moment I heard a loud bang like fireworks. My first reaction was to duck because I wasn’t sure what was happening. I then saw everyone running and I realised it was unsafe and that maybe the sound couldn’t have been fireworks but a firearm instead,” he testified.

Ngcobo said he ran back towards the restaurant corridor with others. During the commotion, he saw Motsoane trip and fall.

He testified that he went to check on Motsoane before noticing AKA lying on the ground.

“I went to check on Tibz if he was okay and I recall seeing Kiernan lying on the floor I was walking out. I proceeded to check if he was okay because I could see some blood and I wasn’t sure if it was on him or on the floor. I asked him if he was okay, he said I can’t breathe. He kept saying I can’t breathe,” Ngcobo told the court.

“I proceeded to ask him if he was hurt and I could not make sense of the words he was saying. We tried to see where the blood was coming from as we were searching his body we realised he had a wound by his chest underneath his arm,” he added.

They called for assistance and attempted to stop the bleeding using towels while waiting for help to arrive.

World.title: Number Of The Day | 78.9% | 20 October 2026
World.content:
South Africa's Debt Problem Is Also a Public Spending Problem

Government debt is often discussed as a percentage of GDP, but the greater danger lies in what borrowing costs take away from the country's ability to invest in its future.

South Africa's debt debate is frequently reduced to whether a particular number is too high. The country has committed to stabilising government debt at 78.9% of gross domestic product, a threshold that has become an important test of fiscal policy. Yet the significance of that promise cannot be understood through the debt ratio alone. The more revealing question is how much it costs to carry the debt, and what those payments prevent government from doing.

A debt-to-GDP ratio compares the stock of government debt with the size of the economy. It gives an indication of the burden the country carries relative to its economic capacity, but it does not tell us everything about affordability. Interest rates, revenue collection, economic growth and the terms of existing borrowing all influence whether that burden becomes manageable or increasingly expensive.

For South Africa, this distinction matters because servicing debt competes directly with other spending priorities. In the 20 October edition of Number of the Day, Francis Herd highlights a striking measure of that pressure: according to the Finance Ministry figures he cites, more than 21 cents of every rand collected in tax revenue has been going towards debt-interest costs.

That is money required to meet obligations arising from previous borrowing, rather than to build something new. It reduces the fiscal space available for education, housing, infrastructure and other services. Debt-interest payments are a necessary part of government finance, but when they consume a substantial share of revenue, they make difficult spending choices even harder.

Why the cost of debt matters as much as its size

Governments routinely borrow to finance their activities, and borrowing is not inherently a sign of failure. Debt can help fund infrastructure and other investments that support future economic growth. The problem arises when borrowing grows faster than the economy's capacity to support it, or when the interest bill leaves too little room for productive expenditure.

Investor confidence plays an important role in that equation. A government viewed as financially risky may have to offer higher interest rates to attract lenders. Those higher costs can place further pressure on the budget, potentially creating a cycle in which expensive debt makes the debt problem more difficult to solve.

The opposite process is possible too. Credible fiscal management can support confidence and help contain borrowing costs. But confidence does not follow automatically from announcing a target. Lenders and rating agencies also examine whether budgets, economic assumptions and subsequent outcomes make that target believable.

The consequences reach beyond financial markets. When debt service absorbs revenue, the trade-off becomes visible in public infrastructure that needs maintenance, services facing pressure and development plans competing for scarce resources. The central economic issue is therefore not simply whether South Africa owes a large amount. It is whether the country can finance its obligations without continually sacrificing the investments needed to strengthen future growth.

A target is a starting point, not a solution

The Medium-Term Budget provides an opportunity to examine the credibility of government's debt plans. Stabilising debt at 78.9% of GDP would be significant if achieved, particularly after the long increase discussed by Herd. But the target is only meaningful if the underlying revenue, expenditure and growth assumptions can sustain it.

Slower economic growth can make a debt ratio harder to reduce even when spending is restrained. Higher borrowing costs can undermine improvements in revenue. Unexpected economic shocks can also derail forecasts. None of these risks makes fiscal commitments pointless; they make transparent assumptions and consistent implementation essential.

South Africa's challenge is ultimately to create a more sustainable relationship between what the state owes and what the economy produces. Reducing the burden of debt service would not resolve every development problem, nor would it guarantee better public services. It would, however, create more room for government to make choices about the future rather than continually paying for the past.

The real test of fiscal progress is not the announcement of a percentage. It is whether that percentage eventually translates into lower financial pressure and greater capacity to invest in the country.

References

· Number of the Day, 20 October 2026. Francis Herd, episode transcript. Source for the 78.9% debt target and the discussion of debt-interest costs.

· General public-finance explanations concerning debt sustainability, borrowing costs and spending trade-offs are analytical context, not additional verified claims about the October 2026 budget outcome.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
