What Came Off the Walls

Activist Marcela Sánchez of Colombia Diversa posted photos of empty walls on the afternoon of Thursday 15 October, and Infobae reported that about 30 pieces from three halls were missing. Vanguardia, citing later reconstructions, reported at least 48 objects taken from five permanent halls.

The missing items included a pride flag that belonged to activist Elizabeth Castillo, a 2006 LGBT march campaign piece and a leaflet on reproductive rights from the Fundación Sí Mujer, according to Infobae. Vanguardia added campaign posters, papers on the 1991 Constitution, a piece critical of mining and a shirt cyclist Lucho Herrera wore in the 1985 Tour de France.

Two of the removed images showed Carlos Pizarro, a former M-19 guerrilla commander killed on 26 April 1990, and Bernardo Jaramillo Ossa, a Patriotic Union presidential candidate killed in 1990. Vanguardia recalled that the Inter-American Court of Human Rights found the Colombian state responsible in 2022 for abuses against Patriotic Union members, and museum staff argue such items are documents, not endorsements.

The halls date from different governments, Vanguardia reported, with the Memory and Nation hall opened in 2014 and two more halls added in 2019 under President Iván Duque. A museum worker who asked not to be named told the paper that campaign posters are historical documents and that an archive is made of such material.

How the Government Defended the Move

President De la Espriella said on 15 October that terrorists would never again be treated as heroes of the nation, according to Infobae. He told Culture Minister Paola Holguín that every “ode to terrorism” featuring Pizarro must disappear from public places.

Holguín wrote on Friday 16 October that the museum is not meant to serve as an “instrument of political indoctrination” or to spread biased versions of history. She added that it cannot be a space for “apology for crime or re-victimisation” and must protect children from sensitive material.

The minister said the museum’s curatorial approach is being evaluated and redesigned, as quoted by Infobae. Her statement does not list which items were removed or say who selected them.

Anonymous museum sources told La Silla Vacía, as relayed by Infobae, that the ministry’s secretary general and the acting museum director picked the pieces. The ministry has not confirmed that account in the coverage we reviewed, and it should be read as an unconfirmed claim.

Reaction in the Streets and in Congress

Protesters gathered outside the museum over the weekend, El Colombiano reported, and Colombian modern art museums and ICOM Colombia, the national arm of the International Council of Museums, issued statements of rejection. Critics call the removals censorship, while the government calls the old displays political indoctrination.

Representative Jennifer Pedraza announced a political-control debate against Holguín, citing what she called censorship of the sector, according to 360 Radio. The debate would also look at the minister’s résumé and suspended funding calls, so it is wider than the museum case.

On Tuesday 20 October, Ombudsman Iris Marín asked Holguín to explain the legal, technical and administrative grounds for the removals, where the pieces are, their condition and whether they can return to the halls, El Universal reported. The ombudsman is a state human-rights watchdog, and her request is not a court order.

The tutela route lets a single judge act within days, as happened here. Our explainer Who Dominates Colombia, Elites and Regions Explained shows how the branches balance each other.

The dispute also touches how Colombians remember a long conflict that the 2016 peace deal tried to close. Our guide Colombia History Explained, From Origins to 2026 sets out that background.

What It Means for You

Travellers to Bogotá should expect gaps in the permanent halls, since Vanguardia described visitors finding bare walls and empty cases in recent days. Check the museum’s own channels for hall access before a visit, and see our What to Do in Bogotá in October 2026 guide for other options.

Investors and companies with Colombian exposure can read the Colombia judge’s step as a sign that judges can act within days on executive orders. Our Bogotá expat city guide and our explainer on Colombian media add context on the capital and the public debate.

What Is Not Known

The court order itself was not available to us, so the terms above rest on Publimetro, Minuto60 and El Colombiano, which agree on the main points. Outlets differ on the party label of the lead plaintiff, so we give only his name and office.

Vanguardia reported that the removed pieces remain in the museum’s custody, but the inventory the court ordered has not been published, so the location and condition of each item are not confirmed. The count differs between about 30 and at least 48 depending on the outlet and date.

The ministry’s one-working-day deadline to answer the court was still running on 20 October, according to La Silla Vacía, and no reply from the ministry or statement from the president on the order was found in coverage reviewed that day. The timing of a final ruling and of the congressional debate is also unknown.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did the Colombia judge order?

The judge ordered the National Museum to keep all pieces removed from its permanent halls in safe custody. The museum must also stop removing items because of their content unless an administrative act justifies it.

Who asked the court to act?

Representative Gabriel Becerra filed the tutela with Jorge Virviescas of the León Zuleta collective and Kevyn Muñoz Torres of Revolución en Rosa. They filed it against the Ministry of Culture and the National Museum.

How many pieces were removed?

Early reports counted about 30 pieces from three halls. Vanguardia, citing later reconstructions, reported at least 48 objects from five halls.

Why did the government remove them?

President Abelardo de la Espriella said he would not accept what he called an apology for terrorism in state spaces. Culture Minister Paola Holguín said the museum must not be a tool of political indoctrination.

Is the order a final ruling?

No, it is a provisional measure while the judge studies the case. The court has not yet decided whether the removals were lawful.

Sources: Publimetro, 19 October 2026; Minuto60, 19 October 2026; El Colombiano, 19 October 2026; Infobae, 16 October 2026; Vanguardia, 18 October 2026; El Universal, 20 October 2026; 360 Radio, 19 October 2026.

NIGERIA · MARKETS

Key Facts — The country Nigeria is Africa’s most populous nation and a major oil exporter. Its currency is the naira.

— What happened On Monday 19 October in Abuja, Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele urged the government to list oil company NNPC and gas exporter NLNG.

— The goal Oyedele wants a US$1 trillion capital market in 10 years; the regulator’s plan aims for N750 trillion (about US$563 billion).

— The market now Listed stocks were worth over N160 trillion (about US$120 billion) in September, up from about N30 trillion (about US$22.5 billion) since 2023.

— Who is involved Oyedele is finance minister and coordinating minister of the economy. Vice-President Kashim Shettima unveiled the 10-year plan.

— The rate used N1,332.82 to the US dollar, the market rate on 20 October 2026.

— Still open No date, price or share size has been set for any NNPC or NLNG offer.

Nigeria’s finance minister, Taiwo Oyedele, urged the government on Monday 19 October to list the state oil company NNPC and the gas exporter NLNG. He wants an NNPC listing to help build a US$1 trillion capital market within 10 years, a goal that matters to foreign investors.

Oyedele spoke at the National Capital Market Conference in Abuja, where Vice-President Kashim Shettima launched a 10-year plan to triple the market. The Securities and Exchange Commission, Nigeria’s market regulator, drew up the plan and aims for about N750 trillion (about US$563 billion) by 2036.

What Oyedele Told the Conference

Oyedele, who is also coordinating minister of the economy, asked the federal government on Monday to speed up plans to list selected state-owned companies. He named NNPC and NLNG, TheCable and Vanguard reported.

He said an NNPC listing would improve transparency and broaden public ownership. He compared it with Saudi Aramco, the Saudi state oil giant, and tied the US$1 trillion goal to a US$1 trillion economy by 2030.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What NNPC and NLNG Are

NNPC Limited is Nigeria’s state-owned oil and gas company, led by group chief executive Bashir Bayo Ojulari. President Bola Tinubu said on Thursday 6 August that it could be listed in full, with no date, as the Rio Times reported.

Nigeria LNG Limited, known as NLNG, exports liquefied natural gas, which is gas chilled into a liquid so that ships can carry it. Its website says a seventh production line, Train 7, is expected to lift output by 35%.

The Master Plan Behind the US$1 Trillion Goal

Shettima unveiled the Nigerian Capital Market Master Plan 2.0, a plan for 2026 to 2036 written by the Securities and Exchange Commission. It aims to lift the market from about N250 trillion (about US$188 billion) to N750 trillion (about US$563 billion) by 2036.

Oyedele said Nigeria should aim higher, since US$1 trillion is roughly 1.8 times the commission’s target at the 20 October exchange rate. Emomotimi Agama, the commission’s director-general, promised that every commitment would have “an owner, a timeline and a scorecard”.

Targets Oyedele Set for the Next Decade

Oyedele proposed that listed stocks rise from 33% to at least 60% of gross domestic product, and listed companies from 146 to 250. He also wants retail investors to rise from 6 million to 20 million.

Pension assets would climb from 6% to 16% of GDP, and sukuk, which are Islamic-law bonds, from 0.3% to at least 5% of GDP. He also set a goal of an investment-grade credit rating within three years.

How the Market Has Grown Since 2023

Agama said listed stocks first passed N100 trillion (about US$75 billion) in January and rose above N160 trillion (about US$120 billion) in September. Shettima said the Nigerian Exchange All-Share Index, the main stock gauge, climbed from about 55,000 points in May 2023 to over 260,000.

Oyedele cited Nigeria’s return to the FTSE Russell Frontier Market Index on Monday 21 September and a 7.4% bond weight in a JPMorgan index. The government wants back into JPMorgan’s flagship index and an eventual upgrade to emerging-market status.

What It Means for US Readers

An NNPC listing would let US funds own part of the oil company on the Nigerian Exchange, though no date, price or share size exists. Funds that follow bond indexes buy bonds in proportion to their weights, so the 7.4% share channels money into Nigerian debt.

A separate share sale by the Dangote refinery drew subscribers from more than 90 countries, which shows foreign appetite for Nigerian listings. Tinubu has said NNPC would be reformed first, so any offer would follow that work.

What Is Not Known

Oyedele gave no date, price or share size for an NNPC or NLNG offer, and the government has not set a timetable. NNPC’s chief executive spoke of 2028 in July 2025, yet the government has not adopted that year.

Also open is how the US$1 trillion goal fits the regulator’s N750 trillion (about US$563 billion) target, and whether private firms will list voluntarily. Oyedele said of private companies: “We cannot force them.”

More: Nigeria news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Taiwo Oyedele propose for NNPC and NLNG?

Oyedele, Nigeria’s finance minister, urged the government on Monday 19 October to speed up an NNPC listing on the Nigerian Exchange. He said it would improve transparency and broaden public ownership.

What is the US$1 trillion capital market goal?

Oyedele wants Nigeria’s capital market to reach US$1 trillion within 10 years, to support a US$1 trillion economy by 2030. The regulator’s own plan aims for about N750 trillion (about US$563 billion) by 2036.

Is there a date for an NNPC listing?

No, neither the minister nor the government has set a date, price or share size for an NNPC listing. President Tinubu said on 6 August that NNPC would be reformed before it is listed.

What is NLNG?

Nigeria LNG Limited, or NLNG, exports liquefied natural gas, which is gas chilled into a liquid so that ships can carry it. Its website says a seventh production line is expected to lift output by 35%.

Why does the NNPC listing matter to US investors?

An NNPC listing would let foreign funds buy shares in a large Nigerian energy company on the Nigerian Exchange. It would also add depth to a market that foreign investors have returned to this year.

World.title: Brazil Voter Arrests Ban Starts 20 October
World.content:
Voters queue at a polling station in Gama, Federal District, with a civil police officer on duty, during the 2022 runoff (file photo; Photo: Pedro França/Agência Senado, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTION RULES

Key Facts — The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest economy, holds a presidential runoff on Sunday 25 October 2026 between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro.

— Why it matters The last week of a close race is when arrests, police action and legal fights can shape turnout, so the rules on who may be detained draw attention from investors and visitors.

— Why now The electoral court announced on Tuesday 20 October that the protection for voters starts that day, five days before the vote.

— What happened From 20 October no voter can be arrested or detained except in three cases, and the protection lasts until 48 hours after voting ends.

— The numbers Five days before the vote, 48 hours after it, 15 days for candidates and three legal exceptions, with the first round on 4 October under the same rule.

— What it means for you The rule protects voters, candidates, poll workers and party observers, and the court text does not mention visitors, so it is no general immunity for travellers.

— Still open Whether any arrest is challenged under the rule before the vote, and how the race ends on 25 October.

— Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 77.2% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 22.5% (20 October, 2:39 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 79% and Kalshi at 79% (Lula: 22% and 21% ), as of 20 October, 5:40 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Brazil voter arrests are barred from Tuesday 20 October 2026, five days before the Brazil election 2026 runoff between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and the conservative candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) said. The ban runs until 48 hours after voting ends on Sunday 25 October, so through Tuesday 27 October.

For US investors and travellers watching a race that InfoMoney describes as technically tied, the rule shows which safeguards apply in the final week. Our Brazil election polls tracker, the Brazil election odds page and the Brazil runoff date guide cover the race itself.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.1 %, Lula 48.9 % 29 national polls from 17 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

The TSE published the reminder on 20 October under its countdown headline “Faltam 5 dias”, which means “five days to go”. The same rule applied in the first round on 4 October, as we reported in Brazil Election Rules: Voter Arrest Ban to 6 October, 90% of Machines Ready.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

How the Brazil Voter Arrests Ban Works

The legal basis is Article 236 of the Electoral Code, which bars any authority from arresting or detaining a voter from five days before an election until 48 hours after it ends. From 20 October no voter can be arrested or detained, with three exceptions.

The exceptions are arrest in the act of a crime, known as flagrante delito, a final criminal conviction for a crime that does not allow bail, and breach of a safe-conduct order issued by the Electoral Justice. Agência Senado explains that a safe-conduct protects a voter from threats or coercion.

Anyone who is arrested must be brought immediately before the competent judge, the TSE says. If the judge finds the detention unlawful, the judge must order the release and hold the person who made the arrest accountable.

Agência Senado adds that vote buying and illegal campaigning at polling-place entrances, called “boca de urna”, are examples of electoral crimes that allow an arrest in the act. It traces the protection to Brazil’s first Electoral Code of 1932, written to stop regional political bosses from intimidating voters.

Who Is Covered and Who Is Not

Voters are protected from Tuesday 20 October to Tuesday 27 October, according to Agência Senado’s calendar for the runoff. Candidates have had a longer window since Saturday 10 October, 15 days before the vote, and can be arrested only in the act.

Poll workers, known as mesários, and party observers, known as fiscais, share the protection only while they perform their duties, the TSE says. The Electoral Code still allows their arrest in the act of a crime.

Agência Senado also says a candidate arrested in the act keeps the right to run even if the arrest stands. Losing eligibility requires a conviction by a collegiate court or a final judgment.

The Campaign in Its Final Five Days

InfoMoney reported on 19 October that Lula’s team sees potential in first-round abstainers and in voters over 70, for whom voting is optional. It put first-round abstention at 33.4 million people, or 21.08%, citing the TSE.

Lula was due in São Luís on Tuesday 20 October and in the Petrolina and Juazeiro region, with rallies planned in Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo on Saturday 24 October, InfoMoney said. Flávio is leaning on allied governors such as São Paulo’s Tarcísio de Freitas, visited Marabá and Manaus on Monday 19 October, and has Fortaleza planned and a motorcade in Belo Horizonte on Saturday.

In the first round Flávio took 47.03% of valid votes and Lula 45.16%, a gap of just over two million votes, Correio da Manhã reported on 5 October. InfoMoney lists a TV Globo debate invitation for Friday 23 October, after the Band debate of Sunday 18 October, which we covered in Lula and Flávio Clash in First Runoff Debate.

Other rules also bite this week. The TSE closed poll registration on Monday 19 October, and published polls must state the field period, margin of error, confidence level, number of interviews, who ran and who paid for the poll, and the registration number.

On 19 October the electoral inspector barred Nikolas Ferreira and Marçal from re-posting content the court had banned, and ordered Meta and X to block paid boosting of their accounts until the runoff, as we reported in Court Bars Nikolas and Marçal From Reposting. The TSE also said voters may vote in the runoff even if they skipped the first round.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro a 77.2% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 22.5% (20 October, 2:39 p.m. ET). The Brazil Presidential Election event has drawn about US$189.0 million in bets, with about US$23.4 million on the Flávio contract and US$27.1 million on the Lula contract.

These prices are bets, not polls, and we draw no link between them and the arrest rule. Live prices are on our odds page.

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 78.6% · Lula 21.5% (US$189 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 79% · Lula 21% As of 20 October, 5:40 pm ET (22:40 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

For investors the rule is a legal reminder and not a market event, and nothing in the sources suggests it changes the vote count or the polls. Readers who follow Brazilian assets can use our Brazil power structure guide and our Brazil geopolitics guide to see who holds power after the vote.

For visitors, the TSE text addresses voters, candidates, poll workers and party observers and does not mention foreign travellers, so it should not be read as general immunity. Our Brazil runoff guide for foreign visitors and the São Paulo expat city guide cover practical points for the weekend.

Voting ends at 5 p.m. on Sunday 25 October, and the TSE says only people already in line at that time receive a ticket and may still vote. Seven municipalities also elect mayors on the same day, the TSE said on 17 October.

What Is Not Known

The sources we reviewed report no arrest challenged under the rule and no safe-conduct issued since 20 October. The TSE has not published figures on how many safe-conduct orders exist.

Article 236 and the TSE page give the end of the protection as 48 hours after voting, and we take the date of Tuesday 27 October from Agência Senado. The race itself is open, and InfoMoney calls it technically tied.

Background: Brazil Tax Reform 2026 Replaces Five Taxes With Two VATs.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does the Brazil voter arrests ban start and end?

It starts on Tuesday 20 October 2026, five days before the 25 October runoff, and lasts until 48 hours after voting ends. Agência Senado gives Tuesday 27 October as the last day.

What are the exceptions to the ban?

Voters can still be arrested in the act of a crime, on a final criminal conviction for a crime that does not allow bail, or for breaching a safe-conduct order. A judge must review any arrest immediately.

Can candidates be arrested before the runoff?

Since Saturday 10 October candidates still in the race can be arrested only in the act, under Article 236 of the Electoral Code. Agência Senado says an arrest in the act does not by itself end a candidacy.

Does the ban protect foreign visitors?

The TSE text covers voters, candidates, poll workers and party observers and does not mention visitors. Visitors should therefore not treat it as a general immunity.

When does voting end on 25 October?

Voting ends at 5 p.m., and people already in line at that hour receive a ticket and may still vote, the TSE says. Results are not given on the TSE page we reviewed.

World.title: China Limits Brazil Poultry Ban to 14 Plants
World.content:
A worker in a broiler house at a poultry farm in Campos Novos, Santa Catarina, Brazil (Photo: Deyvid Setti and Eloy Olindo Setti, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · POULTRY TRADE

Key Facts — The country Brazil sells chicken to buyers worldwide, and the outbreak is on a turkey farm in Santa Catarina, in the south.

— Why it matters The size of each ban decides how much Brazilian poultry still reaches world markets, where it competes with American producers.

— Why now A Newcastle disease case on a turkey farm was confirmed on Sunday 18 October 2026, and the trade decisions came on Monday 19 and Tuesday 20 October.

— What happened China will suspend poultry meat from Santa Catarina only, covering 14 plants, while Mexico has suspended poultry products from all of Brazil.

— The numbers The 14 plants are about 23% of the 61 Brazilian plants approved to ship to China, which took about 10% of Brazil’s chicken exports from January to September.

— What it means for you Eating inspected poultry carries no risk to people, and travellers cannot bring poultry products from Brazil into Mexico.

— Still open How long China and Mexico keep their suspensions, and whether any other property near the farm tests positive.

— Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 78% · Lula 21.5% (US$189 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 79% · Lula 21% As of 20 October, 5:00 pm ET (22:00 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

China will suspend poultry meat from Santa Catarina only, which narrows the Brazil poultry ban that traders feared after a Newcastle disease case on a turkey farm. Brazil’s Agriculture Ministry said on Tuesday 20 October 2026 that the Chinese restriction covers one state and not the whole country.

For US readers, the decision matters because China alone took about 420,000 tonnes of Brazilian chicken in the first nine months of 2026, and a narrow ban keeps the bulk of Brazilian supply on a world market where it competes with American producers. Mexico, by contrast, has closed its market to poultry products from all of Brazil, and that measure also covers items that travellers carry.

Brazil Election Data Room Runoff poll average: Flávio Bolsonaro 51.1 %, Lula 48.9 % 28 national polls from 16 pollsters since 4 October, updated hourly. Every poll, free to download. Open the Data Room · Download the CSV · Embed the chart

We reported the outbreak on Monday in Brazil Poultry Exports Face China Halt and the market reaction in Brazil Meat Stock Falls 4% on Bird Disease. Today’s decisions answer the question those pieces left open, which was whether Beijing would act against all of Brazil.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

How the Brazil Poultry Ban Was Narrowed

China told Brazil’s government it will suspend poultry meat only from Santa Catarina, Trade and International Relations Secretary Augusto Billi told CNN Brasil. The ministry had asked, through its embassy in Beijing, for the restriction to cover four municipalities or at most the state.

The embargo affects 14 plants registered with the ministry, out of 61 now approved to export to China. That is about 23% of those plants, by the figures Billi gave.

Billi credited diplomatic talks held with Chinese officials since Sunday 18 October and the experience of an earlier case. He told Globo Rural, in translation, that China “could in fact have decided to close everything, but we managed to change that understanding”.

The ministry’s assessment is that a recent Chinese on-site audit of Brazil’s animal health system gave Beijing the confidence to regionalise the measure. Its own update says the restriction was limited to Santa Catarina after negotiation by the Brazilian government, which avoided a suspension covering the whole country.

Why the 2024 Precedent Matters

In July 2024, after a Newcastle case at Anta Gorda in Rio Grande do Sul, China first blocked imports from the whole country. It took 26 days to narrow that ban to Rio Grande do Sul alone and 17 months to lift it completely, Billi said.

This time the restriction was regional from the start, so plants outside Santa Catarina avoid that wait. Brazil had stopped certifying poultry products for China from Monday 19 October as a precaution, and Globo Rural reported that companies elsewhere in the country can now resume sales.

For some destinations, the cut-off for certification is 21 September, the day samples were taken at the farm. Cargoes produced after that date cannot be certified for those markets, Globo Rural reported.

What Mexico’s Nationwide Stop Covers

Mexico’s animal health agency Senasica suspended imports of poultry products from all of Brazil, saying the aim is to protect its own flocks because Mexico is free of Newcastle disease. The ministry’s list covers live birds, poultry meat and offal, fertile eggs, chicks up to three days old, and songbirds, ornamental birds and birds of prey sold commercially.

The Mexican measure also covers pet birds and goods that tourists carry, Globo Rural reported. Billi said the decision follows the bilateral health protocol, and Brazil will now negotiate to narrow it to the state, a municipality or the affected area.

Chile has also suspended imports from Santa Catarina only, including fresh poultry meat, table eggs and day-old chicks, the ministry said. The ministry is monitoring the other markets and says it will publish new information as it is confirmed.

What Is Happening on the Farm

The affected farm in Nova Itaberaba holds 6,526 birds, and Brazil’s report to the World Organisation for Animal Health lists 26 cases and no deaths. The birds showed no clinical signs, screening samples taken on 21 September tested positive on 14 October, and a federal laboratory in São Paulo confirmed the virus on 18 October.

The animals are to be culled this week, followed by cleaning and disinfection, Billi said. If no new outbreak appears, Brazil could apply in 90 days to be recognised as free of the disease.

Monitoring covers about 133 properties in Nova Itaberaba and the neighbouring towns of Coronel Freitas, Nova Erechim and Águas Frias. The ministry says the birds stayed on the farm and were not destined for meat production.

What It Means for You

Agriculture Minister André de Paula said on Monday that eating poultry that has passed official inspection carries no risk to people. Newcastle disease is a bird illness, so the trade decisions concern animal health and market access rather than food safety.

For traders, the narrow Chinese scope limits the volume at risk, while Mexico’s nationwide stop is the larger open question. Safras & Mercado analyst Fernando Iglesias estimated losses could reach US$139 million if China and Mexico kept their suspensions as long as in 2024, though regional limits on China could reduce that.

Iglesias expects most restrictions to be reversed between mid and late November. He also said output that cannot leave Santa Catarina could shift to plants in Paraná and Rio Grande do Sul, and that the expected return of Brazilian chicken to the European Union in mid-November should stay on track.

Travellers should not carry poultry products or pet birds from Brazil into Mexico while the measure lasts. Our guides Brazil Geopolitics Explained 2026 and Brazil’s Role in Latin America Explained 2026 set out Brazil’s trade weight, and our Florianópolis expat city guide covers life in Santa Catarina.

What Is Not Known

Neither China nor Mexico has given a date for lifting its measure, and the sources reviewed do not say how long either will last. The Chinese decision is described here through Brazilian officials, and the Chinese customs notice itself was not seen.

It is not known how the virus reached the turkey farm, or whether other properties nearby are infected. The sources reviewed report no results yet from the monitoring of about 133 properties.

The ministry’s update names Mexico, China and Chile as the markets with restrictions so far. Analysts say Brazil has also paused its own certification for China and Malaysia, but no wider list has been confirmed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is China banning all Brazilian poultry?

No, China will suspend poultry meat from Santa Catarina only, according to Brazil’s Agriculture Ministry. The embargo covers 14 of the 61 Brazilian plants approved to ship to China.

What has Mexico done about Brazilian poultry?

Mexico has suspended imports of poultry products from all of Brazil, including meat, fertile eggs and live birds. Brazil will now negotiate to narrow the measure to the affected area.

Is Brazilian chicken safe to eat?

The ministry says eating poultry that has passed official inspection carries no risk to people. The infected birds stayed on the farm and were not destined for meat production.

What is Newcastle disease?

It is a contagious viral illness of birds that affects their breathing, nerves and digestion. Brazil confirmed it on a turkey farm in Nova Itaberaba, Santa Catarina, on 18 October 2026.

How long could the Brazil poultry ban last?

No date has been set by China or Mexico. After the 2024 case it took China 26 days to narrow its ban and 17 months to lift it completely.

Sources: Brazil Agriculture Ministry, update on export restrictions, 20 October 2026; Brazil Agriculture Ministry, press conference of 19 October 2026; CNN Brasil, 20 October 2026; Globo Rural, 20 October 2026; Globo Rural on Mexico, 20 October 2026; CNN Brasil on the Safras & Mercado estimate, 20 October 2026.

KENYA · MOBILE MONEY

Key Facts — The country Kenya is an East African nation led by President William Ruto and the home of M-Pesa, a mobile wallet millions use instead of bank accounts.

— What happened Safaricom, Kenya’s largest mobile operator, has sent money left on old, recycled lines to owners’ current numbers since Thursday 23 July 2026.

— How it works The system matches the ID or passport behind an old line to an active line and moves the balance there. No form is needed.

— The amounts One customer received KSh25 (about US$0.19), while some others got thousands of shillings, according to Kenyan outlets.

— The owner Vodacom, the South African group, holds 55% of Safaricom and keeps it while a court appeal runs.

— What it means for you Visitors who once used a Kenyan SIM may find a small balance returning to a new line under the same passport.

— Still open Safaricom has not said how much money sits in archived accounts or how many customers have been paid.

Safaricom refunds are reaching customers in Kenya who left M-Pesa money on phone lines they later stopped using. Kenya’s largest mobile operator began moving those forgotten balances automatically to owners’ current lines, Kenyan outlets reported from Thursday 23 July 2026.

For US travellers, expats and investors, the Safaricom refunds show how the company behind a famous mobile-money service treats customer cash. The money is matched by national ID or passport, so anyone who held a Kenyan SIM under a passport may be affected.

Why Old M-Pesa Money Is Coming Back

Safaricom switches off a SIM card that goes unused for a long time, and the number can then be sold to a new customer. Tuko, a Kenyan news site, reported on Friday 24 July that this happens after more than six months without airtime.

Any M-Pesa money left on that line is not handed to the new owner. Safaricom refunds it automatically from a store kept under the identity document of the first owner.

How Safaricom Refunds Work

When a person registers a new active line with the same ID or passport, the system moves the stored balance there. HapaKenya, a Kenyan technology site, reported on Wednesday 29 July that no form or request is needed.

A text message says the money came from M-PESA Archived Funds, and the cash can be spent like any other balance. Safaricom told customers that a refund does not mean their current line will be closed.

The Small Message That Sparked Questions

A customer who posts as Blessed Morgan asked Safaricom online why he received KSh25 (about US$0.19) from his old number on 23 July. The Kenya Times reported that Safaricom answered that the money sat on a previous line under his ID.

Tuko reported that for some customers the credits reached thousands of shillings, and People Daily cited one user who saw KSh2,500 (about US$19) arrive. Safaricom explained the credits in replies to customers on social media.

What Happens to Money Nobody Claims

According to Tuko, an owner can still reclaim archived money after proving identity, and the funds do not become Safaricom’s property. After two years unclaimed, they pass to the Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority, the Kenyan state body that holds such money for owners.

HapaKenya advised customers who suspect they left money on an old line to ask Safaricom customer support for a manual balance check. The agent will ask for the original national ID number to confirm ownership of the dormant line.

Who Owns Safaricom Today

Vodacom, the South African mobile group led by Shameel Joosub, keeps its 55% stake while an appeal continues, Business Daily reported on Tuesday 20 October. A High Court ruling had struck down its purchase of an extra 20% stake.

The Rio Times report on the Safaricom appeal explains the court fight in detail. Safaricom has also made M-Pesa payments of up to US$3.85 to business tills free since 7 August, as the report on M-Pesa business payments shows.

What It Means for US Readers

Safaricom refunds may reach Americans who left small balances on a passport-registered SIM, once a new line is registered in the same name. The Rio Times guide to SIM cards and internet in Kenya for foreigners explains how to register a line.

For investors, the Safaricom refunds show the company returning customer money even as the fight over its ownership goes through the courts. The company is profiled on the Rio Times Safaricom page.

What Is Not Known

Safaricom has not published the total value of archived balances or how many customers have had Safaricom refunds. It has also not said whether the transfers will continue on a fixed schedule.

It is open how customers without a current Safaricom line can claim their money, and whether foreign passport holders face extra checks. Owners who are unsure should ask Safaricom directly.

More: Kenya news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are M-PESA Archived Funds?

They are balances left on old Safaricom lines that were switched off after long inactivity. Safaricom stores the money under the original owner’s ID and sends it to a current line registered under the same document.

Do I need to apply for the refund?

No. HapaKenya reported that Safaricom refunds reach matching customers automatically, with a confirmation text message. Anyone who thinks money is missing can ask Safaricom customer support for a balance check.

Does a refund mean my current line will be closed?

No. Safaricom told customers on social media that the credit is only a correction of an old balance. It has no effect on a line that is in use.

How much money can customers get?

Amounts vary with what was left on the old line. One customer received KSh25 (about US$0.19), and Tuko reported that some received thousands of shillings.

What happens if nobody claims the money?

Tuko reported that funds unclaimed for two years go to the Unclaimed Financial Assets Authority in Kenya. They do not become Safaricom’s property and the owner can still claim them there.

World.title: Tech Group Datatec Core Earnings Seen Up 53%
World.content:
Datatec core earnings per share should rise 52.9% to 60.6% in the half-year to August, the Johannesburg tech group told investors on 20 October.

SOUTH AFRICA · BUSINESS

Key Facts — The country South Africa is a middle-income economy at Africa’s southern tip. Datatec, a Johannesburg-listed technology group, sells and runs networking and security systems in over 50 countries.

— What happened On Tuesday 20 October 2026 Datatec said its core earnings per share for the six months to 31 August should rise 52.9% to 60.6%.

— The three measures Datatec core earnings are forecast at 29.5 to 31.0 US cents a share, but headline earnings at only 22.1 to 23.6 cents.

— The drivers Both main divisions, Westcon and Logicalis International, posted record first-half adjusted EBITDA, with an exceptional performance in the United States at Logicalis.

— The shares Datatec shares traded 2.5% higher at R57.44 (about US$3.50) in mid-morning trade in Johannesburg on Tuesday.

— What it means for you Datatec also trades in the US on the OTCQX market as DTTLF, and its US unit is a named driver.

— Still open Revenue, profit in dollars and any interim dividend come with the full results, due on or about Thursday 29 October 2026.

Datatec core earnings per share will rise 52.9% to 60.6% in the six months to 31 August 2026, the company said on Tuesday 20 October. Datatec is a Johannesburg-listed technology group whose Westcon and Logicalis arms sell and run networking, security and cloud systems for business customers worldwide.

Headline earnings, the measure South African listing rules require, will rise only 0.5% to 7.3%. For US readers, one named driver of the stronger operating result is the United States, where Logicalis reported an exceptional performance.

What Datatec Told Investors

Datatec published a trading statement through the news service of the JSE, South Africa’s main stock exchange, on Tuesday 20 October. The exchange’s rules require such a statement once a company is reasonably certain that results will differ by at least 20% from the year before.

Datatec core earnings, which the company calls underlying earnings, are forecast at 29.5 to 31.0 US cents a share, against 19.3 a year earlier. Headline earnings should reach 22.1 to 23.6 US cents against 22.0, and basic earnings 22.8 to 24.3 cents against 21.7.

Why Core Earnings Rise Faster Than Headline

Datatec core earnings leave out items such as share-based pay, amortisation of acquired businesses and deal costs. Headline earnings follow a listing-rule definition that keeps several of those costs in, so the two figures can move apart.

Datatec will publish its full interim results on or about Thursday 29 October 2026, with revenue and profit in dollars. The forecasts in the statement have not been reviewed or reported on by the group’s external auditors.

What Drove the Divisions

Westcon International, the group’s distribution arm for security and networking products, kept up strong growth and posted a record first half at adjusted EBITDA level. Adjusted EBITDA is operating profit before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, with share-based pay, restructuring and deal costs removed.

Logicalis International, which designs and runs IT systems for companies, also posted a record first half and turned more gross profit into EBITDA. Datatec credited an exceptional performance in the United States.

Latin America and a New US Deal

Logicalis Latin America had another weak operating performance as it cuts its reliance on a few telecommunications customers. Even so, recoverable tax credits boosted its bottom line significantly.

Logicalis USA bought Loial, a New Mexico cybersecurity firm, with effect from 31 July 2026, according to a Datatec filing. Business Day counted it as the group’s fourth acquisition this year.

How the Shares and the Special Payout Fit

Datatec shares were up 2.5% at R57.44 (about US$3.50) at 9.55 a.m. on Tuesday after touching R58.27 (about US$3.55), Business Day reported. Rand figures here use 16.43 rand to the US dollar, the rate of 20 October 2026.

The price follows a one-off payout, because the shares traded without a special dividend of R29 (about US$1.77) a share from Wednesday 14 October. The dividend totalled R7.05 billion (about US$435 million, the company’s figure) and was paid on Monday 19 October.

Holders of 78,585,515 shares took the cash, R2.28 billion (about US$139 million), while 94,324,733 new shares went to those who chose scrip. A scrip distribution gives shareholders new shares in place of cash.

The payout followed a deal that closed on 4 August, when funds linked to General Atlantic, a US private equity firm, refinanced Westcon. Business Day reported that General Atlantic provided a six-year loan of US$375 million and took a 5% stake for US$25 million.

What It Means for US Readers

The United States is a named driver, since Logicalis USA had an exceptional performance and added a New Mexico cybersecurity firm in July. Datatec shares also trade on the US OTCQX market as DTTLF, and earnings are reported in US cents.

General Atlantic now backs Westcon, the arm that Datatec says kept up strong growth, so American private capital sits inside the group. See the earlier Rio Times report on the Datatec special dividend and the Datatec company profile.

What Is Not Known

The statement gives no revenue, no profit in dollars and no dividend, and those figures arrive only with the interim results. It does not say how much each division earned or how large the Latin American tax credits were.

The Public Investment Corporation, which manages South African public-sector pension money, told Datatec on Monday 19 October that it sold shares and now holds 12.71%. The size and price of that sale, and any link to the payout, are not disclosed.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Datatec announce on 20 October?

Datatec core earnings per share for the six months to 31 August 2026 should be 29.5 to 31.0 US cents, up 52.9% to 60.6%. Headline earnings are forecast up 0.5% to 7.3%.

Why are Datatec core earnings rising faster than headline earnings?

Datatec core earnings leave out items such as share-based pay, amortisation of acquired businesses and deal costs. Headline earnings keep several of those costs in, so the two measures can diverge.

When will Datatec publish its full half-year results?

Datatec expects to release interim results on or about Thursday 29 October 2026. The forecasts in its trading statement have not been reviewed by its auditors.

Can US investors buy Datatec shares?

Datatec is listed on the JSE in Johannesburg and also trades on the US OTCQX market under the symbol DTTLF. The shares carry currency risk because Datatec reports in US dollars while its main listing trades in rand.

What was the special dividend Datatec paid this month?

Datatec paid a special dividend of R29 (about US$1.77) a share on Monday 19 October, worth R7.05 billion (about US$435 million) in total. Shareholders could take new shares instead of cash.

World.title: Puerto Rico New Fortress Claim Hits US$100M
World.content:
Power lines and a broken pole after Hurricane Maria in Puerto Rico, September 2017. File photo, not from this story. (Photo: SSgt. Michelle Y. Alvarez-Rea, US Air Force, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

PUERTO RICO · ENERGY

Key Facts — The country Puerto Rico is a US territory whose residents are US citizens, and its public power company is known as PREPA, while Genera PR runs the public power plants and LUMA Energy runs the transmission and distribution lines.

— Why it matters The court fight will help decide whether about US$100 million of costly diesel ends up on the power bills of US citizens on the island or on a gas supplier.

— Why now On Monday 19 October 2026 the head of the contract administrator told a House committee that the claim now stands near US$100 million, and on Tuesday 20 October the energy regulator said customers have paid none of it.

— What happened The government amended its federal lawsuit against NFEnergia LLC, a subsidiary of New Fortress Energy, over diesel burned when the company did not deliver liquefied natural gas.

— The numbers Power now costs about 33.86 cents per kilowatt-hour after a rise of roughly five cents in October, and a separate September fuel shortfall of US$48 million to US$54.3 million awaits the regulator.

— What it means for you Hotels, restaurants and shops on the island pay the new rate this quarter, and the regulator has not said when it will rule on the shortfall.

— Still open Whether a federal judge holds New Fortress responsible, and whether the regulator adds any fuel shortfall to bills from November or from January.

Puerto Rico has raised its New Fortress claim to about US$100 million, the head of the island’s gas contract administrator told a House committee on Monday 19 October 2026. The claim covers diesel burned when the company did not deliver the liquefied natural gas (LNG) for San Juan’s power units, and the energy regulator says customers have paid none of it so far.

For US readers the case tests who pays when a private fuel supplier fails a US territory, because the dispute sits before a US federal court and officials say recent events were also referred to federal prosecutors. Puerto Rico’s residents are US citizens, so the result will reach the power bills of American households and businesses on the island.

We covered the opening of the fight in Puerto Rico Pays US$1.25 Million a Day for Gas Delay. The new figure, officials say, adds up every occasion on which gas failed to arrive.

How the New Fortress Claim Grew to US$100 Million

Osvaldo Carlo Linares, who heads the Third-Party Procurement Office (3PPO) that administers the gas contract on behalf of Genera PR, the operator of the public power plants, said an amended complaint was being filed that day. He called the figure of about US$100 million the estimate used for the filing, and said it covers every incident in which missing gas forced the island to burn costlier fuel.

The earlier claim was filed in June and stood at US$55.3 million in El Vocero’s account, while NotiCel put it at about US$58 million. El Vocero said the new filing adds more than US$40 million, and NotiCel said recent costs account for more than US$30 million, so the total is an estimate and not an audited sum.

El Vocero said the first claim covered diesel burned at units 5 and 6 of the San Juan combined-cycle plant and at temporary units at Palo Seco. Carlo Linares put diesel at three to four times the price of gas, which is why each gap in supply costs so much.

Download the PDF checklist

Why Customers Have Not Paid Yet

Energy Bureau president Edison Avilés Deliz said on Tuesday 20 October, according to NotiCel, that “consumers to date have not paid a single cent” of the claim. At the hearing on 19 October he said the Bureau had kept about US$58 million out of the fuel reconciliation, and later a further US$17 million, while the contract dispute is examined, and that this pause was not an order to stop paying the supplier.

Avilés Deliz told the House committee that the government must win in court to avoid another rise in the power bill. He said the issue is bigger than whether bills rise, because the system faces a liquidity gap of US$100 million, and Carlo Linares estimated that the case could take one to two years.

The Gas Dispute Behind the Claim

According to the government, New Fortress stopped supplying gas to units 5 and 6 of the San Juan plant on 16 September, and the units have burned diesel since. On Monday 28 September Governor Jenniffer González Colón ordered a lawsuit in the US District Court for Puerto Rico to force the company to open its terminal to a replacement supplier under a clause known as tolling.

On Tuesday 13 October the tanker Amur River reached the company’s San Juan terminal, and Judge María Antongiorgi Jordán denied the power company’s request for a preliminary order. She told it to show cause by 19 October why the case was not moot, and 3PPO now asks for a declaratory judgment on how the clause must work in future outages.

New Fortress did not attend the House hearing on 19 October and excused its summoned executive, who was in New York. Committee chairman José Hernández Concepción said he will issue a new summons with a contempt warning.

In a written statement quoted by El Vocero the company said it has acted in line with its contractual obligations and that any government decision will rest on the contracts and the law. El Nuevo Día reported that the company denies breaching the contract and blames problems on ship access to San Juan Bay, and the claims against it remain allegations that a court has not decided.

Power Rates and the Next Fuel Adjustment

The Energy Bureau approved a rise of 5.28 cents per kilowatt-hour in the fuel and purchased-power charges on Wednesday 30 September, according to El Vocero. Primera Hora put the total rate at 33.86 cents per kilowatt-hour, and the firm Inteligencia Económica estimated the quarter’s extra cost at US$218 million across households, businesses and government.

LUMA Energy told the Bureau in a recent filing that September fuel costs ran above what rates collected, a gap Primera Hora put at US$48 million and El Vocero at US$54.3 million. On Tuesday 20 October the governor called a possible new rise “an outrage” and blamed LUMA, while a LUMA spokesman said the company only passes on the report because generators’ fuel spending exceeded budget, and that LUMA does not use the fuel.

Avilés Deliz said the shortfall must first be studied and gave no date for a decision. The sources reviewed do not say whether this shortfall and the US$100 million claim overlap.

What It Means for You

Visitors and residents pay the October rate already, and a further adjustment is possible but not decided, so the next bills depend on a regulatory ruling with no date. Our guides Puerto Rico Explained for Americans and Puerto Rico Geopolitics Explained 2026 set out how the island’s status shapes decisions like this one.

Inteligencia Económica warned that about 12,000 small firms could close if power stays above 30 cents per kilowatt-hour for two quarters, and said a mid-sized supermarket could pay about US$5,250 more per month. The firm’s figures are its own scenarios, and our earlier report Puerto Rico Natural Gas Dispute Could Add US$48 a Month to Power Bills looked at the household bill.

For investors, the outcome matters for a gas supplier that holds a long contract and a terminal in San Juan. Carlo Linares said that if the government wins it could ask the federal court to seize New Fortress equipment at the Puerto Nuevo terminal, some of it worth up to US$500 million.

What Is Not Known

The amended complaint itself could not be opened for this article, so the US$100 million figure rests on officials’ statements at the hearing as reported by El Vocero and NotiCel. The two outlets differ on the earlier claim and on the size of the increase, and neither gives a court docket number.

It is not known whether the diesel claim and the US$48 million to US$54.3 million shortfall overlap, or when the Bureau will rule on the shortfall. The sources reviewed also do not show when the court will schedule the next step or how New Fortress answers the new figure.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the New Fortress claim in Puerto Rico?

Puerto Rico says New Fortress owes it about US$100 million for diesel burned when gas was not delivered. The figure is an estimate given at a House hearing on 19 October 2026.

Have Puerto Rico customers paid the claim?

The Energy Bureau president said on 20 October that customers have not paid a single cent. He said the amounts stay out of rates while the courts decide who is responsible.

What does New Fortress say about the dispute?

The company says it has acted in line with its contractual obligations and wants a reliable supply. It did not attend the 19 October hearing, and the government’s accusations remain unproven in court.

Could Puerto Rico power bills rise again?

A request from LUMA about a September fuel shortfall of US$48 million to US$54.3 million is before the Energy Bureau. The Bureau president said it must first be studied, and no decision or date exists.

Why does this matter to US readers?

Puerto Rico is a US territory and the case is in a US federal court, with a referral to federal prosecutors reported. The outcome shapes power costs for US citizens, businesses and visitors on the island.

ETHIOPIA · TELECOMS

Key Facts — The country Ethiopia is a landlocked East African nation of more than 120 million people, led by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. Its capital, Addis Ababa, is home to the African Union.

— What happened The board named Tariku Demissie acting chief executive on Sunday 18 October, The Reporter, an Addis Ababa paper, said. He replaces Frehiwot Tamiru, who led the firm for eight years.

— Why the change Parliament approved Frehiwot Tamiru as Minister of Innovation and Technology on Thursday 8 October, in a wider cabinet reshuffle by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.

— Who is Tariku Tariku Demissie is a senior technology executive at the company who earlier served as chief infrastructure officer, according to The Reporter.

— The numbers In the year to June 2026, Ethio Telecom’s revenue was about 216 billion birr (about US$1.33 billion), and operating profit reached 92.9 billion birr (about US$574 million), up 47.5%.

— Who is Ethio Telecom Ethio Telecom is Ethiopia’s state-controlled telecom operator, with roughly 90 million customers. It also runs telebirr, the mobile money service used by 60.6 million people.

— Still open The board has not said how long the acting period lasts or when a permanent chief executive will be chosen.

Ethio Telecom, Ethiopia’s state-controlled mobile and internet operator, has a new acting CEO. Its board of directors named Tariku Demissie to the post on Sunday 18 October, The Reporter newspaper in Addis Ababa said.

The Ethio Telecom acting CEO takes over from Frehiwot Tamiru, who ran the company for eight years before joining the cabinet. For US investors and aid agencies, the company is Ethiopia’s biggest digital gateway, with about US$1.33 billion in yearly revenue.

Who Is Tariku Demissie

Tariku Demissie comes from inside the company, where The Reporter says he served as chief infrastructure officer. A conference biography lists him as chief technology officer, responsible for network and systems operations.

His background is in building and running networks rather than in finance or sales. That fits a company that still has to extend 4G and 5G across a country of more than 120 million people.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Frehiwot Tamiru Left

Frehiwot Tamiru had led Ethio Telecom since 2018, when she became chief executive. Parliament approved her as Minister of Innovation and Technology on Thursday 8 October.

Her move came in a cabinet reshuffle by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, which the Rio Times described in its report on the new cabinet. The company made no public statement about a successor in the first days after her appointment.

What the Company Earns

In the year to June 2026, revenue was about 216 billion birr (about US$1.33 billion), over a third higher, The Reporter said. Operating profit rose 47.5% to 92.9 billion birr (about US$574 million), and core earnings hit 113.1 billion birr (about US$699 million).

Data and internet services made up 31.1% of revenue, overtaking mobile voice at 23.5%. The figures use the central rate of 161.8 birr to the US dollar on 20 October 2026.

Telebirr and the Customer Base

Telebirr, the company’s mobile money service, reached 60.6 million customers after adding 8.54 million in the year, The Reporter said. It handled 2.61 billion transactions, up 145.3%.

Active mobile data users rose 10.7% to 51.53 million. Total customers are about 90 million, and the company’s plan aims for 100 million by 2027-28, according to Senegal’s Osiris news site.

The Competition and the Shareholders

Safaricom Ethiopia, the private rival run by Kenya’s Safaricom, had about 14.8 million customers in mid-2026, according to the research firm Omdia. Its roughly 87 million mobile subscribers still dwarf that figure.

Small shareholders have been waiting for their first payout, which the company promised in the Ethio Telecom dividend report of September. A new chief executive will have to deliver it and hold the growth rate.

What It Means for US Readers

This is the largest telecom operator in Ethiopia, a market of more than 120 million people where foreign technology and payment firms want to grow. A change at the top can shift deals on 5G and mobile payments.

Investors in Ethiopia watch the company because it earns foreign currency from roaming and wholesale deals. It earned US$188.48 million in foreign currency in the year to June 2026, The Reporter said.

What Is Not Known

The board has not said how long Tariku Demissie will serve as acting chief executive. It is also open whether he will be confirmed in the post or replaced.

No announcement has covered changes in the management team or the 100 million customer target. The timing of the first dividend is also open.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is the new acting chief executive?

Tariku Demissie, a senior technology executive at the company, was named by its board of directors on Sunday 18 October. The Reporter said he previously served as chief infrastructure officer.

Why did the old Ethio Telecom chief leave?

Frehiwot Tamiru was approved by parliament as Minister of Innovation and Technology on Thursday 8 October. She had run the company for eight years.

How much does the operator earn?

Revenue for the year to June 2026 was about 216 billion birr (about US$1.33 billion). Operating profit was 92.9 billion birr (about US$574 million).

What is telebirr?

Telebirr is the operator’s mobile money service, which lets people send money and pay bills by phone. It had 60.6 million customers in the year to June 2026.

Is the acting chief executive permanent?

No, the post is acting, and the board has not said when a permanent chief executive will be chosen.
