World.title: Jaime Salmoreno, exarquitecto, cura y cantante: “No me importa el éxito. Para San Bartolomé, su mayor triunfo fue ser despellejado vivo”
World.content:
Para aquellos a quienes les tocó ir de pequeños a colegios religiosos, el auge del pop cristiano puede resultar desconcertante. Cualquiera diría que canciones como Alabaré, alabaré o Vamos a la casa del Señor ya encarnaban la refinación máxima de esta disciplina, con melodías pegajosas, letras machaconas y una fuerte resistencia a abandonar la cabeza del oyente que se somete a ellas. Pero el canon sigue abierto. El padre Jaime Salmoreno (Alcalá de Henares, Madrid, 45 años), cuyo nombre artístico combina los apellidos Salido Moreno, es el último grito en un género que vive un momento comercial extático. Hakuna Music Group –los predicadores del movimiento Hakuna, fundado por un sacerdote del Opus Dei– congregaron a 15.000 almas en su última actuación en el Palacio de Deportes de Madrid. Íñigo Quintero, también vinculado al Opus, sorprendió al colocar una canción de ambiguo mensaje evangélico en el número uno mundial de Spotify. Y los vallisoletanos Siloé llamaron la atención de nada menos que Coldplay, que compartió su música en redes.

“Ciertamente, esto no se ha dado antes”, dice el sacerdote a ICON. “De un tiempo a esta parte, han sido llamadas o vocacionadas personas con talento, de modo que ha surgido la posibilidad de invertir un poco más en la música no solo cristiana, sino católica. También entiendo que ahora, con las redes sociales, las generaciones actuales están perdiendo el miedo a expresarse sin complejos”. Salmoreno acumula más de 50.000 oyentes mensuales en streaming y sus canciones también reúnen fans en TikTok. El pasado junio actuó junto a Fito Robles, cantante de Siloé, en la vigilia de jóvenes con el papa León XIV, en Madrid. El himno de la visita del pontífice, Alza la mirada, también contó con su rúbrica, junto a otros compositores. Por su manera de entonar, Jaime Salmoreno suena como una especie de versión católica de Astrud, con arreglos más austeros y letras, no en vano, frecuentemente autoconfesionales. “Igual que cuando alguien llega a un confesionario y a mí se me transmite un dolor, una alegría o una duda, la música es una forma del artista de confesarse con su público. Transmite una emoción. Eso es lo que yo hago. A veces expreso cosas mías y, otras veces, cosas que son de otros, pero con las cuales empatizo”.

El padre Jaime Salmoreno posa para ICON en la parroquia de Santiago Apóstol, en Torrejón de Ardoz. Pablo Monge

Salmoreno oficia en la parroquia de Santiago Apóstol, en Torrejón de Ardoz. No nota mayor afluencia desde que su popularidad excede los límites terrenales de la casa del Señor. “Si tienen curiosidad, prefiero que la gente venga a ver a Dios, no a mí”. Desdeña la fama por la fama: rechazó “hasta tres veces” (las mismas que Pedro a Jesús) ir a La Voz, el concurso de talentos de Telecinco, donde en su día concurrió el expadre Damián. La atención le sobrevino en 2024 por un vídeo que tampoco subió él. “Hicimos una peregrinación a Fátima, en Portugal. Cerquita está Nazaré, donde hay un santuario mariano con unas vistas muy bonitas y allí un hombre estaba haciendo con la guitarra una versión de I’m yours”, explica, deteniéndose brevemente a entonar el estribillo. “Nos encantó cómo cantaba el chico. Atraído, busqué cantar con él e hicimos un par de canciones, entre ellas Shallow”. Con el cura encargándose de las voces de Lady Gaga –que la interpretaba a dueto con Bradley Cooper en Ha nacido una estrella (2018)–, la actuación fue grabada por un parroquiano y Salmoreno la reenvió a su familia. “Dos meses después, me llamó un productor de Mediaset, al que había llegado el vídeo después de que mi madre lo subiera al Facebook. Me dijo que no quería desaprovechar ese talento, que si podía avisar a unos amigos suyos de una productora”.

Así, el sacerdote forma ahora parte del catálogo de 33 Producciones, donde comparte plantel con Jedet o Carlos Baute. No tiene inconveniente con la música secular. “Nada de lo que hay en el hombre le es ajeno a Dios, excepto el mal, que es incompatible con él”, resume. Entre lo que no es ajeno a Salmoreno, el cura enumera el jazz, el pop anglosajón, el góspel o “las baladas de los cantantes heavies”. “Mi forma de cantar está vinculada a esta música y cantantes que me gustan. Whitney Houston me parece sobrehumana. Me gustaban los arreglos que hacía Madonna en sus canciones, cómo se fue actualizando, o Björk, por decir algo más raro. De españoles, unos años atrás me gustaba mucho Pablo López, Malú… Joaquín Sabina hace letras como nadie. Me gusta el deje de Vanesa Martín, igual que la de los girasoles, ¿cómo se llamaba? ¡Rozalén! Compone de maravilla esa mujer”. El cóctel de influencias, a la espera de que el clérigo complete su primer trabajo para el sello, ya se ha plasmado en dos sencillos, Todo tuyo y Tú eres la luz, ambos grabados en español e inglés.

Antes, el cura tenía editados dos álbumes. El primero, Confidencias, contradicciones y conversión (2012), previo a ser ordenado sacerdote, funcionaba como un disco conceptual sobre su descubrimiento de la fe. Salmoreno, antes de sentir la llamada de Dios (si bien creyente desde pequeño), era un arquitecto con una flamante carrera en EE UU, residiendo en una esquina de Central Park, en Nueva York. “He tenido siempre mucha suerte, porque generalmente he estado en el sitio adecuado y en el lugar adecuado para acabar consiguiendo mis sueños. Pero tenía una sed mayor que el beneficio que ese sueño reportaba”, describe. Entre los trabajos realizados al otro lado del Atlántico, recuerda el proyecto de un dúplex en lo alto de la Torre Trump, “probablemente para él”, o una tienda de skaters en Broadway. Encontró un estudio que quiso hacerle socio y tramitarle la ciudadanía, con vistas a asumir encargos de China o Emiratos Árabes. “Aun así, yo tenía el síndrome del impostor. Me enfadé un poco con Dios, por estar poniendo en mi corazón una sed que yo no podía saciar. Pensé que a lo mejor Dios podía ser egoísta conmigo, dándome una sed mayor de lo que mis méritos podían lograr, e intenté tener una crisis de fe. No era una crisis de fe como tal, yo tenía conciencia de su existencia a nivel intelectual, moral y afectivo, pero me enfadaba su decisión, me enfadaba que no concordara con mi deseo. Sin embargo, la vida sin Él resultaba un fracaso, una mentira. La vida no era suficiente para mí”.

El punto de inflexión llegó alrededor de una juerga. “Era un fiestón como los de las películas, en lo alto de una torre en Tribeca, donde todo el mundo iba muy bien vestido, todos eran guapos. Estar ahí era el colofón de las cosas que había soñado, la cima del éxito al que un chico de veintitantos puede aspirar. Me acuerdo de cuando volvía de esa fiesta en taxi, que me decía: ‘Bueno, pues esto es, ¿ahora qué?’. La cuestión es que estaba cerca el Miércoles de Ceniza [primer día de la Cuaresma cristiana, que culmina en la Semana Santa]. No me dio tiempo de ir, así que el jueves me acerqué a una iglesia del Upper West Side, donde había cuatro personas. Comparado con la fiesta, ¡vaya fracaso!”, lamenta. “Entonces mi cara me topó con el sagrario, el lugar de la presencia de la Eucaristía [las hostias consagradas]. Cuando volví la cara, tuve una certeza clara que me sorprendió: ‘Donde estoy yo, está tu casa”, rememora, con ojos vidriosos. “Había una frase de Jesús que a mí me quemaba por dentro: ‘¿De qué te sirve ganar el mundo si pierdes la vida?’. Volví a España, probé a entrar al seminario y empecé a entender muchas cosas de mí mismo, de mi personalidad, de mi forma de querer, de cómo muestro y vivo mis afectos”.

Rezos, vino y rock & roll

La decisión del padre Salmoreno, dice, sorprendió a algunos amigos y a otros no. “Al final, tenía muchos círculos distintos. La mayoría de la gente de Arquitectura no eran creyentes. Luego estaban los de la parroquia, mis amigos de Sevilla, los del instituto o la gente del kárate”. Lo más duro para el párroco fue el proceso con sus progenitores. “Unos padres no solamente tienen a sus hijos, también viven sus ilusiones a través de ellos. Y yo las estaba satisfaciendo. Mi padre quería haber sido arquitecto, con lo cual mi triunfo era su triunfo, estaban orgullosos. No obstante, aunque ellos eran creyentes, no entendían aquello que estaba sucediendo, les parecía una locura. Yo tenía claro que el Señor iba a llevar esto por buen puerto, pero en ese momento estaba destrozado, mis hermanos decían: ‘Estás matando a nuestros padres”.

Felizmente para la familia y el sacerdote cantante, todo se fue pacificando. “No fue inmediato, ni mucho menos. Pero la relación que tengo ahora con mis padres no la cambiaría por nada”. Como alguien desenmascarado, asegura que sus relaciones son más veraces, que ha dejado de sentirse “impostor”. Sobre si la música es una vocación equiparable a la espiritual, Salmoreno admite que ya estaba ahí. Se recuerda siendo eurofán con su hermano. También, antes de su sacerdocio y de emprender una carrera musical en solitario, militó en otra banda religiosa de rock de Alcalá de Henares, La Voz del Desierto. ¿Cómo es un cisma en el contexto musical cristiano? ¿El que quiere irse clava una nota en la puerta del local del ensayo, como Martín Lutero en Wittenberg? “Creo que es importante dejar a cada persona su espacio. Nos une el mismo Cristo, nos une la misma fe, la pasión por Él, la misa, los sacramentos, pero tenemos formas muy distintas de vivir las cosas. En mi caso, dejar La Voz del Desierto fue consecuencia directa de que me iba a Estados Unidos, pero es verdad que no me identificaba con la música que se hacía. Estuvo bien, además aprendí y disfruté muchísimo, pero no me sentía representado”.

Jaime Salmoreno, entre los bancos de su parroquia en Torrejón de Ardoz. Pablo Monge

La incursión musical de Jaime Salmoreno y su contrato con 33 Producciones cuentan con la autorización del obispo de su Diócesis. Nada de rictus severos ni llamadas al orden para restringirse al canto gregoriano. “Yo creo que es importante aprender a disfrutar las cosas de una forma legítima, que no agote la verdad, la profundidad de la vida. Hay que ser disfrutón, pero entendiendo que se disfruta, sobre todo, a largo plazo”. Por eso no piensa, insiste, en el éxito comercial. “No me importa hacia dónde lleva esto, me importa que sea de Dios. No hay público más excelso que ese. Si Dios me lo pide, no me importaría cortar por lo sano e irme a un monasterio. Hay una cosa que dijo Benedicto XVI: ‘Dios no es sinónimo de éxito’. Seguimos a un crucificado. Piensa en los mártires, parece un fracaso que a alguien le despellejen vivo, como a San Bartolomé, y sin embargo es su mayor momento de éxito, porque expresan hasta qué punto es valioso eso que viven y custodian en su corazón”. El razonamiento le lleva a un peculiar discernimiento sobre el eterno conflicto en la separación entre obra y autor: “Mis éxitos no son míos. Yo administro las canciones, pero no son mías, son del que me las da, para el que las recibe”. Así, para Salmoreno, una propuesta como Lux (2025), de Rosalía, vive más allá de si las intenciones de la artista son solo iconoclastas. “En la historia de la Iglesia, independientemente de la intención de muchos autores, Dios ha hecho maravillas”.

¿Habla Dios también a través de Flos Mariae, las hermanas convertidas en meme por su extrañísima música (y vídeos)? “Cada uno comparte desde lo que tiene. Hay personas en la Iglesia que cantan mal, pero es lo que tienen. Si lo que tienen lo ofrecen, eso es lo mejor. Pienso más como mira una madre a dos hijos, que uno es más torpe, pero cuando ve que el torpe se esfuerza lo mira con cariño. Esa mirada cariñosa es importante que la trabajemos, también a nivel social”.

World.title: PSV hold on to book narrow Champions League win in Porto
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

PSV survived a second-half onslaught in Porto to secure their first win of the Champions League group stages.

Guus Til scored the only goal when he tapped in from close range after Esmir Bajraktarevic’s shot had come back off the post and was steered across goal by Sven Mijnans.

The Eindhoven club were worth their narrow lead against Francesco Farioli’s side after dominating possession in the first half, but rarely troubled Diogo Costa in the Porto goal.

Til went close with a header early in the second half before putting PSV ahead in the 57th minute.

But the visitors had to defend heroically as Porto poured forward in search of an equaliser, aided by an increasingly fragile Matej Kovar.

The goalkeeper put his defenders in jeopardy with a weak clearance in the 72nd minute, but redeemed himself by saving Victor Froholdt’s shot with his chest before Lutsarel Geertruida blocked the follow-up from Pepê.

A minute later Kovar was left stranded after he rushed out of his penalty area, but Sergiño Dest managed to hack the ball away before Alberto Costa could poke it into the open goal.

At the other end, substitute Denis Man came close to scoring a second for PSV with his first touch when his curling shot beat Costa but failed to sneak inside the post.

The 1-0 win lifts PSV to a provisional 16th place in the Champions League table at the halfway stage of round three, while Porto are still looking for their first point.

Their next match is at home to Belgian side Club Brugge, who will make the short trip to Eindhoven on November 4.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Council of Churches in the Netherlands is temporarily stepping in to help shelter refugees amid the ongoing asylum crisis.

An overflow of asylum seekers continues to leave many sleeping outside, while those who have already been given residence permits stay in asylum centres awaiting housing.

This caused trouble throughout the summer months, and, with winter approaching, the shortage of beds poses a new danger to the homeless.

The initiative, called Actie Onderdak, was launched by the Council’s 19 member churches and organisations, including protestant, catholic and reformed denominations.

The Council has written to all local councils and parishes asking them to help shelter families currently housed in asylum centres so more beds can be freed up.

The Council requested churches offer space in empty rectories or annexes where possible. The intention is to give families three months in a new location where they can “find peace and get to know their surroundings”.

The plan was developed in coordination with the refugee settlement agency COA, and also endorsed by asylum minister Bart van den Brink.

According to the Council, COA will ensure refugees can move on to a new location after their three-month church stay ends.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Netherlands has met its target for filling its gas reserves before the onset of winter, but only after reducing its limit to the European Union minimum of 64%.

The Dutch government set a target of 80% capacity by November 1 in 2022, after the full-scale Russian invasion of Ukraine sent wholesale prices soaring.

Last year it only managed to reach 73.6%, while a surge in prices triggered by the United States’ military action against Iran prompted the state energy company EBN, which is responsible for buying winter supplies, to reduce its orders.

In August the reserves were 45% full, prompting EBN to ask the government to lower its target to 64%, the minimum level agreed between EU member states.

Since then the reserves have been filled to 65.5% and the company hopes to be able to keep topping up supplies for another two weeks.

Last year the level peaked on November 1 and began falling on November 7. At the lowest point, on April 2, the reserves were just 4.5% full.

World.title: Amsterdam hopes 20km/h cycle lane limit will change behaviour
World.content:
Amsterdam city council has introduced an experimental speed limit of 20km/h for cyclists to see if riders can be persuaded to slow down.

Tourists, commuters and shoppers have all complained in recent years of feeling unsafe on the capital’s congested bike paths, but the only speed restriction is a 30 km/h limit for motor vehicles.

A temporary speed limit has been set on a section of Amstelveenseweg, one of the main routes into the city from the south, for four weeks to gauge its effect on cyclists’ behaviour.

But instead of enforcing the limit through fines and cautions, the city council has put up boards showing people how many of their fellow bike users are staying below 20 km/h, in the hope they will nudge people into being more considerate.

Traffic alderman Elise Moeskops told AT5 the idea of the experiment is to see if the signs will encourage a shift in cycling culture.

“If you enforce everything in the city you end up with a very harsh police state, and we don’t have the staff for that,” she said.

Infrastructure problems

“Are people prepared to cycle more slowly if we remind them that that’s an option? The question is what the social norm is on the cycle lane, because we don’t really know.”

But Kees Bakker, spokesman for the cyclists’ union Fietsersbond, was sceptical of the idea. He said better infrastructure was the solution to crowded bike lanes.

“The cycle lane on that road is very narrow and poorly laid out,” he told Dutch News. “There’s a busy pavement alongside it, so pedestrians spill over to the cycle path.

“It doesn’t make much difference if the speed limit is 20 km/h or 50 km/h, because the path is too narrow and there’s no room to overtake.”

Bakker said speed limits were likely to be less effective in bike lanes because not all cyclists travel at the same speed and they need space to overtake.

“Cars mostly drive in file at 30 km/h, but the range of speeds is much wider for cyclists,” he said. “Some of them ride at 15 km/h, others do 25 or even 30. There needs to be room to accommodate everyone, including people who want to coast along side by side at 15 km/h.”

World.title: Dutch destinations: Go back in time in eastern Drenthe
World.content:
Eastern Drenthe is perhaps the most underrated part of the Netherlands. Its rolling scenery, its history and its villages – low thatched farmhouses, tiny brick churches and woodlands – make it a perfect place to spend a few sunny autumn days.

Assen is the provincial capital. It has the region’s main museum and boasts the second-biggest department store in the Netherlands. It is also home to the Dutch TT circuit, offering a wide variety of motorcycle races from April to October. But the real charm of the region is in the countryside.

A weekend is not enough to take in everything, so here is a taster of what eastern Drenthe has to offer.

What to do

Visit the hunebedden

Eastern Drenthe is all about hunebedden, the Neolithic burial chambers built by the Funnel Beaker people over 5,000 years ago. Drenthe is home to 52 of the 54 known hunebedden in the Netherlands, and many are concentrated around Borger, where the national hunebed centre is based.

The biggest hunebed, with the not-so-romantic name D27, is located in the woods next to the visitors’ centre. The grounds are also home to a bizarre collection of zwerfstenen, or boulders, which were brought down to the province from Scandinavia by glaciers. Many of the stones have labels showing exactly where in Sweden or Norway they came from.

In addition, the centre has a café and a sort of Neolithic playground – the Prehistoric Park – where children can check out recreations of ancient homes. During peak season volunteers in costume are on hand to explain about the lives of people who lived in the region and demonstrate ancient crafts. No dogs.

Walk along the Hondsrug

The Hondsrug (literally “dog’s back”) is listed as a Unesco Global Geopark because of its unique history, deriving from the last two ice ages. This 70-kilometre-long glacial ridge made of sand and clay is the only one of its kind in Europe. There are dozens of walking and cycle trails to explore, as well as small museums, such as the De Nabershof working farm near Emmen. You can find out more about the region’s geology at the visitors centre, next to the hunebed centre in Borger.

Stroll around Orvelte

About 20 minutes south of Assen is Orvelte, a Drenthe village untouched by time, which has become a sort of open-air museum. It’s car-free – you park on the outskirts – but there is a horse-drawn “bus” if you have little ones with you who don’t want to walk.

Stroll past the thatched farmhouses, stop off for what we were told is the best apple pie in Drenthe, and check out the little museums – which seem to be based largely on the locals’ hobbies, such as collecting model cars and rare sheep.

There is a good sprinkling of shops, some of which sell tourist tat, but some are upmarket outlets selling wonderful antique pottery and glass, as well as clothes and bric-a-brac. Plenty of options for lunch and morning coffee. If you are into Christmas themes, Orvelte will transform into a Christmas village from December 18 to 20.

Catch up on history at the Drents Museum in Assen

The Drents Museum in the provincial capital Assen hit the headlines in 2025 when criminals broke in overnight and stole a number of priceless gold relics, most of which have since been recovered. There is no Romanian gold on show any longer – the current special exhibition is about Angkor in Cambodia – but the museum is well worth a visit to find out more about the history of the region.

It is heavy on the infotainment, so there’s plenty to keep the kids occupied, but the museum nevertheless has something for everyone. Located in several buildings linked by tunnels and overground walkways, the museum has Neolithic finds, art (a couple of Van Goghs), recreated stijlkamers (period rooms), temporary exhibitions and a fine café for lunch.

Go on a tree walk

The Boomkroonpad – treetop path – takes you from the roots of an oak tree up into the treetops, where you can walk along a very solid metal structure and admire the forest from above. The path is also the starting point for five forest floor walks, ranging from three to 16.5 kilometres, and there are plenty of organised activities for families – deer and mushroom spotting, for example – all year round.

Where to eat

All the attractions we visited had cafés for lunch, mainly selling standard-fare sandwiches and broodjes kroket. Assen has a good selection of cafés and restaurants for dinner. We ate at our hotel, Rikus, which uses local produce and offers three-, four- and five-course menus. Be warned: the portions are big as well as being delicious.

Where to stay

Rikus, a small hotel in the village of Eext, about 20 minutes from Assen and Borger, has an eclectic interior and big bedrooms with views over the countryside. As a couple we paid €331 for bed, breakfast, a three-course dinner and drinks.

There is a hotel and a quaint-looking B&B in Orvelte, and Assen is home to Hotel de Jonge, with a large café terrace in the heart of the old city. Drenthe is popular with Dutch holidaymakers, so, as you would expect, there are plenty of campsites and holiday parks to choose from as well.

Anything else

Unless you are big on cycling or long walks, you really need a car to get around the region. The attractions can get very busy at weekends in the summer months, which may well dent their charm. The Dutch TT Grand Prix takes place on the last Sunday in June.

World.title: Primary school teachers reject four-day week amid staff shortage
World.content:
School leaders in the Netherlands are opting against the idea of a four-day week for primary schools amid a critical shortage of teachers.

A survey conducted by Nu.nl and the Academy & Association of School Leaders (AVS) found that of 308 heads of schools, only three (less than 1%) said they had chosen to reduce required attendance days for pupils as a solution to the crisis.

Primary schools are short of roughly 5,800 teachers nationwide, about 6.3% of all teachers, according to research institute Centerdata.

Despite an increase in teacher numbers since 2024, when the shortage stood at 8.1%, low salaries and long hours remain a problem for enticing people to join the profession. The previous generation of teachers is also retiring, worsening the gap.

Leanne der Steeg, a policy advisor at AVS, told Nu.nl that a four-day school week does not necessarily help the teachers and can harm education.

“A four-day school week also brings ‘hassle’ with it,” she said. “It is not just a matter of sending a class home. Thought must be given to the missed teaching time. Will it be made up at another time, will homework be assigned, and what about children of working parents? And if you free up a teacher for a day by opting for a four-day school week, it requires preparation before they can stand in front of another class.”

World.title: Rail fares to go up by 4.7% next year to help pay for new trains
World.content:
Dutch national train operator NS is set to raise fares by almost 5% on average in 2027, exceeding the rate of inflation for the third year in a row.

The increases are needed “to purchase new, comfortable trains, pay for rising costs and keep investing in good services,” Daan Schut, the management board member responsible for fares, said in a press statement on Tuesday.

NS is offsetting the increase by offering bigger discounts on off-peak fares for passengers who buy in advance. The maximum reduction on so-called PrijsTijd deals will go up from 60% to 80% next year.

The company said it also wanted to discuss reviving the discounted summer subscription rate, which allowed passengers to travel off-peak and at weekends for €49 a month in July and August, rather than the regular fee of €127.50.

The Railrunner fare for children, which allows under-12s to travel across the country all day for a flat rate, is being frozen at €2.50, and the KidsVrij subscription for families, which gives free travel up to the age of 11, will stay unchanged.

The minimum fare for short journeys is going up to €3.10, while the supplement for the high-speed line between Schiphol and Rotterdam is rising by 20 cents to €3.40.

Rail passengers’ organisation Rover criticised the above-inflation rises, pointing to the success of the summer discount as proof that people will travel by train if it is an affordable option.

“Now that NS is finally seeing its passenger numbers growing, passengers are being punished with big ticket increases. By constantly using the maximum room that NS has to raise ticket prices, it is holding back further growth,” a Rover spokesperson said.

Fares have gone up by around 6.5% for each of the last two years, partly to correct the 1.5% rise in 2023, when inflation was 10%. In 2024 prices were frozen thanks to a government cash injection of €120 million.

NS made a profit for the first time in years in 2025, recording a net gain of €380 million, though most of this came from a recalculation of its access charges during the coronavirus pandemic, when fewer trains ran. The charges are the costs the company pays to use the track network.

World.title: Millions to get compensation from takeaway apps over hidden fees

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Food delivery apps Thuisbezorgd and Uber Eats have been forced to stop hiding fees and advertising fake discounts after a complaint by consumer watchdog Consumentenbond.

Millions of customers will also receive a payout voucher in compensation ranging between €5 to €30, the watchdog said.

The companies were putting “small order fees” and other surcharges only at the end of orders, and were advertising misleading discounts for some takeaways.

The Consumentenbond accused Thuisbezorgd in July of hiding charges that often added €2 to €4 to an order. Fake discounts were also show; in one example, Indian snacks priced at €3.75 were later shown as “reduced” from €7.50 to €6.

Both companies told news agency ANP the changes followed “constructive” talks with the Consumentenbond. Uber Eats had already adjusted its charges in June.

World.title: Polish leaders condemn Hegseth’s “scandalous” remarks downplaying role of US allies in Afghanistan
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Leading figures from Poland’s ruling coalition have hit back at US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth over his recent remarks downplaying the contribution of America’s allies during the war in Afghanistan. The speaker of parliament, Włodzimierz Czarzasty, called the comments “scandalous”, while Prime Minister Donald Tusk read out a message sent to him by a Polish army medic who had declared dead the last of the 44 Polish soldiers who died in Afghanistan. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk ⤵️ Chciałbym, żeby te słowa dotarły do naszych sojuszników, żeby już nigdy więcej nikt nie lekceważył wysiłku naszych żołnierzy. pic.twitter.com/gGJkh4Gnft — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) October 20, 2026 The controversy stemmed from a speech the US defence secretary gave to US military cadets in Tennessee on Saturday. Hegseth referred to his time serving as a US Army officer in Afghanistan, where he recalled that the International Security Assistance Force (ISAF) headquarters had flags from over fifty countries. “Except,” Hegseth said, “there were maybe five [countries] that contributed. It was actually closer to one or two that actually, by the end, were involved in kinetic operations. In fact, the patch ‘ISAF’ – we joked that it meant ‘I Saw Americans Fighting.'” The comments earned quick reproach from Polish foreign minister Radosław Sikorski, who aimed a message at Hegseth on social media, saying: “Tell that to the families of 44 Polish soldiers who died securing the tough Ghazni province.” Tell that, Mr @SecWar, to the families of 44 Polish soldiers who died securing the tough Ghazni province. https://t.co/vm4TM0sMJO — Radosław Sikorski 🇵🇱🇪🇺 (@sikorskiradek) October 18, 2026 On Tuesday, the remarks earned even stronger reproach from Czarzasty, who is the speaker of the Sejm, the more powerful lower house of parliament, and the leader of The Left (Lewica), one of the groups that forms Poland’s ruling coalition. At a press conference, Czarzasty said that Hegseth’s “scandalous” comments are “harmful to the families of Polish soldiers and to Polish national pride”. He also criticised President Karol Nawrocki – an opponent of the government and conservative ally of Donald Trump – for not condemning Hegseth’s remarks. It is “an insult to Polish soldiers” that Nawrocki, who serves as commander-in-chief, “is unable to stand up for their dignity and the dignity of those who died”, declared Czarzasty. To skandaliczne, że prezydent Polski boi się potępić polityków amerykańskich za brak szacunku do polskich żołnierzy, którzy zginęli w Afganistanie. pic.twitter.com/uyv54yDvrI — Włodzimierz Czarzasty 📚📖 (@wlodekczarzasty) October 20, 2026 Later on Tuesday, Tusk read out to his cabinet a text message he said he had received from a former military medic, whom he did not name. “Please stand up for soldiers, I beg you,” wrote the medic. “During my tour in Afghanistan, we confirmed the death of the last Polish casualty, a platoon sergeant whose wife was pregnant in Poland at the time.” “I received a medal from the Americans for helping them, for treating Americans. I didn’t have to do that. We treated them with our own Polish medicines,” they added. Tusk then added his own remarks, stating: “I would like these words to reach our allies. So that no one will ever again downplay the efforts of our soldiers. Wherever our allies, including our closest ally, the Americans, have needed our participation, Polish soldiers stood shoulder to shoulder with them.” Tusk also referenced Nawrocki’s silence on the matter. “Frankly, I was also counting on the president speaking out on this matter. But it seems I miscalculated.” Tusk is the first European head of government to directly criticise Hegseth’s remarks, although a spokesperson for British Prime Minister Andy Burnham did say on Monday that it was “wrong to diminish the role” of British personnel, 457 of whom died in Afghanistan. Of the 3,621 coalition deaths during the war in Afghanistan, around two thirds were Americans (2,461). The rest came from 31 different countries, with Poland’s 44 fatalities the seventh most of any nation. Hegseth’s remarks are not the first time that the Trump administration has caused anger in Poland by downplaying allies’ role in Afghanistan. In January, Trump himself suggested that other countries had “stayed a little back, a little off the front lines”. That prompted General Roman Polko, who commanded Poland’s GROM special forces unit in Iraq and Afghanistan, to call the US president “a coward who has never been on the front lines”. The former commander of Poland's special forces in Iraq and Afghanistan has condemned Donald Trump for questioning the contribution of America's allies "This is the cynicism of a coward who hasn’t been on the front lines himself," said General @PolkoRoman https://t.co/kElkAO5qX4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 23, 2026 The Polish government has also clashed with the US on other issues. In January, Tusk joined other European leaders in calling for Greenland’s sovereignty to be respected, following Trump’s calls for the island to be brought under US control. The following month, Tusk declared that Poland would not be a “vassal” of the US and suggested that Nawrocki wanted Poland to be too subservient to Washington. Czarzasty has twice this year clashed with the US ambassador over critical remarks he made towards Trump. However, at the same time, the Polish government has sought to maintain positive relations with Washington, given America’s role as Poland’s most important security partner. In June, Poland formally requested that the US establish a new permanent military base on its territory. Hegseth himself has praised Poland, calling it a “model ally” last year. The US State Department this month also announced that it was pushing for Poland to be allowed to join the G20 “as soon as possible”, pointing to its “growing leadership position in the international arena”. On Monday afternoon, following media reports of the arrest, a spokesman for the military police confirmed that they had detained a 31-year-old man of Polish and Ukrainian citizenship, who holds the rank of senior private reserve. The suspect, who had at the time been undertaking a course at the Military Medical Academy (WAM) in Łódź, is being held on suspicion of declaring readiness to act for the benefit of a foreign intelligence service against Poland. That crime is punishable by up to eight years in prison. W dniu 16 października 2026 r. żołnierze z Oddziału Żandarmerii Wojskowej w Łodzi, zgodnie z postanowieniem Prokuratora Działu do Spraw Wojskowych Prokuratury Rejonowej Łódź-Polesie w Łodzi, dokonali zatrzymania mężczyzny w wieku 31 lat, obywatelstwa polskiego i ukraińskiego, w… pic.twitter.com/MLpqzfT4iO — Żandarmeria Wojskowa (@Zandarmeria) October 19, 2026 The Polish authorities have not revealed which foreign intelligence service the suspect – who has been placed in detention for three months – is believed to be associated with. Speaking later to reporters, deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk said that the man had “clearly shown himself to be someone who is conducting reconnaissance of certain types of military installations belonging to the Polish armed forces”. He also revealed that the suspect had recently obtained Polish citizenship. While the authorities have not released further information, Rzeczpospolita, a leading newspaper, reported earlier on Monday that the suspect, whom it named as Vasiliy, had been found in possession of several different phones, documents, and a large amount of money and gold. Poland has recently seen a number of high-profile cases of individuals charged – and in some cases convicted – of spying on behalf of Russia and Belarus. Poland’s security services recently revealed that the number of espionage cases they launched last year was more than double the figure for 2024. Over those two years combined, there were more investigations than in the previous three decades. This month, a former Polish soldier was sentenced to five and a half years for spying on behalf of Russia. The tasks assigned to him included reconnaissance of Rzeszów-Jasionka airport as part of a possible plan to assassinate Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky while he travelled through Poland. Poland has detained and expelled 15 Russians and Belarusians who tried to take part in youth world karate championships that were taking place in the Polish city of Bielsko-Biała. “Eleven Belarusian citizens and four Russians entered the country on tourist visas, which was inconsistent with the declared purpose of their stay in Poland,” said border guard spokesman Szymon Mościcki. After being detained, they received orders to leave the country within eight days, which is “the shortest possible deadline”, he added, quoted by broadcaster TVP. Piętnastu obywateli Rosji i Białorusi zostało zatrzymanych przez Straż Graniczną. Przyjechali do Polski na wizach turystycznych, choć prawdopodobnie zamierzali wziąć udział w mistrzostwach świata w karate. Otrzymali decyzje nakazujące opuszczenie kraju.https://t.co/czcjQKZ2kw — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) October 19, 2026 The announcement came one day after the karate world championships in the cadet, junior and U-21 categories had finished in Bielsko-Biała. In early October, Russia’s TASS news agency had reported that some of the country’s junior karatekas, as competitors are known, had planned to compete in the tournament. The World Karate Federation (WKF) allows Russian and Belarusian athletes to compete under a neutral banner. However, Poland has a strict policy of not allowing Russian and Belarusian athletes to compete in tournaments on its territory. This year, it banned them from taking part in a World Cup ski jumping event. It was also removed as host of two European junior weightlifting championships for banning Russian and Belarusian athletes. On 15 October, the day after the championships in Bielsko-Biała had started, TASS reported that none of the Russian athletes had been allowed to register by the Polish organisers. Paweł Połtorzecki, president of the Polish Karate Union (PUK), confirmed that, despite PUK warning them not to come, Russian and Belarusian athletes had sought to take part, prompting the organisers to ask the border guard to conduct an inspection. “The first sign was the appearance of a Russian at the refereeing course,” he revealed, quoted by TVP. “That’s when the first detention occurred.” Gazeta Wyborcza, a leading Polish daily, reports that the Russian karatekas had obtained tourist visas from other countries in the European Schengen area, of which Poland is part. Poland itself does not issue tourist visas to Russians. Poland has been removed as the host of two European junior weightlifting championships after refusing to allow Russian athletes to take part The European Weightlifting Federation says it "does not accept discrimination based on geopolitical circumstances" https://t.co/j7PfiTHZ1M — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 9, 2026 Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Poland has been one of Kyiv’s closest allies, providing military and humanitarian support while also pressing for tougher international sanctions against Moscow. Meanwhile, Poland has become the primary target in Europe for sabotage operations carried out by operatives working on behalf of Russia, including arson attacks and an attempt to derail a train. Russia has also repeatedly violated Polish airspace with drones, missiles and, most recently, a helicopter. In response to Russia’s aggressive actions, Poland has successively shut down all Russian consulates on its territory. Moscow responded by likewise closing all Polish consulates that it previously hosted. In January, Russia warned its citizens against travelling to Poland due to “Russophobia”. Poland says it has broken up an international criminal group responsible for laundering an estimated 337 million zloty (€77 million) by using currency exchange offices to illegally process money obtained from internet scams. Nine suspects – eight Ukrainians and one Belarusian – have been detained in a series of raids, which also resulted in the seizure of gold and cash worth over 1 million zloty. Służby rozbiły międzynarodową grupę zajmującą się praniem pieniędzy z oszustw inwestycyjnych i kryptowalut. Zatrzymano 9 osób, a skala transakcji przekroczyła 337 mln zł. Zabezpieczono złoto i gotówkę wartą ponad 1 mln zł. @Straz_Graniczna @PolicjaCBZC @ABW_GOV_PL pic.twitter.com/g2NQoqaPvP — Marcin Kierwiński (@MKierwinski) October 19, 2026 The accused – four women and five men aged between 26 and 53 – were arrested in Łódź, Warsaw and Małopolska province, announced Krzysztof Kopania, spokesman for the Łódź regional prosecutor’s office, which is leading the investigation. The detainees are four female cashiers, three men running the exchange offices, and two couriers used to transport money. All have been charged with participating in an organised criminal group and money laundering. They could face up to 15 years in prison if convicted. Prosecutors say that the gang, which operated in the cities of Warsaw, Lublin, Wrocław, Katowice and Gdańsk, collected money that had been obtained through internet fraud and transported it to cryptocurrency exchanges. It was then processed without complying with anti-money laundering procedures. Proceeds were then transferred to bank accounts, sent abroad by car, or concealed in fictitious purchases of gold. Most money was ultimately invested in cryptocurrencies. “The scale of the operation was enormous,” said Kopania. “It is estimated that between February 2025 and July 2026, members of the group took steps to conceal the origins of approximately 337 million zloty.” The ringleader was a 34-year-old Ukrainian national who made the key decisions and oversaw the domestic and international channelling of funds obtained from illegal sources, according to the Internal Security Agency (ABW) and border guard, which were also involved in the operation. Seven of the accused have been placed in pre-trial detention for three (or in one case two) months, while two have been bailed and ordered not to leave Poland. World.title: Lithuania says Ukrainian drone that struck car entered its airspace from Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. This article has been updated to include a statement from Poland’s defence ministry issued on Monday afternoon. Lithuania says there is “no doubt” that a Ukrainian drone which exploded on its territory on Sunday, hitting a moving car, entered its airspace from Poland. However, Poland has so far said that there is no confirmation of an object crossing the border. Meanwhile, Ukraine has apologised for the incident, saying that Russian electronic warfare had diverted the drone’s path during an operation against military targets in Russia. Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine is spilling over onto the Eastern flank of NATO and EU. This morning, NATO fighter jets stationed at Šiauliai Air Base scrambled once again after an unidentified object entered Lithuanian airspace. What appears to be a drone exploded… — Gitanas Nausėda (@GitanasNauseda) October 18, 2026 On Sunday morning, Lithuania confirmed that a drone had entered its airspace and exploded, causing damage to a moving vehicle. NATO jets were scrambled in response to the incursion but were not able to visually identify the object. President Gitanas Nausėda said that the incident was further evidence that “Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine is spilling over onto the Eastern flank of NATO and [the] EU”. Meanwhile, Lithuanian defence minister Robertas Kaunas revealed that preliminary information indicated the drone had entered from Polish airspace. “I have already contacted the Polish defence minister and asked Poland to join the investigation so that we can look into this incident together,” said Kaunas, quoted by broadcaster LRT. However, a spokesman for Poland’s defence ministry, Janusz Sejmej, told the Polish Press Agency (PAP) on Sunday that “there is no confirmation [from our radar systems] of [an object] crossing the border from Poland to Lithuania”. Polsat, a leading Polish broadcaster, cited unnamed sources at Poland’s defence ministry saying that they believed the drone in fact took off from within Lithuanian territory, around 30 kilometres from the Polish border, and then flew deep into the country. In response, Deividas Matulionis, an advisor to the Lithuanian president, told the Baltic News Service (BNS) on Monday that “I can say very unequivocally we have credible evidence that the drone crossed the Polish border”. Later, the country’s prime minister, Mindaugas Sinkevičius, said that “there is no doubt that it entered…from the Polish side”. He also confirmed that the evidence indicates the drone “is of Ukrainian origin”. We regret the incident that occurred this morning in Lithuanian airspace, which may have resulted from Russian electronic warfare diverting drones during an operation against legitimate military targets in Russia. We apologise for any disruption, risks, and concern this may have… — Heorhii Tykhyi (@SpoxUkraineMFA) October 18, 2026 Those remarks followed a statement on Sunday afternoon from Heorhii Tykhyi, the spokesman for Ukraine’s foreign ministry, who appeared to confirm that the drone was Ukrainian. “We regret the incident that occurred this morning in Lithuanian airspace, which may have resulted from Russian electronic warfare diverting drones during an operation against legitimate military targets in Russia,” wrote Tykhyi. “We apologise for any disruption, risks, and concern this may have caused.” The spokesman said that Ukraine would “share all relevant information with our Lithuanian partners to establish the full circumstances of the incident”. However, he gave no further information on what type of drone was involved, where it was launched from, and what its target was. Lithuania borders Belarus, an ally of Russia, and the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, as well as Poland and Latvia. In March and May this year, a number of Ukrainian drones aimed at targets in Russia entered the airspaces of NATO members Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Finland, likely due to Russian electronic jamming. On Monday afternoon, Poland’s defence ministry issued a statement “strongly refuting” media reports suggesting that sources within the ministry had identified the drone as having taken off within Lithuania itself. It added that the ministry, in cooperation with its Lithuanian partners, was still “conducting a detailed analysis” of what had taken place. World.title: Poland condemns attack by Israeli settlers on delegation that included Polish diplomats
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland has condemned an attack by masked Israeli settlers on a delegation of European diplomats – including Polish ones – that was visiting the West Bank. It called for a “decisive response from the Israeli authorities”, saying that the incident is “further evidence of the settler violence that the Palestinian population in the West Bank faces on a daily basis”. The attack has likewise been condemned by France and Belgium, whose nationals were also in the delegation, and the European Union, as well as by the Israeli foreign minister. Masked Israeli settlers attacked European diplomats, a French mayor and Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, prompting European condemnation. The violence comes amid unprecedented settler pogroms during the olive harvest. pic.twitter.com/wsP6edL62y — Al Jazeera English (@AJEnglish) October 18, 2026 On Saturday, the delegation – which included members from France, Belgium and Poland as well as representatives of the Catholic church – visited the mostly Christian Palestinian village of Taybeh near Ramallah in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. They had come to assess the situation following regular recent attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians trying to harvest olives on their own land. During the visit, the delegation came under attack, with parts of the incident caught on camera. France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, reported that Bernard Baudoux, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France, had been “violently assaulted” during the incident. He demanded that Israel arrest the perpetrators and “urgently put an end to these criminal acts of violence”. Late on Saturday afternoon, the spokesman for Poland’s foreign ministry, Maciej Wewiór, issued a statement confirming that the attack had taken place and that the delegation had included an unspecified number of Polish diplomats, who he said had not been harmed. “We express our deep outrage and strongly condemn this incident,” added Wewiór. “Poland consistently opposes violence by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank. Attacks on representatives of the diplomatic corps are absolutely unacceptable.” The spokesman said that Poland now “expects urgent and detailed explanations from the Israeli authorities” and for the perpetrators of the attack to be identified and held accountable. “We also expect effective measures to prevent similar incidents in the future.” ❗Potwierdzamy, że na Zachodnim Brzegu Jordanu doszło do ataku na konwój, w którym znajdowali się przedstawiciele korpusu dyplomatycznego, w tym polscy dyplomaci. Według wstępnych informacji za atak mogą odpowiadać izraelscy osadnicy. Polskim dyplomatom nic się nie stało. Z… — Rzecznik MSZ – Maciej Wewiór (@RzecznikMSZ) October 17, 2026 On Sunday, Poland’s foreign ministry issued a further statement in which it “condemned the attack by masked settlers…during a solidarity visit to a town known for its centuries-old Christian presence”. The incident “is further evidence of the settler violence that the Palestinian population in the West Bank faces on a daily basis”, they added, calling for a “decisive response from the Israeli authorities”. The attack was also “strongly condemned” on Sunday by the European Union’s diplomatic service, which said that it “expects full accountability as well as effective measures to prevent continued acts of violence and violent harassment against Palestinians”. Belgium’s foreign minister, Maxime Prevot, said that his country would continue to “press for EU sanctions against those responsible for this violence and those who support them”. 🇵🇸 I condemn in the strongest terms the attack by masked settlers in Taybeh, in the occupied West Bank, against Palestinians, our Consul General, French and Polish diplomats as well as catholic representatives. A French mayor was assaulted and a Belgian vehicle damaged. Our team… — Maxime PREVOT (@prevotmaxime) October 17, 2026 In the wake of the incident, Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu had urged people to show “caution before drawing conclusions” over what had happened. He claimed that there is “a coordinated campaign to smear Israel and the Jewish residents” of the West Bank. However, the Israel Defence Forces (IDF) said that it “strongly condemns the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Israeli rioters”. But it added that “the consulate’s visit was not coordinated with the IDF”, which is “important to prevent incidents of this kind”. Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, also issued a condemnation of the attack and said that police had opened an investigation. The IDF strongly condemns the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Israeli rioters. Police forces and forensic investigators from the Judea and Samaria District are entering the area accompanied by… — Israel Defense Forces (@IDF) October 17, 2026 The incident involving the diplomatic group came a day after around 80 Israeli settlers had attacked Palestinians harvesting olives, with Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine among those injured. Levine told the Committee to Protect Journalists, an American non-profit organisation, that she had been pushed to the ground by a group of masked settlers, who “were kicking me for I think at least 10 minutes”. That incident prompted criticism of Israel from the United States, whose ambassador, Mike Huckabee, called it a “despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards”. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, said he was “disturbed” by the incident and confirmed that “we’ve asked the Israelis to crack down on that”. .@SecRubio on reporter Heidi Levine being attacked in the West Bank: "We're very disturbed by those images and what we're seeing….the President has been very clear, he's said this repeatedly, he does not want to see friction or crisis going on in the West Bank." pic.twitter.com/Xg10vteeXK — CSPAN (@cspan) October 18, 2026 In August this year, Poland summoned Israel’s ambassador to express its “great disappointment” that the IDF had discontinued an investigation into the strikes on an aid convoy in Gaza in 2024 that killed seven humanitarian workers, including a Pole, Damian Soból. In May, Poland issued a five-year entry ban on Israeli national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir for his treatment of detained activists, including Polish citizens, from a flotilla seeking to reach Gaza. Last year, Israel criticised Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, after he suggested that Israeli politicians are causing the starvation of mothers and children in Gaza. The Israeli foreign ministry called the remarks “unacceptable” and urged Tusk to “remember the lessons” of the Holocaust. World.title: Poland moves to allow more municipalities to charge tourist fee
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Many more municipalities in Poland will be allowed to charge a daily fee for tourists and other overnight visitors after a change to the law dropping environmental requirements for levying such charges. Kraków, which received 8.7 million overnight tourists last year, had in particular been pushing for the change. However, Poland as a whole has seen a recent boom in visitor numbers, recording the EU’s second-fastest growth in the number of nights in tourist accommodation last year. #Krakow #opłataturystyczna #ustawa 🚨🔥Z OSTATNIEJ CHWILI! 🔥🚨 📢 Prezydent RP podpisał nowelizację przepisów dotyczących podatków i opłat lokalnych, PIT oraz PCC. 🏨 Najważniejsze zmiany dla branży turystycznej dotyczą opłaty miejscowej i uzdrowiskowej. 🗓️ Od 2027 r. za jej… pic.twitter.com/9ATvENvNol — Kraków (@krakow_pl) October 15, 2026 Until now, a “visitor’s fee” could be levied by municipalities with beneficial climatic features, “scenic qualities” and the capacity to accommodate people visiting to benefit from these attributes, as well as localities in areas with the status of a “spa protection area”. In practice, this largely applied to seaside and mountain resorts. Kraków did charge a visitor’s fee between 2004 and 2015, but was subsequently unable to do so due to a toughening of environmental requirements. The city has long suffered from bad air pollution, though it has taken significant steps to tackle the issue. Now, under new legislation proposed by the government earlier this year and signed into law by President Karol Nawrocki this week, the requirement for beneficial climatic features has been scrapped, meaning many more places will be able to charge the visitor’s fee. From 1 January, municipalities with scenic qualities will be able to charge visitors up to 5 zloty (€1.14) for each night they stay in hotels, guesthouses and short-term rental accommodation for up to one month, a rise on the current maximum of 3.46 zloty. Additionally, whereas previously only people visiting for the purposes of tourism had to pay, the fee now applies to all visits, including for work or health purposes, reports broadcaster TVN. People with significant disabilities, children with certified disabilities and their carers will be exempt from the fee. In another change, fees will be collected directly by accommodation providers, who will be required to maintain detailed records, reports the Infor news service. Passing fees on in a timely manner will entitle providers to receive at least 10% of the money they collect. Poland saw the EU's second-fastest growth in tourism in 2025, behind only the Mediterranean island state of Malta https://t.co/WVkRbHtU7o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 19, 2026 In 2024, Kraków appealed to the government to be allowed to charge tourists a fee, noting that “overtourism leads to tensions and social discontent”, as the “local community suffers” and “residents increasingly feel like tourists in their own city”. With its UNESCO-listed Old Town, Wawel royal castle, and former Jewish district of Kazimierz, Kraków is regularly named as one of Europe’s best tourist destinations. Last year, a record 16.25 million people visited the city, of whom 8.7 million stayed overnight. While that is a boon to the local economy, it also often causes tensions with residents, who complain about noise and disruption. In 2024, the city created the new position of “night mayor”, whose role is to reconcile the needs of tourists, businesses and residents. Poland’s government has approved legislation that would allow local communities to ban short-term rentals of the type offered through services such as Airbnb. Such accommodation has boomed in recent years, often prompting a backlash from local residents https://t.co/8MRfRWTDxd — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 3, 2026 Following this week’s change to the law, Kraków city hall confirmed that it would now again be able to collect a visitor’s fee “if the statutory conditions are satisfied and the municipal council adopts an appropriate resolution”. The city’s recently elected new mayor, Łukasz Gibała, who will be sworn in next week, said before Sunday’s election that he was in favour of a tourist tax of at least 20 zloty per night, four times the new maximum. “In western European cities there are rates of that size and higher,” Gibała said, quoted by financial news service Money.pl. “Maintaining the city in the face of the influx of tourists is costly. In Kraków, private business owners profit from tourism, whilst the city and its residents foot the bill.” Poland as a whole has also experienced a boom in tourism. Last year, the country recorded the European Union’s second-largest growth in the number of nights spent in tourist accommodation. Its increase of 7% was behind only the Mediterranean island state of Malta (9.9%). World.title: Poland drops proposal to criminalise providing help to illegal migrants following outcry
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s interior ministry has withdrawn a proposal to make it a criminal offence, punishable by up to three years in prison, to provide support to migrants who are in the country illegally. The idea had prompted criticism from human rights groups and even opposition from within the government. The interior ministry said the amendment had been intended to clamp down on migrant smuggling. But activists feared it would criminalise humanitarian aid, such as that provided to migrants who have irregularly crossed the border from Belarus. Za udzielenie bezinteresownej pomocy migrantom nie będzie groziła kara do trzech lat więzienia. Po burzy, którą wywołała publikacja „Rzeczpospolitej” i po sprzeciwie resortu rodziny, MSWiA wycofuje się z pomysłu „karania za podanie posiłku”.https://t.co/Q0N52IMRVn — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) October 15, 2026 Under current Polish law, anyone who facilitates the illegal stay of a person in Poland in exchange for financial or personal benefit can be jailed for up to five years. However, this week, the interior ministry proposed an amendment that would also have penalised anyone who knowingly “enabled or facilitated” the illegal stay of someone in Poland, even if not for financial or personal benefit. The offence would have been punishable by up to three years in prison. “Currently, this behaviour is not criminalised, creating a loophole for those who exploit such situations and, under the pretext of helping migrants, aid them in their illegal stay, thus serving as a springboard for further illegal migration,” wrote deputy interior minister Czesław Mroczek, quoted by the Rzeczpospolita daily. That immediately prompted concern that the law could be used against volunteers and residents of border areas who provide aid – such as food, water, medical treatment, clothing or shelter – to migrants who have crossed illegally from Belarus. Since 2021, tens of thousands of people, mainly from Asia and Africa, have tried to cross that border with the encouragement and support of the Belarusian authorities. They have sometimes used violence against Polish border officers. Poland and the EU accuse Belarus of “weaponising” migration as part of the “hybrid warfare” being waged by Russia and its allies against European countries. They have implemented tough border protection measures to prevent crossings and facilitate “pushbacks” of those who cross. However, many human rights and aid organisations argue that the migrants – over 100 of whom have died around the border since 2021 – are often victims of this process and need humanitarian support. Two dead bodies found in the river on Poland's border with Belarus likely belong to migrants from a group seen being pushed into the water by Belarusian officers as part of efforts to encourage irregular crossings into the EU, says a Polish minister https://t.co/xsnPd6FeO3 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 16, 2025 In response to the interior ministry’s proposal, 61 organisations, including Amnesty International, the Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights and the Auschwitz-Birkenau Foundation, signed a joint statement condemning the plans, which they said “violate international standards binding Poland”. The organisations warned that the proposed wording could expose medical staff treating migrants, lawyers providing legal assistance, facilities working with children, and organisations supporting victims of human trafficking to criminal liability. “This measure is not aimed at smugglers, but rather at activists or residents of border areas who provide humanitarian aid to foreign nationals who have crossed the border illegally and are present in Poland,” attorney Radosław Baszuk told the Rzeczpospolita daily. Baszuk previously represented five Polish activists who were prosecuted for providing food, clothing and shelter to a group of Middle Eastern migrants who had entered Poland from Belarus in 2022. A group of five activists have been found not guilty of enabling the illegal presence in Poland of Middle Eastern migrants whom they provided aid to after they had irregularly crossed the border from Belarus. Prosecutors had been seeking prison sentences https://t.co/RpfhVWL4hY — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 8, 2025 They were acquitted last year, with the ruling made final in March this year after an appeal. But Baszuk told Rzeczpospolita that, under the interior ministry’s proposed amendment to the relevant law, his clients could been convicted. On Wednesday, Poland’s commissioner for human rights, Sylwia Gregorczyk-Abram, also wrote to the justice ministry to “express concern” that the proposed changes “could lead to criminal liability for charitable or humanitarian activities undertaken towards individuals whose residence status has not yet been regulated”. Even a member of the government, the minister for family, labour and social policy, Agnieszka Dziemianowicz-Bąk, expressed her “firm opposition” to the plans on social media. She is from The Left (Lewica), one of the junior partners in Poland’s ruling coalition. ‼️ Ciepły posiłek, nocleg, potrzebne leki – za to wolontariusz ma trafić do więzienia nawet na 3 lata? 😡 Nie ma zgody Lewicy na kryminalizowanie pomocy humanitarnej! Ministra Agnieszka Dziemianowicz-Bąk zwróciła się do ministra Waldemara Żurka ze stanowczym sprzeciwem wobec… pic.twitter.com/QskUfJmgsu — Lewica (@__Lewica) October 14, 2026 In response to the growing criticism, the interior ministry announced on Friday that it was withdrawing the proposal, saying it decided to do so “to eliminate any doubts and prevent the misinterpretation of regulations”. “From the beginning, the ministry’s sole objective has been to tighten the system and target the organisers of this practice [of migrant smuggling],” said the ministry, quoted by Rzeczpospolita. “Legal provisions must effectively protect the state’s borders against organised crime, while simultaneously fully safeguarding humanitarian values ​and life-saving activities.” The number of attempted illegal crossings by migrants from Belarus to Poland fell from 15,500 in the first half of 2025 to 235 this year – a drop of over 98% Poland also now claims a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally https://t.co/RFZkd7CeIk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 Both the former Polish government and the current one, which took power in December 2023, have regularly faced criticism from human rights groups over their response to the migration crisis on the Belarus border. Earlier this year, the previous human rights commissioner, Marcin Wiącek, expressed concern over a ban on asylum claims introduced by the government in March 2025. He noted that the measures had been described as a temporary solution, but have remained in place ever since. The government, however, argues that its measures have been effective in preventing the illegal trafficking of migrants. Its data show that attempted border crossings from Belarus fell from around 15,500 in the first half of last year to less than 250 in the same period this year – a drop of over 98%. It also now claims to have a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally.
