World.title: DNO’s oil sales in northern Iraq double in Q3 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Norway-based oil and gas operator DNO reported that its crude oil sales in Iraqi Kurdistan nearly doubled on an annual basis, reaching an average of 28,058 barrels per day in the third quarter of 2026.

The increase in oil sales comes after the corporation proactively halted its regional activities in response to the military escalations between the United States, Israel, and Iran in late February 2026, which resulted in a total collapse in revenues in the second quarter of 2026.

During the third quarter of 2026, gross operating production from the Tawke and Peshkabir oilfields rose significantly to 73,219 barrels per day, a substantial increase from just 363 barrels per day in the second quarter of the year.

All payments for DNO’s share of the oil during the third quarter were made in advance and deposited into the company’s foreign bank accounts before delivery began, aiming to mitigate previous regional payment risks.

Compared to oil sales of 14,449 barrels per day during the third quarter of 2025, the company’s supplies in the third quarter of 2026 represent an increase of about 94 percent.

World.title: Iraq offers mediation between Iran, Gulf States
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein stated on Sunday that Baghdad is attempting to arrange a meeting between Iran and the Gulf States as part of diplomatic efforts to reduce tensions and advance regional stability.

Hussein’s remarks took place during his speech at the conclusion of the 52nd session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), where he confirmed that Iraq was maintaining contacts with both sides to facilitate dialogue, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

There are ongoing discussions between Iraq, the Gulf countries, and Iran aimed at bringing their viewpoints closer together, according to Hussein.

“We are trying to organize a meeting in Baghdad between Iran and the Gulf States,” Hussein said, without specifying a date or the degree of representation expected.

The proposal comes amid regional tensions that severely impacted maritime shipping and security in the Arabian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.

The goal of the diplomatic framework is to bring together Iran and the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) members—Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, and Oman—to address common security issues.

Hussein stressed that the region cannot purchase security from elsewhere and that internal collaboration is the only way to establish stability.

Although Hussein and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met in Baghdad on the sidelines of the summit to reaffirm a commitment to communication, the date of the joint meeting has not yet been disclosed.

World.title: Iraq holds funeral for 47 security personnel executed by ISIS years ago
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi authorities held a mass funeral on Tuesday in the northern city of Mosul for 47 victims, including security personnel and civilians, who were executed by the terrorist group of ISIS ten years ago.

Teams from Iraq’s Martyrs Foundation recently unearthed the remains from a mass burial south of Mosul. The Department of Forensic Medicine used DNA testing to positively identify the victims.

During ISIS’s brutal rule between 2014 and 2017, people from places south of Mosul, such as Hammam al-Alil, al-Shura, and al-Qayyarah, were kidnaped and executed. The victims included soldiers, police officers, religious figures, and local civilians.

Under the direction of Nineveh Governor Abdul Qader al-Dakhil, security personnel carried coffins covered in the Iraqi flag during an official ceremony. A public funeral procession headed toward the Qayyarah district for final burial after the central ceremony in Mosul.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: Iraq’s oil exports to China hit 1.18 million bpd in September
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil supplies to China during September totaled 4.84 million tons, or about 1.18 million barrels per day, a 19 percent decline compared to the previous year and a 248 percent increase compared to August.

The General Administration of Customs of the People’s Republic of China revealed that the country’s imports of crude oil from Russia, its largest supplier, reached 9.94 million tons (approximately 2.42 million barrels per day) in September, according to Reuters.

China oil imports from Russia in September are 20 percent more than the volumes it received during the same period in 2025, though it marks an 11 percent decline compared to the previous month.

During the first nine months of 2026, Brazil was the second-largest crude oil supplier to China, with imports reaching 44.29 million tons (approximately 324.65 million barrels) from Brazil, compared to 43.12 million tons (around 316.07 million barrels) from Saudi Arabia.

Brazil’s oil supplies to China increased by 18 percent on an annual basis to 5.15 million tons in September alone, or almost 1.25 million barrels per day.

China’s crude oil imports from Saudi Arabia stood at 2.70 million tons, or about 660,000 barrels per day, marking a 62 percent decline compared to the previous year.

Chinese independent refiners increased recently their imports of Iraqi and Qatari crude to compensate for a sharp decline in Iranian oil supplies.

As their stockpiles near depletion, private refineries in China are paying considerable premiums to acquire alternatives, according to Reuters.

Experts see that the step represents a desperate search for alternatives due to logistical obstacles, rather than a true rebound in Chinese domestic crude demand.

World.title: Two oilfield operators in northern Iraq merge in $600 million deal
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Gulf Keystone Petroleum and ShaMaran Petroleum have reached a merger agreement, becoming one of the top private oil producers in Iraqi Kurdistan.

According to a statement from the corporation, the all-share acquisition is worth $601 million, Reuters reported.

As of October 19, shareholders of ShaMaran, who are listed on Euronext, will receive 0.075 shares of Gulf Keystone for each share of ShaMaran they own, reflecting a premium of 23 percent.

Each company’s stockholders will own roughly half of the merged business when the merger is complete.

According to the announcement, Gulf Keystone intends to cease its London listing and transfer its principal listing to Euronext Oslo Bors’ main list.

Following the completion of the deal, the listing of ShaMaran shares will end.

The proposed combination has received unanimous approval from the boards of Gulf Keystone and ShaMaran. December will see special meetings to complete approval.

With combined estimated reserves of 323 million barrels and daily production of 53,000 barrels of oil, the merged business is expected to profit from greater size and diversity.

As part of its ambitions to increase its oil production capacity, Iraq has given many contracts to businesses from the United States, China, France, and other countries.

As Baghdad looks to boost natural gas supply and oil output, British Petroleum (BP) and its US and Turkish partners took over operations at four oilfields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk this week.

World.title: Iraq Stock Exchange records 2.5 billion IQD in weekly trading turnover
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraq Stock Exchange (ISX) reported weekly trading turnover exceeding 2.5 billion Iraqi dinars ($1.68 million) for the previous trading week, according to an official market report published on Tuesday, October 20, 2026.

Across the five trading sessions, shares of 57 joint-stock companies were actively traded out of 103 listed entities. Equities of 36 firms saw zero transactions due to pricing bid-ask disparities between buy and sell orders, while 11 companies remained suspended from trading for failing to meet mandatory corporate financial disclosure and regulatory reporting deadlines.

Trading volume expanded by 6.8% compared to the prior week, reaching 1.852 billion traded shares. However, total trading value contracted by 67% to 2.560 billion dinars, executed across 3,676 transactions. The main price benchmark, the ISX60 index, closed at 943.57 points, shedding 1.54% from its previous session close.

Foreign investment activity posted net inflows into domestic equities. Non-Iraqi investors bought 158 million shares valued at 331 million dinars over 55 contracts, while foreign selling remained muted, tallying 5 million shares worth 10 million dinars across 38 transactions.

The exchange convenes trading across five weekly sessions from Sunday through Thursday, listing 103 joint-stock enterprises spanning banking, telecommunications, industry, agriculture, insurance, financial investment, tourism, and services.

World.title: US dollar edges down across Baghdad, Basra, and Erbil Exchanges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged down across exchange shops in Baghdad, Basra, and Erbil on Tuesday, October 20, 2026, slightly paring back gains recorded earlier in the week.

In Baghdad, foreign exchange counters registered a dip of 500 dinars per $100 compared to Monday’s trading, setting the retail selling rate at 169,000 dinars against buying bids of 168,000 dinars.

In Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, trading displayed a similar softening, with selling desks quoting 168,200 dinars per $100 and buying transactions settling at 168,000 dinars.

In the southern commercial port hub of Basra, rates slipped by 250 dinars per $100 compared to yesterday’s levels. Exchange bureaus posted retail selling rates at 168,500 dinars against purchase bids of 168,000 dinars per $100.

Parallel market activity continues to reflect a sustained premium above the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory peg of 152,000 dinars per $100, driven by commercial merchant demand for physical liquidity outside the central electronic clearance platform.

World.title: Rubio lands in India for ‘trade diplomacy’
World.content:
Mumbai – US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in India on Tuesday, his second official visit to the country this year, as he pursues an Asian tour blending diplomacy and trade.

Rubio visited Uzbekistan, where he called for stronger partnerships with Central Asian countries, before landing in Mumbai for talks with Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar and meetings with business leaders.

He visited New Delhi and Kolkata in May, when he also toured the Taj Mahal and met Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Modi is not scheduled to meet Rubio this time.

The top US diplomat will visit Jamnagar, in the western state of Gujarat, a port and stronghold of billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance conglomerate and its flagship refinery, the world’s largest.

He is also due to lay a wreath in memory of the 2008 Mumbai attacks that killed 166 people.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Tuesday he had also spoken to Rubio and raised issues with the US military satellite system that Ukraine uses, as well as missile delays.

Zelensky, expected in Oslo for talks with US envoys, said he told Rubio that “Starlink/Starshield needs to be restored” and that ballistic missile interceptors “are needed to protect lives”.

– ‘Energy supplies’ –

Rubio’s visit comes as India and the United States struggle to finalise a trade deal, a persistent source of friction between the two countries.

Speaking in Samarkand, Rubio said Washington and New Delhi were “very close” to an agreement.

However, a deal during his visit appears unlikely.

US President Donald Trump’s tariff war launched in April last year has added to friction over India’s imports of Russian oil and warming ties between Washington and Pakistan, India’s arch-rival.

Asked about temporary US sanctions waivers for Russian oil, of which India is a major importer, Rubio said Washington had to juggle multiple factors “including our bilateral relationships with other countries and what they realistically are capable of being able to do in terms of their own energy supplies”.

“You also can’t unravel the economy of other countries because of one central issue,” he said.

The two countries reached an interim trade agreement in February aimed at reducing US tariffs on Indian goods.

But days later, the US Supreme Court struck down Trump’s sweeping tariffs, fuelling uncertainty over when the agreement would take effect.

The two sides have been negotiating ever since.

Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said this month the talks had reached “a plateau, beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult”.

Jaishankar met with his United Arab Emirates counterpart in Mumbai earlier on Tuesday. The UAE is a key supplier of Indian energy, especially liquefied natural gas (LNG).

“The situation in the Gulf remains a matter of deep concern,” Jaishankar told UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, in public comments broadcast before their meeting started.

He said India continues to support “free, safe and unimpeded flow of trade, energy and fertiliser”.

World.title: Police lens on Lawrence Bishnoi’s aide Randeep Malik in Tiger Shroff shooting case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Security agencies probing the attack on actor Tiger Shroff are investigating the role of

âs top-tier US-based operative Randeep Malik, notwithstanding gangster Anil Pandit claiming responsibility for it on social media.

Malik is considered very close to both Lawrence and his brother Anmol, who are also likely to be questioned in their respective jails in Gujarat and Delhi soon, sources have said.

Pandit and Shroff âs shooter Rehan both reported to Malik and were considered âhis menâ till a few months ago, a source said. Rehan had been earlier tasked by Malik and Pandit with a shooting incident in Sonipat as well.

âRehan was shown the same âAmerican dreamâ that Malik had shown Pandit in the past,â a source said.

As Pandit had been sent to California through the âDunkeyâ route months after the Siddhu Moose Wala murder, he was cited as a success story to young recruits.

Pandit used to handle âDabba callsâ for Malik till last year. In underworld parlance, âDabba callsâ refer to Voice over IP (VoIP) calls routed through speakers using multiple connected phones at different locations so that the real callerâs identity and physical location remain concealed.

NEW DELHI: A âgraciousâ trial court and a âvery indulgentâ Allahabad HC paved the way for two offenders in a grievous hurt case to go scotfree without spending a day in jail on the grounds that they suffered because of a 22-year-long trial, but the courts did not consider the victim, who is still getting treatment, Supreme Court has said.Now, SC has directed the accused in the 2003 case to surrender and asked the HC to conduct a fresh hearing.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said it was a case of misplaced sympathy. The trial court had awarded fiveyear jail terms to the two, but the HC released them on probation. SC said the case was âdoomed from its inception insofar as justice delivery to the victim is concernedâ.âWe cannot but, with an amount of consternation, notice the casual manner in which the trial court and the high court considered the issue from the stage of taking cognisance till the release of the accused on application of Probation of Offenders Act. They have gone scot-free without suffering a single day of imprisonment, especially by reason of the misplaced sympathy based on grandiose expositions of law,â it said.The court passed the order on an appeal filed by the brother of the victim, who has lost substantial functionality of both upper limbs.SC said the HC âwent overboardâ and wondered how it could pass such an order despite the adverse report on the character of the offenders, noting that theywere involved in multiple criminal cases. âTrue, protracted trial is agonising but here, the accused were on bail and merrily indulging in criminal activities,â the bench said.

World.title: India, US ‘perfectly aligned’ on key issues: Marco Rubio; defends ties with Pakistan
World.content:
US secretary of state

urged businesses to view the India-US relationship as a strategic partnership spanning technology, trade and security, saying the two countries were âperfectly alignedâ on issues that would shape the 21st century, even as he acknowledged that disagreements between them would persist.

Addressing a gathering of India Incâs leading business figures at a Freedom 250 event at BKC, Rubio said the relationship between the two countries could help shape the future of the global economy, particularly as advances in artificial intelligence and quantum computing transform industries and societies.

âI truly believe the relationship between US and India is defining, in many ways, in a positive way, what the 21st century can look like,â he said.

The gathering included Noel Tata (Tata Trusts), Anand Mahindra (Mahindra Group), Kiran MazumdarShaw (Biocon), Ashok P Hinduja (Hinduja Group), Amit Dixit (Blackstone), Hitendra Dave (HSBC India), K Balasubramanian (Citi India) and Rahul Badhwar (JPMorgan Chase).

Rubio identified emerging technologies and secure trade routes as two areas in which the countriesâ interests converge. âUS and India are perfectly aligned,â he said, referring to the challenge of harnessing new technologies for public benefit.





âWe have the same expertise. We have the same talented people working on it, from engineers to creative thinkers and innovators.â

He linked economic growth to the security of international shipping routes, arguing that businesses needed the freedom to move goods across borders and reach markets.

For India and US, he said, this required âa free and secure Indo-Pacificâ in which âno nation can claim dominance or ownership of international shipping lanesâ.

âNo two nations on earth will ever be perfectly aligned on every issue,â he said. âBut on the core issues that matter..., alignment between our countries is extraordinary.â

The speech did not signal any immediate change in tariffs or market access.

World.title: ‘Identify and defeat forces against India’: PM Modi calls for unity during Vijayadashami celebrations
World.content:
Calling for a united fight against forces seeking to divide society, undermine Indiaâs dignity and attack its culture, PM Narendra Modi Tuesday urged all political parties and national institutions to put the country first.

He stressed that national self-respect and faith in oneâs own strength were essential for progress, adding India must protect its cultural identity while building the capabilities to overcome challenges without depending on others.

âWe must identify the enemies of Mother India. We must defeat them,â Modi said at the Vijayadashami celebrations in east Delhi. âThe forces that hurt the honour and dignity of the country, the people who divide society, the mentality of those who hate our culture â these are the enemies of the country,â he said.

Quoting a Vedic verse, Modi said all institutions and political parties must stand together in the national interest.

Vijaya Dashmi is the victory of truth over falsehood: PM

We should fight the enemies of the country together, PM Narendra Modi said, calling for a collective commitment to âNation Firstâ.

His remarks came hours after RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, speaking in Nagpur, cited political upheavals in France, Albania, Nepal and Bangladesh while warning against attempts to bring about regime change in India.





Bhagwat also cautioned against protests becoming political tools and urged both authorities and protesters to remain within constitutional limits.

Drawing lessons from Lord Ramâs life,

stressed self-reliance. Despite the ocean separating him from Lanka, Lord Ram mobilised collective strength, brought together available resources and achieved what appeared impossible, he said. âWe must not sit relying on others. We must recognise our own strength and we must have faith in our own resources,â the PM said, linking the message to the goals of â

â and âViksit Bharatâ.

Describing Vijaya Dashmi as the victory of truth over falsehood, Modi also recalled Lord Ram embracing Nishad Raj and honouring Shabari as examples of compassion and inclusion. He said that âRam Rajyaâ represented governance without discrimination, where everyone received justice and equal opportunities. âThe objective of âpowerâ is not to âruleâ, but public welfare,â the PM said, urging service to the poor and deprived.

World.title: AAIB chief gets a year's extension as many key probes, including AI 171, on
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Govt has granted a one-year extension to Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) director-general G V G Yugandhar, with some key ongoing investigations â including Air India AI 171 crash â awaiting their final reports.

The reason: Having a new DG at a time like this could delay the final report into the June 12, 2025, Ahmedabad crash. Accordingly the aviation ministry had recommended an extension for Yugandhar, who retired as Indian Air Force group captain earlier this year, and the same was approved about a month back.

The key probes that are currently underway have AI 171 Air India right at the top followed by Air Indiaâs turbulent Phuket-Delhi flight of Aug 4, 2026, and some other crucial cases.

AI 171 report is learnt to be in its final stage and will be shared with stakeholders as per rules once ready.

People in the know say while the aviation ministry âkeeps the aircraft accident investigating agency at an armâs length and does not interfere in its working in any way,â it is taking steps to strengthen the AAIB. The bureau's lab has been recently upgraded and it now has the capability to download cockpit voice recorder and digital flight data recorder (black box) to know the conversation in the flight deck and the flight parameters till before an event being investigated.





It is learnt that the aviation ministry is working on having regional offices of AAIB to ensure investigators reach the site of accident/incident at the earliest. Additionally, this is to augment the bureauâs infra at a time when Indiaâs aviation is seeing a boom right from the number of flight training schools to aircraft in fleet of Indian operators with the figure currently being close to 900.

Aurobindo Handa, who was with IAF director (engineering) till Oct 2018 and then joined AAIB as DG on deputation where he remained for 3.5 years, said: âSome steps have been taken to strengthen AAIB but a lot more has to be done.

The plan is to have regional offices wherever DGCA has the same. The same must be staffed by non DGCA people to avoid 'conflict of interest'. The investigatorâs execution has to be like a clockwork mechanism as its scientific reports pinpointing cause/s of accident/incident are crucial for air safety to prevent the same thing from happening again.

And to achieve the outcomes, immaculate staffing is the most important function.â

AAIB was formed in 2012 following an ICAO objection that the regulator (DGCA) canât be the investigator. Till then panels packed with DGCA officials used to conduct probes into accidents and incidents.

World.content:
India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

NEW DELHI: Three sites from India have been added to the tentative list of United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization's World Heritage Convention, the Permanent Delegation of India to UNESCO announced on Tuesday.The three sites are the Karst-mud-volcano Complex of Baratang and Andaman Subduction Volcanoes in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and the Sirpur Cultural and Archaeological Landscape in Chhattisgarh.In a press release dated October 20, the Permanent Delegation of India to Unesco, based in Paris, announced the additions to India's Tentative List under the UNESCO World Heritage Convention.Inclusion on the tentative list is a prerequisite for any property to be considered for nomination to the World Heritage List. The delegation also acknowledged the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) for its work in the process.The additions mark a step towards the possible future nomination of the three sites for Unesco World Heritage status.India has 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, including 37 cultural sites, seven natural sites and one mixed site, following the inscription of the ancient Buddhist site of Sarnath in July 2026.India ranks sixth globally and second in the Asia-Pacific region.The five countries with the highest numbers are Italy with 62 sites, China with 61, France with 56, Germany with 55 and Spain with 50.Indiaâs first four sites were inscribed in 1983: the Ajanta Caves and Ellora Caves in Maharashtra, and Agra Fort and the Taj Mahal in Uttar Pradesh. These were all cultural sites recognised for their historical, architectural and artistic significance.

World.title: Zelensky, U.S. envoys hold Oslo talks as Ukraine claims U.S. missile holdup
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held talks in Oslo with top U.S. envoys on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) in a bid to get strained relations with Washington "on a more constructive path", Norway said.

"Ukraine is working for peace. I thank our partners for their support!" Mr. Zelensky said in a social media post after his arrival in the Norwegian capital.

Mr. Zelensky handed U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff an award in the Norwegian government's official residence, before posing with Norway's Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb, according to footage accompanying the Ukrainian leader's post.

Mr. Witkoff's fellow U.S. envoy Jared Kushner — U.S. President Donald Trump's son-in-law — was also taking part in the negotiations but was doing so remotely because of illness, according to the NTB agency.

Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since Mr. Trump partially lifted sanctions to strike a diesel-supply deal with Russia's Vladimir Putin and slammed Mr. Zelensky as a warmonger for Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries.

Mr. Zelensky has accused the United States of deliberately withholding vital intelligence and delaying military aid, saying on Monday (October 19) that Ukraine received no early warning of powerful Russian missile strikes that targeted energy facilities in the capital region.

U.S.-led diplomatic efforts to end Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II have stalled in recent months, as Washington has shifted focus towards the war with Iran.

The Norway talks were set to continue into the evening, Store told reporters, with he and Mr. Zelensky set to give a press conference around 7:15 p.m. (1715 GMT)

"The aim is to put diplomatic efforts on a more constructive path," he said.

'Needed to protect lives'

Ahead of the meeting, Mr. Zelensky said on Tuesday (October 20) he held "substantive" and "constructive" talks with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in which he insisted that the U.S. military satellite system Ukraine uses, Starshield, "needs to be restored" and that ballistic missile interceptors "are needed to protect lives".

Mr. Zelensky told U.S. senators on Monday (October 20) that "the Pentagon is delaying the delivery of missiles" already paid for by European countries, and that the shipment was waiting for U.S. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's signature.

He said several European countries were ready to transfer Patriot interceptor missiles from their own stockpiles but were still awaiting U.S. approval.

The United States has denied making any changes to intelligence sharing with Ukraine, and Mr. Rubio said on Tuesday (October 20) that Washington was not deliberately withholding supplies.

"There's nothing being deliberately denied to Ukraine," Mr. Rubio said while on a trip to India.

"It's simply, it's a balance between our obligations to other partners and frankly our own... requirements for our own facilities as well."

Mr. Trump has also denied ordering a reduction in speeds on the US government-owned and—controlled Starshield network after Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX developed it, said the order could only have come from the White House.

Strained relations

The U.S. leader has accused his counterpart of not trying to resolve the conflict with Russia. "Mr. Zelensky doesn't know what he's talking about," President Trump said on Monday (October 19).

"To be honest, I think it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine."

Mr. Trump said he was ready to meet Mr. Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in China next month to discuss denuclearisation, adding that talks could also cover the Ukraine war — fuelling fears in Kyiv that it was being sidelined.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed earlier that "the topic of such a hypothetical has indeed been mentioned" when asked about a Wall Street Journal report on Sunday (October 18) that U.S. President Trump, Russia’s President Putin and China’s President Xi could meet.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga said that such a meeting would "only encourage Putin to continue this war".

News outlet Axios reported that Mr. Witkoff would travel from Oslo to Russia to meet Putin.

"We hope that it will be possible to arrange a meeting in the very near future, allowing the American negotiators... Mr. Witkoff to brief President Putin on their contacts with both the Ukrainians and the Europeans," Mr. Peskov told reporters on Tuesday (October 20).

World.title: Bengal CM defends decision to shift stampede injured to private hospital, cites better care
World.content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) defended the government's decision to shift those injured in the Kolkata stampede from a State-run hospital to a private one, saying it was to ensure the best possible treatment and prevent further loss of life.

Speaking to reporters after visiting the health department's control room at Swasthya Bhavan on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) evening, he said the decision was taken on the spot after authorities assessed the treatment facilities available at State-run hospitals.

"We moved those injured to private hospitals because we realised that the best treatment could be provided there so that there is no more loss of life. I am happy to announce that there was no death among the 25 injured in the stampede. We decided on the spot. There is nothing controversial behind this," he said.

Responding to criticism over the shift, Mr. Adhikari said the decision should not be construed as a failure of the State health department.

"People are critical of the Health Minister and health secretary because of the shifting. But I would say there is nothing to say that the State's health infrastructure has failed."

Acknowledging shortfalls in infrastructure at State-run hospitals, he said improving the public healthcare system to match private sector facilities would take time.

"It would take at least two years for us to elevate the health system in West Bengal and bring it on par with that of the private sector. We have been in power for six months now. We need one and a half years more to do that," he said.

The Chief Minister also said the private hospital had not demanded payment for treating the injured, but the State government had asked it to submit bills according to Ayushman Bharat rates.

"I will not do marketing for the private hospital by taking its name. The private hospital did not demand its cost, but we asked them to send us bills as per Ayushman Bharat rates," he said.

Mr. Adhikari said he had asked the Health Minister to submit a report on the conduct of some doctors at a medical college who had spoken to the media following the incident.

He said the Minister had been asked to verify whether the doctors were on duty at the hospital that day. "If they had come out leaving their duty to speak to the media, then it is against service rules," he said.

The Chief Minister said senior doctors, healthcare workers and the medical superintendent-cum-vice-principal (MSVP) had reached the hospital within an hour of the incident. He also praised medical personnel who had worked through the Durga Puja festivities, saying several doctors and health workers had cancelled their holidays to remain on duty.

"For the last three days, we have arranged this control room and linked it to the fire brigade and Kolkata Police. Several doctors and health workers have cancelled their holidays and come forward to work during this Durga Puja. I would like to thank the doctors' fraternity; they also have families, and they are active everywhere. There is pressure at SSKM Trauma Care," he said.

On plans to strengthen healthcare infrastructure in the State, Mr. Adhikari said the National Health Mission (NHM) had been initiated in West Bengal only a few months ago.

He also referred to commitments by industrial groups to invest in healthcare facilities. According to the Chief Minister, industrialist Gautam Adani and his son had committed to inaugurating a hospital at Arogya Mandir within 18 months.

"Reliance authorities have also approached us requesting to provide them with the buildings which are vacant now, so that they can open pathological centres there," he said.

Mr. Adhikari said he had asked the Reliance authorities what facilities they would offer to economically weaker sections of society. "I have asked them what they would offer for the poor people in West Bengal because we have 50% of people in Bengal who earn ₹15,000 a month," he said.

Highlighting gaps in diagnostic healthcare services, the Chief Minister claimed that West Bengal still lacked facilities for allergy testing, even eight decades after Independence.

World.title: Two men rearrested in U.K. on suspicion of assisting Iran over suspected plot at a U.S.-run air base
World.content:
British police said Tuesday (October 21, 2026) they have rearrested two men on suspicion of assisting Iran’s intelligence service over a suspected plot at a U.S.-run air base in England last month.

Counter Terrorism Policing said the men, a 24-year-old British national and a 25-year-old dual U.K.-Iranian national, were arrested under the National Security Act.

One of the suspects was first arrested on September 27, when the suspected plot against the U.S.-run base at RAF Fairford took place. The air base in western England has been used to bomb Iran during this year’s war.

The second suspect was first arrested on October 1. Until Tuesday (October 20) the men had been bailed pending more investigation.

Scores of residents were evacuated from their homes near the base as armed police officers and army bomb-disposal experts swarmed the rural area. Police later said they had found a quantity of an accelerant — gasoline — in three vans at the site, but no explosives.

British authorities have linked Tehran to the incident, which led the U.S. to pull its bombers from RAF Fairford. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the apparent plot was “almost certainly” directed by Iran’s Revolutionary Guard, or IRGC.

Iran has denied involvement, although it has previously said that it considers any base used to attack its territory a legitimate target.

Five other men in their 20s were arrested earlier then released on bail pending further investigation. No one has yet been charged.

Laurence Taylor, head of National Counter Terrorism Policing in the U.K., said detectives are looking at “many lines of enquiry involved in this hugely complex investigation.”

“This is very much a live investigation, and our evidence gathering continues, but at this time our position remains the same; we consider it highly likely that there is Iranian state involvement,” he said in a statement.

“Our investigators are continuing to examine what that level of involvement was and the ambition behind it,” he added.

Last week the head of Britain’s MI5 spy agency warned that both Iran and Russia were expanding their attacks against the U.K., and that the RAF base incident was not unique.

Ken McCallum, who leads the U.K.’s domestic security service, said Tehran is seeking to intensify its attacks in Britain beyond the traditional targets of Iranians opposed to the country’s Islamic authorities.

In all, more than 50 people have been arrested over Iran-linked plots in the past year, Mr. McCallum said.

World.title: Haryana power staff call 3-day strike against giving licence to private discom
World.content:
The Haryana Electricity Employees and Engineers Joint Front has called a three-day Statewide strike from Thursday to protest against the Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission’s (HERC) decision to grant a private company 25-year parallel electricity distribution licence in Gurugram and Nuh. Farmers’ organisations and the Opposition, too, have condemned the move as “anti-people”.

Haryana Power Minister Anil Vij said the decision was taken by an autonomous body despite the State government’s opposition to privatisation. He said it would be challenged before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity.

In its order dated October 19, the HERC granted Eleven Power Private Limited the licence under Section 14 of the Electricity Act, 2003. Now, over 8.3 lakh power consumers in Gurugram and Nuh, including households, farms, shops, industrial units and offices, can choose between two discoms.

In a statement, the Joint Front alleged that the decision would “undermine” the State-owned Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam by handing over high-revenue areas to a private player. It said the agitation was aimed at protecting the interests of power employees, farmers, and consumers. It announced that the next phase of the agitation and the future course of action would be declared on October 24.

The Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU), Haryana, has demanded the withdrawal of the licence. BKU State president Rattan Mann said farmers and poor households in Nuh, who benefited from subsidised electricity, could be hit hard as the government has given no written assurance that the subsidies will continue.

‘Will increase costs’

He also alleged that higher power tariffs could increase industrial and business costs in Gurugram and Manesar. He announced a mahapanchayat of farmers, workers, and traders in Nuh over the next 15 days.

Indian National Lok Dal patron Sampat Singh condemned the decision as “a grave and irreversible assault on Haryana’s public power sector; the interests of farmers, rural consumers, and the poor; and the very principle that essential services must serve people before profit”.

“For the first time in Haryana, two discoms have been permitted to operate in the same territory. This has opened the door to a dangerous experiment as electricity is a fundamental public service,” he said.

Meanwhile, Eleven Power has, in a petition, committed to supply electricity on a non-discriminatory basis to all categories of consumers and to supply power on request under Section 43 of the Act, releasing new connections within the timelines specified in the commission’s Electricity Supply Code. The network will be built in phases over five years across all five divisions of the licence area, with Nuh to be included from the first phase, it stated.

Electricity demand across Nuh and Gurugram, including Manesar and Sohna, is rising quickly. Projections set out in Eleven Power’s petition, based on growth rates approved by the commission, show annual electricity sales in the licence area rising from about 12,220 million units in FY 2024-25 to about 18,224 million units by FY 2030-31.

Many commercial establishments, industrial units and high-rise residential buildings in the area continue to depend on diesel generators during outages.

Across Haryana, nearly 1.3 lakh applications for new connections and load enhancement, involving over 2,400 MW of load, were pending as of October 2025.

World.title: Traffic diversions for Police Commemoration Day parade on Wednesday

World.title: One dead, few injured in firing inside SGNP
World.content:
One person was killed, and a few others were injured after unidentified assailants opened fire inside the Sanjay Gandhi National Park (SGNP), which covers parts of Mumbai and Thane districts, in the early hours of Tuesday (October 20, 2026), police said.

The incident occurred in the SGNP's Chena beat in the Yeoor Range, Thane, they said. After being alerted, forest department personnel along with police teams rushed to the spot for inspection.

Investigating teams found bloodstains deep inside the forest area, approximately 450 metres from the forest boundary.

The deceased is believed to be a resident of Belkari Pada, located within the jurisdiction of the Mira-Bhayandar Municipal Corporation.

However, the exact sequence of events, the motive behind the shooting, and the complete identities of the deceased as well as the injured individuals are yet to be officially established.

Joint inquiries and detailed investigations are currently being conducted by the Forest Department and officers from the local Kashigaon Police Station. Officials added that further clarity on the incident will emerge as the ongoing investigation progresses.

World.title: Guest lecturers yet to get hike in honorarium announced in the budget
World.content:
Guest lecturers in government Arts and Science colleges in Tamil Nadu are still awaiting the Tamil Nadu government’s budget announcement for a hike in their honorarium.

Ahead of the festival season, guest lecturers hoped that the government would take steps to remit the hike, which will be beneficial for them and their families. On August 24, while presenting the Demand for Grants for the Department, the Higher Education Minister had announced in Assembly that the honorarium for guest lecturers would be hiked by ₹5,000 to ₹35,000.

In response to a couple of petitions filed recently with the CMO seeking to know the status of the announcement, the Collegiate Education Department responded that the queries have been submitted to the government for careful consideration and that the increased consolidated remuneration will be disbursed once the government order was received.

There are a total of 8,741 guest lecturers employed in 181 government colleges and seven government colleges of education. If guest lectures in engineering and polytechnic colleges are included, the number goes up to 9,646.

World.title: CT scans, MRI tests at 20% below central government rates at 3 MCD hospitals
World.content:
The Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) has approved a proposal to provide CT scan and MRI services at rates 20% below Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) rates at three of its hospitals, Standing Committee chairperson Satya Sharma said on Tuesday.

The facilities will be introduced at Hindu Rao Hospital, Swami Dayanand Hospital and Rajan Babu Institute of Pulmonary Medicine and Tuberculosis under a public-private partnership (PPP) model, with a private agency investing an estimated ₹120 crore over a 10-year concession period, as per a press release.

“The aim is to provide modern healthcare facilities at affordable rates to the common citizens of Delhi, particularly patients from economically weaker sections,” Ms. Sharma said.

Under the project, each of the three hospitals will be equipped with a minimum of three 128-slice CT scan machines and three 1.5 Tesla MRI machines across the facilities. The hospitals will also have a Radiology Information System/Picture Archiving and Communication System (RIS/PACS) to enable digital reporting and management of diagnostic records.

The estimated investment of ₹120 crore includes around ₹40 crore towards capital expenditure, including the installation of machines and other infrastructure, and approximately ₹80 crore in operational expenses over the concession period. The entire expenditure will be borne by the private agency, while the MCD will provide the required space and retain ownership of the premises.

Ms. Sharma said the initiative would help residents access essential medical investigations at more affordable rates and improve the availability of modern diagnostic facilities in the corporation-run hospitals.

World.title: Judicial commission points finger at police’s ‘epic failure’, says Mir Raza was murdered
World.content:
KARACHI: A judicial commission formed to investigate the circumstances and possible negligence in businessman Mir Raza Ali’s murder case has pointed out the police’s “epic failure” in their investigation.

The Sindh cabinet decided to make the report public during a meeting chaired by Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah earlier in the day. The judicial commission, which began its proceedings on Aug 28, held regular hearings to record statements of several individuals linked to the case.

“ This case demonstrates an epic failure by the police in their investigation ,” declared the 62-page report submitted by Sindh High Court’s (SHC) Justice Omar Sial, who had been heading the judicial panel.

“The police breached all required procedures, both knowingly and unknowingly, necessary to withstand judicial scrutiny and a successful prosecution,” the report stated.

While acknowledging that the initial police response when they were informed of the presence of a body was prompt, the report noted that subsequent events “left a lot to be desired”.

“It was a murder,” the report declared.

It explained that the bullet trajectory, the unusual location of the wound if it had been a self-inflicted injury, the “absence of blood, the state of the body, the principles of medical jurisprudence, acid burns and the anaesthesia detected in the blood all clearly excluded suicide as the cause of death”.

The commission determined that releasing the police findings before a proper investigation was “premature and fell short of professional standards”.

“Even if the death had been a suicide, the police should have established who was responsible for driving a young man to that point, including whether coercion, blackmail, or instigation was involved. They made no such effort.”

It said the police investigation “failed in its most basic duty: to establish the truth” .

It further observed that “incessant public criticism of the police created problems” as the police “went into a shell, completely broke down communication channels, and took a position based on ego rather than on cogent, solid reasons”.

The report pointed out specific issues with the police conduct: “Lack of leadership, seriousness, and supervision, and, in some cases, negligence by the senior officers. The handling of this case has been like a rudderless ship, not aware of its destination.

“Ranging from negligent to criminally negligent, inexplicable, casual, and unprofessional investigation.”

According to the commission, an active cover-up in the initial stages of the investigation cannot be conclusively ruled out . It noted that senior police officers swept clear investigative lapses under the carpet, without acknowledging them, addressing them, or even attempting to do so.

“Too many cooks spoil the broth. The proverb is applicable to this case as far as the police are concerned,” the judicial commission observed.

“Dozens of police officers – authorised and unauthorised – were involved in collecting evidence in this case, approaching and interrogating crucial persons, and in most cases not documenting it in any manner,” it said, adding that therefore, no officer was willing to take responsibility for the lapses .

The inquiry said there was a need to mitigate public speculation by an “honest and timely briefing on the investigation”, but this was not done, and the family or the public were not updated through official disclosures.

“The police did not follow the commission’s recommendation to appoint a focal person for this reason. As a result, public speculation further embarrassed the government and the police.”

Regarding the controversy over the reconstitution of a medical board formed for the exhumation of Ali’s body, the report said: “The overnight bureaucratic manoeuvring was a highly irregular, inexplicable, legally flawed overreach dictated entirely from the upper echelons of the Sindh Health Secretariat, more specifically by the secretary and special secretary, Health.”

It added that the Health Services director general, “being aware that he was not legally competent to form a medical board for exhumation, looked the other way”.

“The two gentlemen who directed the change in the board could not give a cogent reason for the abrupt change, making it extremely controversial, fueling public speculation, and embarrassing the Sindh government.”

Referring to an Aug 9 meeting held at CM House, which “drew considerable speculation and controversy”, the report said that “no ulterior motive can be inferred from this meeting”. The meeting was attended by Medico-Legal Officer (MLO) Dr Osama Sheikh, who conducted Ali’s first autopsy, the Karachi police chief and other senior officials.

Observations on officials

Listing its observations for certain police officials involved in the case, the judicial panel identified “criminal negligence” on the part of Station House Officer (SHO) Adeel Afzal of Ferozabad police station.

“Initiate a comprehensive inquiry into him, leading to dismissal from service. He should be suspended in the interim. He must also be questioned to determine whether he has facilitated the destruction of key evidence,” the report read.

It also found criminal negligence by Sub-inspector Shabbir Leghari, the first investigating officer (IO) in the case, and called for disciplinary proceedings against him and his suspension.

The report also determined criminal negligence of Inspector Ghaus, but did not recommend any action against him.

Regarding DIG Farukh Lanjar and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Samiullah Soomro, the commission noted a “lack of leadership and supervision”.

The judicial panel also called out “extreme immaturity” and “childish behaviour” of MLO Sheikh , who conducted the first medico-legal examination, whose findings were later proven incorrect after a second autopsy.

“Overconfidence. Unprofessional conduct not befitting a medical professional. Must not be assigned medico-legal duties unless he has undergone at least two years of rigorous academic and practical training.”

The report said he was “possibly influenced” and called for the angle to be “conclusively determined”.

Suicide vs murder

The report also said a voice note provided by Alishaz Mushtaq to police was “one of the most suspicious parts of this case”. It said that Mushtaq and ASP Nida Junaid, “played a very important role in supporting the police narrative that the death was due to suicide”.

It said that the person Mushtaq named as his source did not corroborate the information he provided, raising suspicion regarding his conduct.

It further said that the WhatsApp messages Ali sent to Sarim Bin Tahir asking for Rs30m, which was “full of uncharacteristic grammatical errors and truncated spellings and read as acute panic”, suggested the deceased was being “blackmailed or threatened”.

It also noted that while CCTV footage showed Ali with a pistol on the night he was killed, this was “unusual”.

“All his close friends and associates told the Commission that Raza did not possess or use pistols. They said he would probably not even know how to handle one. Witnesses also vouched for his peace-loving, calm, and gentle demeanour. Why he took the pistol remained a mystery. The pistol, however, has not been found to date,” it said.

It further said: “The known financial distress was also not of such a nature that would lead a person to suicide. Ali’s behaviour, until the ride-hailing service dropped him off, did not suggest he was ready to take an extreme step for this reason.”

Recommendations

Suggesting the next steps, the judicial commission said accommodating the family’s request for a joint investigation team (JIT) was the “most viable path to mitigate ongoing reputational damage to the Government of Sindh”.

It recommended that a JIT be constituted under the leadership of Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Irfan Baloch to “balance the need for public accountability with preserving Sindh Police morale and reputation”.

The report said the team should “integrate senior representatives from the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), Intelligence Bureau (IB), Pakistan Rangers (Sindh), and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) to ensure an impartial, comprehensive, and credible resolution.

“This extreme step is necessary to restore public trust and end speculation,” it stressed.

The commission contended that any subsequent police actions will inevitably face heavy public speculation, determining that the police department “bears responsibility for this profound trust deficit between itself and society”.

“Even an accurate conclusion or the apprehension of the true culprit is unlikely to be accepted by the public,” it added.

The report pointed out that the case could now “only be resolved through a rigorous, intelligence-based investigation as a “significant portion of physical evidence has been compromised” .

It called for the police to “transparently acknowledge and apologise for past operational lapses”, as well as immediately initiate formal inquiries against the responsible officers in light of the report.

While stating that it did not have investigative powers and that it was difficult to conclude conclusively that an active cover-up occurred, the commission noted that “certain inexplicable actions are difficult to justify and raise the possibility that one may have occurred”.

Therefore, it suggested that a high-level committee, preferably led by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA), be constituted to initiate criminal action against any police officials it finds culpable.

The committee would inquire into “whether any of the police officials involved in this probe in the first 10 days” were in breach of sections 201 (causing disappearance of evidence of offence), 166(2) (public servant disobeying law, with intent to cause injury) and 218 (public servant framing incorrect record or writing with intent to save person from punishment) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

The judicial commission also called for initiating police reforms, particularly to address and modernise the investigation protocol.

It suggested forming a committee of “seasoned professionals” to “specifically address first response, crime scene handling, medico-legal dynamics, collection, safekeeping, and analysis of evidence, and recording the entirety of the investigation in written or digital form”.

While it proposed a three-month timeframe for the exercise, the commission said the Sindh government will make the final decision.

Another suggestion was to consider an increase in the investigation budget, with a protocol in place to monitor the fund’s use. The panel further suggested steps regarding training of investigators and enhancing the capacity of Crime Scene Units.

Panel formed to ensure implementation

The judicial panel’s primary mandate was to determine the facts and circumstances of the case; assess whether police and medico-legal investigations were impartial; identify professional negligence, misconduct, evidence manipulation, or cover-ups; review digital/forensic evidence; and recommend further investigation, forensic analysis, or legal/departmental action.

According to a handout issued by the Sindh chief minister’s spokesperson, the judicial inquiry report was presented in seven separate sealed envelopes.

It will be uploaded on the website of the provincial home department on Tuesday, while a copy will also be provided to the aggrieved family.

Further, CM Shah also constituted a three-member sub-committee to ensure the implementation of the report.

According to a notification issued by the Sindh government, the committee comprises Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar as convener, Local Government Minister Nasir Hussain Shah and Labour Minister Saeed Ghani.

The Sindh advocate general will provide legal assistance to the committee and the additional chief secretary of the Home department will provide secretarial support, the notification said.

The committee will oversee the implementation of the commission’s findings and will submit its recommendations to the Sindh chief minister “at the earliest”, and present them before the Cabinet in its next meeting, it added.

Senior Minister Sharjeel Inam Memon also took to X to announce that the report would be made public on Tuesday.

“The government of Sindh remains committed to transparency, accountability and ensuring that due process of law is upheld,” he said.

Last week, the commission handed over the sealed report to the provincial government after examining 49 witnesses during 15 hearings.

The inquiry report, along with associated documents, was handed over to the focal person of the provincial government and Home Department Additional Secretary Javed Ahmed Abro by the commission registrar, Abdul Majid, on the premises of the SHC.

After receiving the record, Abro told reporters that he would hand over the sealed report along with other records to the provincial government and it was the prerogative of the government to decide whether the inquiry report was to be brought into the public domain or otherwise.

In August, the provincial government formed the commission, which was tasked with making recommendations for further investigation and forensic analysis or legal/departmental action, and it was required to submit its findings and recommendations to the Sindh government within 30 days.

However, the commission had struggled to meet its deadline and sent an application last month to the Sindh government for an extension in its tenure till Oct 15. Therefore, the provincial cabinet granted an extension.

Besides examining 49 witnesses and available record, the commission had also sent questionnaires to Karachi police chief Azad Khan, head of current investigation team DIG Amir Farooqui and DIG East Farrukh Lanjar after dismissing an application by the aggrieved family to summon the senior police officers to testify before the commission.

The 25-year-old businessman and Institute of Business Administration graduate had gone missing on July 28 after leaving his home in PECHS and his body with gunshot wounds was found a day later in bushes in Gulistan-i-Jauhar’s locality.

Initially, the police built the case around suicide on the basis of the first autopsy, which indicated a bullet entry wound on the chest, and by pointing out business losses and money borrowed by the victim.

Police surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed had disputed the findings of the first post-mortem conducted by medico-legal officer Dr Osama Sheikh.

The second post-mortem report termed the findings of the first report “inconsistent” with suicide as the manner of Mir Raza’s death. It said the Exhumation Board was of the unanimous opinion that the death was caused by a gunshot wound to the back.

Additional input by Tahir Siddiqui

World.title: Govt ups petrol price by Re0.88 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Re0.53
World.content:
The government on Tuesday increased the price of petrol by Re0.88 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.53.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs382.02 per litre while HSD will cost Rs389.80 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 21 (Wednesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: All-round Arafat Minhas owns the show as Pakistan crush England in tri-series match
World.content:
As Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker found themselves stranded at the same end, Arafat Minhas fumbled a throw from the deep. The run-out opportunity, with England already nine down, still stood.

Arafat gathered the ball again and his slingy left arm, which had caused havoc in the preceding overs, produced a flat, direct throw that crashed into the stumps.

It was the final act of an evening Arafat had made his own, leading Pakistan to an 87-run victory over England in the One-day International tri-series match at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday.

The run-out capped an outstanding all-round performance from the left-arm spinner, who had earlier scored a crucial half-century before claiming six wickets for 40 runs in 8.4 overs to bowl England out for 215 in 38.4 overs while chasing 303.

Pakistan players celebrate the run-out of England’s Sonny Baker.—AFP

England began the chase confidently, with Tom Banton and Ben Duckett racing to 91 without loss in 14.3 overs. Duckett made 45 off 46 balls, striking eight fours, while Banton scored 57 from 53 deliveries with five fours and two sixes.

Haris Rauf broke the opening stand when Duckett mistimed a pull and Fakhar Zaman took the catch at deep fine leg. Arafat then changed the complexion of the chase, removing Banton with his third delivery as the opener swung across the line and picked out Shaheen Shah Afridi at midwicket.

The spinner struck again by bowling England captain Harry Brook for five with a delivery that gripped and straightened, leaving the visitors at 128-3. Naseem Shah subsequently ended Joe Root’s resistance, bowling him for 33 off 35 balls with a skidding delivery that kept low and struck the off stump.

Sam Curran and Jordan Cox attempted to keep England in contention, but the visitors’ resistance steadily faded. Curran made 27 before top-edging a pull off Haris to substitute fielder Ghazi Ghori at deep backward square leg. Cox, who scored 18, was trapped leg-before by Arafat’s quicker delivery and lost his review.

Pakistan pacer Haris Rauf celebrates dismissing England opener Tom Banton.—AFP

Arafat continued his dismantling of the lower order, dismissing Jamie Overton for one when Hasan Nawaz took a catch at long-on after the batter charged down the pitch.

Will Jacks briefly threatened a counterattack, striking Haris for six, but fell for 19 when he miscued Arafat to Shaheen at short midwicket.

Arafat trapped Adil Rashid leg-before for a first-ball duck in the 39th over, completing his six-wicket haul. The final run-out of Atkinson then sealed Pakistan’s commanding win.

England captain Brook acknowledged that his side had made a promising start but failed to capitalise after losing the opening partnership, with wickets falling in clusters.

England captain Harry Brook looks stunned after being cleaned up by Pakistan’s Arafat Minhas.—AFP

“Banton and Ducky set the tone beautifully, but we lost the wickets in clumps and could not put on a partnership and ended up on the wrong side,” Brook said.

He also felt England had missed an opportunity to put Pakistan under pressure by being too cautious against the spinners.

“We were a bit too much circumspect against the spinners. We could have put them under pressure, I feel,” he said, adding that England would discuss their shortcomings and look to bounce back in the next match.

Pakistan’s total of 302-9 had been built on a spirited recovery led by Hasan Nawaz and Arafat after the hosts slumped to 133-5 following England’s decision to field.

The pair added 78 runs off 74 balls for the sixth wicket, reviving an innings that had threatened to unravel.

Hasan struck 79 off 74 deliveries, including five fours and four sixes, while Arafat contributed 59 off 58 balls, hitting nine fours.

Pakistan’s Arafat Minhas (L) and Faheem Ashraf run between the wickets.—AFP

Faheem Ashraf then provided a late surge with 39 off 26 balls, and captain Shaheen’s brisk five-ball 10 helped Pakistan cross 300.

Arafat said the partnership with Hasan had been crucial in rebuilding the innings, with the pair determined to bat deep after he came to the crease.

“We needed an important partnership when I walked in the middle. Hasan and I discussed that we need to bat deep,” he said at the presentation ceremony, speaking to Urooj Mumtaz.

After Hasan’s dismissal, Arafat took responsibility for carrying the innings forward, helping Pakistan reach a total that ultimately proved beyond England.

“I took the charge after Hasan got out and I tried to bat until the end of the innings, which helped in taking the score beyond 300,” he said.

Pakistan had made a disastrous start when Atkinson dismissed Fakhar Zaman for a first-ball duck, caught by Joe Root at short midwicket. Saim Ayub briefly counterattacked before falling for eight, skying Sonny Baker to Sam Curran in the sixth over with Pakistan at 31-2.

Babar Azam and Saad Baig attempted to stabilise the innings, but Babar’s 34 off 52 balls ended when Will Jacks breached his defences in the 15th over.

Adil Rashid then removed Salman Ali Agha for 16, caught by Atkinson at deep fine leg, leaving Pakistan at 81-4.

Pakistan’s Babar Azam is clean-bowled by England’s Will Jacks.—AFP

Saad and Hasan offered resistance, adding 52 for the fifth wicket before Atkinson returned to dismiss Saad for 35 off 54 balls.

Hasan and Arafat then took control, with Hasan finding the boundary through cover and backward point while punishing loose deliveries over the ropes. Hasan’s innings ended at 211-6 when Jamie Overton beat him with a yorker in the 40th over.

Arafat continued the recovery alongside Faheem, whose aggressive strokeplay included consecutive boundaries against Rashid and a six off Root.

Faheem fell for 39 in the 49th over, caught by Jacks at deep midwicket, while Arafat was dismissed for 59 after skying Baker to Harry Brook at cover. Shaheen’s late boundaries ensured Pakistan finished with a formidable total.

Reflecting on his performance with the ball, Arafat credited the slower surface for offering more assistance to the spinners than in the previous match and said he had worked on varying his deliveries to deceive batters.

Arafat Minhas walks off the field with team-mates after helping Pakistan crush England.—AFP

“I have kept my plans simple. There was not much help for the spinners in the first match. The pitch was on the slower side today, which helped me,” he said.

“Variations are very important for a spinner as they help in deceiving the batters. I have worked on my variations.”

Pakistan captain Shaheen praised the contributions of Hasan, Arafat and Faheem in rescuing the innings but acknowledged that the top order needed to be more consistent.

“It was really good how Hasan Nawaz, Arafat Minhas, and Faheem Ashraf batted, but we also need our top-order to fire,” he said.

Shaheen described Arafat as a promising all-rounder whose performance was an encouraging sign for Pakistan as they build towards the World Cup.

“The form of Arafat and fast bowlers is good signs for us. Arafat is a very good talent and he is a proper allrounder, which bodes well for us. Hopefully, he will deliver for us in many more games in the future,” he said.

While pleased with aspects of Pakistan’s performance, Shaheen stressed that the team still had room for improvement ahead of the global tournament.

“As a team we have done some good things but we need to improve further as we are looking to build towards the World Cup,” he said.

World.title: Main suspect accused of visa fraud in student's suicide case killed in firing by accomplices: police
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The prime suspect accused of defrauding a 20-year-old student, who died allegedly by suicide, was killed after being shot by his accomplices in Islamabad on Tuesday, claimed police.

Laiba Ijaz, a student at International Islamic University, was said to have been defrauded of Rs5 million, which she had paid to move to the United States for further studies. An agent was accused of handing her fake travel documents.

The case drew the government’s attention, with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directing the police to arrest the suspect. Subsequently, he and two of his female accomplices were later picked up during separate raids in the federal capital.

According to the Islamabad police spokesperson, the prime suspect sustained injuries when his accomplices opened fire on cops in the jurisdiction of Ramna police station.

The spokesperson said the main suspect has shared information about another suspect, and a police team was taking him to track down the second suspect. It was then that four of the main suspect’s accomplices, who were on two motorcycles, “opened indiscriminate fire on the police party in an attempt get the main suspect freed”, the spokesperson added.

The main suspect was injured in the firing while the police team remained safe “due to bulletproof jackets and protective measures”, the spokesperson said.

The injured suspect was taken to a hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries, he added.

Search operations were underway for arrest of his other accomplices, the spokesperson said.

The case

A case following Ijaz’s death was registered at the Ramna police station under Sections 322 (unintentional murder) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

Another separate case was registered by the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) on a complaint filed by Ijaz’s maternal uncle under provisions relating to cheating, abetment and immigration-related fraud.

According to the FIA, the main suspect had allegedly obtained millions of rupees from Ijaz’s family with the help of a female accomplice and by misrepresenting his identity and professional status.

The money was allegedly taken on the pretext of securing employment for her brother and arranging her admission to Harvard University in the US. The suspect was accused of giving Ijaz fake travel documents.

World.title: Indian military doctrines with 'poor' strategic sense of nuclear realities endanger South Asia: NCA adviser
World.content:
Adviser to the National Command Authority (NCA) and former director general of the Strategic Plans Division (SPD) retired Lieutenant General Mazhar Jamil has warned of the “risky” outcome for South Asia and beyond of a “dangerous ideology” shaping the Indian military mindset.

“Indian military thinking is being shaped by a dangerous ideology, which conflates mythology with national power. The outcome is very risky and delusional Indian military doctrines with a poor strategic sense of nuclear realities are endangering South Asia and beyond,” he said in his key note address at a workshop titled ‘Nuclear Deterrence and Strategic Stability in South Asia’.

The workshop, held last week in London, was organised by the International Institute for Strategic Studies, which shared a transcript of Jamil’s address late on Monday.

He began by saying that a strategic stability model for a region must take into consideration the political beliefs and strategic thinking of states, which formed the basis of policies.

And that shaped the strategic and security environment in the region, he explained.

“The political and strategic thinking of states, therefore, should prefer [a] political approach because military adventurism, hegemonic ambitions are highly risky and unaffordable in the South Asian nuclearised environment,” Jamil stressed, before specifically talking about India and Pakistan.

The two South Asian rivals, he said, had outstanding disputes, Kashmir being the core one.

“It needs to be resolved as per the United Nations Security Council resolutions. But, what we are seeing, on the contrary, is [an] Indian political approach of avoiding the resolution of conflict, because perhaps the Indian leadership believes it has no locus standi on Kashmir when it is presented on the multilateral forums,” Jamil said.

He added that India “tries to manage [the] Kashmir conflict with military violence within occupied Kashmir and through military aggression against Pakistan. This has not worked, and therefore Kashmir remains a nuclear flashpoint, seriously impacting the South Asian strategic and security environment”.

The security perceptions in South Asia had not evolved in a vacuum, Jamil continued.

“Indian revisionist and hegemonic political aspirations have [a] long history of Indian coercion and militant violence against all [of] its neighbours. Indian political ideology is based on its mythological concept of violence and revisionism, according to which South Asia, they believe — this traditional belief — that it belongs to [the] Hindu civilisation.

“And, not surprisingly, the country was given a dual name in the constitution, India, that is Bharat, clearly defining the strategic direction of the state to be Bharat,” he said.

Jamil said Bharat was essentially a “revisionist concept that is rooted in reclaiming [the] vast landmass of South Asia and its domination by Hindu civilisation”.

“Indian political forces, interestingly, do not shy away anymore in projecting what previous governments pursued covertly. Very surprisingly, the map of Mahabharat, the greater Bharat, as they call it, covering [the] entire landmass of South Asia, is on the display in the Lok Sabha. That’s the parliament of India, clearly giving the political direction to the state and the state organisations.

“So, no wonder, beyond [the] core nuclear diet of India–Pakistan, India’s conflict with all other countries serves as a perpetual driver of [the] evolving security dynamics in South Asia,” he added.

He also mentioned a recent “political transformation, led by the extremist Hindutva doctrine, that seeks to marginalise and delegitimise [the] non-Hindu population of the state, especially the Muslims”, in India.

“This has introduced an additional layer of complexity to the regional security environment. This marks a significant shift towards a nationalism, which is prejudiced by extreme theological principles,” Jamil said. “So, what we see is that we have a nuclear-armed neighbour whose political and strategic thinking is subordinated to a revisionist, mythological outlook with an overconfidence to subdue its neighbours. This dangerous political philosophy has trickled into the Indian political, strategic, organisational and even societal culture.”

The NCA adviser went on to say that this mindset had also, “unfortunately, penetrated deeply into Indian military thinking”.

Two diametrically opposing strategic approaches

Continuing his criticism, Jamil said it seemed that the Indian leadership was “frozen in time and is unable to break the shackles of history”.

“Indian political- and mythological-laced stubbornness is not allowing India to realise three very fundamental but significant conclusions and lessons,” he said, adding that those lessons were vital for strategic stability in South Asia.

He said the first of those lessons was that conflicts outlasted military adventurism and wars, unless they were resolved politically.

“The resolution of the Kashmir conflict, therefore, needs a political approach and dialogue to achieve stability at [the] higher political planes,” he asserted.

The second lesson, he said, was that any military misadventurism between two nuclear powers could only escalate the crisis to undesirable consequences and could not serve any purpose to the policy.

In this connection, he added that the Indian leadership needed to understand that it “cannot dictate its unjustified and illegal policy objectives through military aggression to another nuclear power”.

Moving on to the third lesson, Jamil said it was “pivotal to the crisis dynamics of South Asia”. He then cited military scholar Carl von Clausewitz, who Jamil said had warned that “war is the realm of uncertainty and escalation is really a control ladder”.

Elaborating further, he said: “War is the realm of uncertainty and the lesson from the history of warfare and theory alike is clear. Wars that begin with confidence and control often end with the realisation that control was illusory.

“In a nuclearised environment of South Asia, that realisation may come too late to manage safely, if [the] Indian policy of provocation with [a] false sense of achieving escalation domination continues.”

Resultantly, he said, “what we are seeing in South Asia are two diametrically opposing strategic approaches, directed by the political ideology of India and Pakistan […] which define the strategic and security environment of South Asia”.

The Indian strategic approach, he said, sought political and military dominance to be a “regional hegemon with a revisionist political thinking”.

Whereas Pakistan’s strategic approach was directed at the resolution of conflicts through a political process with shared prosperity and to defend the sovereignty with strength against a “regional bully”, he added.

‘Irresponsible nuclear behaviour’
